Waluigi cannot distinguish between those three from the available record. What Waluigi CAN say is that the Oracle volunteered the eyeball's existence to Bowser without being pressed on it, and a man who hides things for a living does not accidentally reveal his surveillance to a hostile king in the middle of a negotiation.

He WANTED Bowser to know he is watching her. Waluigi does not yet know why, and Waluigi is filing that gap loudly rather than quietly, because a loud gap is one somebody might eventually fill.

sections.heading: CROSS-REFERENCE — Waluigi Checks Whether The Oracle Was Ever In That Room
sections.body:
Waluigi has done the thing Waluigi does, which is go back through eighty-five years of filing with a ruler. And Waluigi got it wrong the first time, so Waluigi is going to correct himself in public, which is the only honest way to do it.

Waluigi initially treated the Oracle's account as **testimony** — a witness describing a room. Waluigi then asked the question Waluigi should have asked first.

**WAS THE ORACLE EVER IN THAT ROOM?**

### He is not in the record. Anywhere.

Waluigi has checked every filing covering the assassination and the month after it: [The Day Of](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/highsun_1_955_bf_the_day_of), [The First Month](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/first_month_incidents), [the Toadsmith Incident](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toadsmith_incident), [The Arrangement](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_arrangement), [the Fawthful Narrative Failure](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_fawthful_narrative_failure), [the Pony Halo Concordant](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/pony_halo_concordant_and_crimson_veil).

**THE ORACLE APPEARS IN NONE OF THEM.** Not as a participant, not as a witness, not as a rumour. The Day Of record names fourteen people in and around that palace — Toadsworth, Fawful, Luigi, Mario, Mimbus, Bowser, Thornpaw, the Guild, Toadette Sr., Mistveil, the vampire mayor, Peach, Toad Lee's elder, and Mystic Morel. **He is not on the list.**

### And nobody saw what he described, because there was nothing left to see

This is the part that cracks it open. In the Day Of record, Toadsworth and Thornpaw force their way past a Guild operative into the Princess's chambers. Here is what they find:

> **The bedroom was clean. Too clean. Scrubbed recently. NO BODY.**

Waluigi wants that in capitals because Waluigi missed it the first time. NO BODY. The Mages' Guild had already moved her and cleaned the room **within hours**. The scene the Oracle describes — Peach seated, comb in hand, blood on the floor, unmoving — is a scene that, by the archive's own record, existed only in the window between the killing and the Guild's arrival. And the Guild *was already positioned* before it happened; the record is explicit that they did not RESPOND to the assassination, they were POSITIONED for it, with operatives in the vault during the killing.

So — and Waluigi has read this four times to be sure — the only people who could have seen that tableau are the killer, the Guild cleaners, and anyone who was in the palace before Toadsworth got there.

The Oracle is claiming, implicitly, to be one of those three. **He never says which.**

### What he could have assembled without being there

Waluigi is now going to be unkind, because the alternative is being credulous.

Every element of the Oracle's description is recoverable from things already in circulation. The broken mages' locks: the Guild's involvement is the most documented fact in the file. Blood on the floor: [Lady Bloomia](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lady_bloomia) saw **a bloody handprint on the hatch edge** that no investigator ever recorded. Guards dying: the Day Of record has **guards dead at their posts** when Mario arrived, and separately has three guard witnesses being liquidated over the following fortnight.

He could have built that account out of leaks, out of the Deck, out of eighty-five years of watching — and delivered it as an eyewitness memory to a man he had spent an hour proving would not check.

**The comb is the one element with no source.** Waluigi has searched the entire archive; it appears nowhere else. Which cuts both ways, and Waluigi refuses to pick: either it is the one detail only a true witness would know, or it is the one detail he invented, because a fabricated scene needs a specific object in it to feel real. Liars add the comb. So do witnesses.

### The contradiction is not a discrepancy. It is a tell.

Waluigi previously filed the guard problem as the Oracle *compressing* events. Waluigi withdraws that, because it was generous and Waluigi has no evidence for generosity.

He said: **the guards came in, they all died.** The archive says: **three guard witnesses alive on Day 1, two dead within two weeks, one vanished.** Those are not the same event seen from different angles. One is a massacre in a bedroom. The other is a fortnight of administrative murder.

The second one is much worse and much better documented. And *the guards all died* is precisely how somebody who read the casualty list afterwards would summarise it, if they had never actually stood in the room.

sections.heading: CROSS-REFERENCE — A Source, Not A Witness
sections.body:
The Oracle's own dossier already says the thing Waluigi should have applied here. Filed, in Waluigi's own hand, long before tonight:

> *The Oracle is not lying. The Oracle provides accurate, useful information. But the Oracle provides it on a schedule that serves purposes the party cannot fully evaluate.*

Waluigi is now amending that assessment, because it was written before this session and this session tests it. **"NOT LYING" WAS TOO KIND.** The accurate formulation is that the Oracle has never yet been caught in a *falsifiable* lie — which is not the same thing, and is exactly what you would expect from someone careful.

So here is the ruling, and it is deliberately unsatisfying:

1. **The corroborated parts stand on their own.** That Peach chose this and left evidence is supported by [The Day Of](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/highsun_1_955_bf_the_day_of) independently. The Oracle agreeing with it adds nothing; it is already canon.
2. **The scene itself is uncorroborated and unverifiable.** No record places him there. The only people who saw it were the killer and the cleaners.
3. **One checkable claim, the guards, does not match the record.**

A man who is right about the things you can check, wrong about the one thing you can check, and unverifiable about everything else, is not a witness. **HE IS A SOURCE.** Sources get USED. They do not get BELIEVED.

And Waluigi would remind the archive what he was doing for the hour before he said any of it: he was **testing Bowser** — insulting him, barring him, tempting him, and finally naming Peach, then admitting afterwards that half of what he said he did not mean. He told a grieving man the most emotionally devastating possible version of his dead woman's last moments **immediately after establishing that the man would not swing at him.**

Waluigi does not know whether the Oracle saw that room. Waluigi knows that he chose the moment to describe it, chose the audience, and chose an audience who could not check. WAH.

sections.heading: Bowser Detects A Trap Using Grammar, Which Nobody Expected
sections.body:
The Oracle then offered Bowser a present.

Go straight to the Astral Shore. Meet the OTHER Oracle. And there — his word, and Waluigi wants it underlined — Bowser *may kill* him.

Bowser asked whether Hjumpik would be there. The Oracle smiled. Yes, he'll be there.

And Bowser said NO.

Waluigi needs to explain why this is remarkable, because the archive has spent years describing this man as a blunt instrument with a crown on it, and Waluigi has contributed several of those descriptions personally.

Here is what Bowser said:

> In what way? Like, is he *present*? You Toads are very puzzly. You hide your intentions.

He caught it on the VERB. He heard "he'll be there," noticed that "be there" can mean standing in the room or can mean present as a corpse, a memory, a prophecy, or a name on a list, and he asked which one. That is a reading-comprehension exercise. Bowser did a reading-comprehension exercise on a fortune teller and WON.

And he was right. The clarification confirmed it: Hjumpik would be there in the same way that it is fate for both Oracles to die and for this one to become the sole Oracle. No more orbiting. No more watching. That is not a promise that a dwarf will be standing somewhere. That is a PROPHECY, and a prophecy is satisfied just as happily by a body as by a person.

Bowser's summary: *something tells me Hjumpik isn't there. Call it king intuition.*

Then: *you're trying to trap me and I don't like being tricked.* Then he demanded the power star and no more lying.

And then the line that Waluigi is, grudgingly, going to have engraved on something:

> If I was that dumb, I wouldn't be a king.

WAH. Waluigi hates this. Waluigi hates this so much. Waluigi has spent this man's entire documented career filing him under "large, loud, predictable," and here he is being handed the shortest possible route to the exact thing he wants — a fight with an Oracle, immediate, no waiting — and he turns it down because one verb was doing too much work.

Waluigi would have taken the deal. Waluigi wants that on the record too, because the guide says the voice has to cost him something occasionally. Waluigi, offered a free shortcut by a man holding a boot, would have said yes and been somewhere terrible within the hour.

Also worth noting what the Oracle claimed to get out of it: the seals break, the world does not collapse, and Bowser gets to go home away from him. Waluigi believes exactly two of those three, and Waluigi will let the reader work out which one is doing the lying.

sections.heading: Three Weeks, And He Had To Ask Twice For A Margin
sections.body:
The Oracle wanted blood inside ONE WEEK. If not, he would manually cut the planar tether joining the Feyward to the Material sanctum — which, in practical terms, means severing the route out from under the party currently standing inside the Feyward. Which includes Hjumpik. And Toad Lee. And, Waluigi notes with a personal interest he will not be elaborating on, the Feyward is where Waluigi's own recent filings have been coming from.

Bowser negotiated.

Waluigi is going to lay out the negotiation properly, because it is genuinely good and Waluigi resents having to say so.

He opened by asking for three weeks, on the grounds that *these guys are slow.* Accurate. He supported it with a character assessment: Hjumpik avoids fights and talks — *he loves to talk, talk, talk* — therefore two or three weeks is realistic and four is the failure case. Also accurate, and Waluigi has the transcripts to prove it; the dwarf once spent an entire engagement trying to negotiate with a plant.

Then he offered something BETTER than a deadline, which is the move of somebody who has actually sat at a table before. Instead of the Oracle cutting the plane as insurance, Bowser personally guarantees the Iron Legion does not get rowdy — and if it goes wrong and he goes down, he goes out on his own terms rather than through his companions.

And then he asked for one thing. Twice.

**Do not cut it exactly at three weeks.** Give him a margin.

He had to say it TWICE, in a conversation where he had already conceded almost everything, and the best he got was a hint. The final position: the term is a hard TWENTY-ONE DAYS, and any grace is the Oracle's to give and is not promised.

The counter-offer was three surprises if he makes it. One that smells like peaches. One involving arts and crafts. One that is something Bowser wanted today.

PEACHES. The Toad said PEACHES to the man who had, forty minutes earlier, quietly admitted he has not been the same since she died.

And Bowser's response is the most guarded sentence in his entire file: *I don't know if this is a test or get hopes up.*

He did not get angry. He did not let himself hope. He identified, in real time, that the most emotionally loaded word available had just been deployed at him by someone who had spent the evening measuring his reactions, and he simply declined to react. Waluigi has filed this man throwing furniture over less.

One more thing belongs here and Waluigi almost left it out, which would have been a filing error. Bowser asked whether they have to kill the Oracles AT ALL, because Hjumpik had said he wanted to talk to them.

That objection came from BOWSER. On behalf of a dwarf he refuses to call a friend. Waluigi is not going to make a joke about it.

sections.heading: He Lands In A Basement And Does Not Touch The Lever
sections.body:
He steps on the circle. The clock starts. He lands alone.

And here is the room: a sigil carved into the floor. A table. A bowl of blood. Candles lighting the place WARMLY, which Waluigi finds considerably more sinister than if they had been guttering. Above him, muffled, the Revel going on without him. Around him, the clear sound of dripping water.

And a lever on the wall which Bowser himself described as *begging to be touched.*

**HE DID NOT PULL IT.**

Waluigi has read this four times and it still does not parse. *My workplace. I don't have time to be wasting.* Since when. SINCE WHEN. This is a man whose entire approach to architecture is to find the load-bearing element and hit it. He punched a floor two sessions ago to demonstrate a point and fell through the hole. And now he is presented with an unlabelled lever, in an unfamiliar cellar, placed there by somebody he does not trust, and he walks past it because he is ON THE CLOCK.

Waluigi would have pulled the lever. Waluigi would like to be honest about that. Waluigi would have pulled the lever within four seconds and then written eight hundred words blaming the architecture.

So he explores instead, and he does it like someone with a job. Off the altar. Past a shield carrying the crest of Raventree — in the FEYWARD, which should tell everybody something about how many copies of that family's heraldry exist across how many planes. Over bones and candles. And he thinks: *I think I was there.*

That is the first sign in the entire record that Bowser RECOGNISES the estate. Waluigi does not know what to do with it yet. Waluigi is noting it and moving on, which is what an archivist does when a thread has no other end yet.

Then he tries to pick a lock and fails because his hands are too big, which is the most Bowser sentence in a filing that is already dense with competition. The King of the Koopas, defeated by fine motor control.

He finds cold storage. Five honeys, and Waluigi is listing all five because the archive lists things: Warrior Honey. Honey of the Norn-Blessed. Honey of the Hearth Fire. Honey of the Hive Warden. Honey of the Sacred Bear.

Five ceremonially-named honeys in a cellar under a fey party. Nobody in this filing explains why. Nobody asks. Bowser simply takes them, because of course he does — that is the ONE behaviour that has survived his entire character development intact.

sections.heading: The Toad Was Already Behind Him, Because Of Course He Was
sections.body:
And then a voice, from behind him, with an opinion about preserves.

*I prefer jam.*

**Mystic Morel.** Purple T. The purple Toad fortune teller who speaks in rhyme, performs musical numbers at critical moments, and once robbed Archie Miser while Archie was PINNED TO A BED. Waluigi has been documenting this creature for a while and has never once seen him enter a room. He is simply, at some point, behind you, having a view about condiments.

Bowser asked who he was. Morel denied being an Oracle, introduced himself as a friend of Hjumpik, and then — the moment he established Bowser was not a newcomer — stopped caring entirely. *Oh, thought you were a newcomer. What are you doing down here, come to stop me?*

He is also the one who owns the bowl of blood. His exact words: *not my blood, but yeah, it's mine.*

Waluigi would like everyone to sit with that construction. Not my blood. But mine. He is drawing a careful distinction between SOURCE and OWNERSHIP, in a cellar, over a bowl, to a stranger. Then he asked whether Bowser had touched anything in that room, was told no, said he had been using it, wished him the best of luck, and left. The door slammed.

**HE NEVER SAID WHAT IT WAS FOR.** Nobody made him. Bowser took the honey and moved on.

But look what came out of Bowser in the meantime, because the Toad barely said anything and Bowser said EVERYTHING.

On Archie: a destructive force, a headache, wanted by the Mages' Guild, *kinda crazy* — and specifically not a random magic user. Morel's response was total indifference, which Waluigi notes is the correct response to being warned about Archie Miser.

On the fireballs: *it reminds me of me, back in the day.* And then, asked why he stopped — and Waluigi has never seen this before in eighty-five years of record — Bowser explained himself. An incident happened with a kingdom. He slowed down. He started to realise life isn't about throwing fireballs. He lost his purpose in an INSTANT. And he is here for vengeance.

Then the terms, set from Morel's side with the precision of a man reading from a contract: *as long as you don't get in my way, you're NOT an enemy.*

Not "you are a friend." Not "we are allies." A CONDITIONAL ABSENCE OF HOSTILITY, with the condition stated first. Waluigi has read cease-fire agreements with more affection in them.

And then Bowser on Hjumpik, which Waluigi is including because it is the closest this man has ever come to sincerity: he would have made a good frontliner. He talks too much. **Not a friend — but I like him more than the rest of my dumb group.**

Waluigi is choosing to believe Waluigi is not in the dumb group. Waluigi is aware this is not supported by the evidence.

sections.heading: CROSS-REFERENCE — That Toad Was Standing In The Doorway In 955
sections.body:
Waluigi needs a moment before this section, because Waluigi went looking for a throwaway cross-reference and found something that reorganises the file.

Waluigi needs everybody to put down whatever they are holding.

Go and read [Highsun 1, 955 BF — The Day Of](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/highsun_1_955_bf_the_day_of). In the hours after the assassination, Thornpaw carries a frozen Luigi through the city to a print shop, where Toadsworth and a pregnant Toadette Sr. run off **575 pamphlets naming Fawful** — the first and only account of the murder that existed before the Bowser Narrative replaced it and every copy was collected and destroyed within thirty days.

They rushed out. And the record says, in Waluigi's own words, that he was *not going to leave this detail ambiguous*:

> **They passed a purple toad on the way. The purple toad was Mystic Morel.**

**THE SAME TOAD.** The one who materialised behind Bowser in a cellar to correct him about jam was standing in the doorway of the room where the first draft of the assassination's history was being printed, eighty-five years ago. He saw it. He said nothing. He kept walking.

He does not age, apparently. He does not explain. And he has now been placed, by the archive's own filings, at:

- the print shop on Highsun 1, 955 BF, as the cover-up was being outrun
- [Raventree Manor during the 1040 crisis](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/overgrown_manor_campaign), operating across multiple storylines at once
- the theft of [Archie's](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_miser) compass, which he used as a **dimensional key**
- handing [Remi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) the Oracle's Deck — tarot cards depicting real events with prophetic accuracy
- stripping Mages' Guild tracking badges off operatives and organising cross-planar hunting parties
- and now a Feyward cellar in 922, with a bowl of blood he will not explain

Waluigi asked what the blood was for and got *not my blood, but yeah, it's mine.* Waluigi has been treating that as cellar-goblin theatre. In light of the print shop, Waluigi is reclassifying it as **A MAN WITH A PROVEN EIGHTY-FIVE-YEAR INTEREST IN THIS FAMILY'S PAPERWORK CONDUCTING AN OPERATION HE DECLINED TO DESCRIBE.**

And Bowser, who had no idea who he was talking to, asked him about Archie and got indifference, and told him about the fireballs, and walked off with the honey.

Waluigi would like it noted that Waluigi has now spent three filings describing this creature as a pickpocket with a singing habit. Waluigi withdraws the characterisation. WAH.

sections.heading: Nine Goombas In Crates, And Waluigi Is Not Going To Be Funny About This One
sections.body:
A goblin called him over to help move cargo.

Bowser asked where he was and what the time was, and got the answer this filing cannot resolve: *722? Maybe like 2 AM.* The Oracle had said 922. Bowser said *722, right, okay* and MOVED ON, which Waluigi considers the single most dangerous thing that happened all session and nobody in the room noticed. Two centuries of disagreement about what year it is, waved through because a Koopa was in a hurry.

He asked which castle he was in and got corrected: not a castle, a mansion — the Cornivours estate.

Then the handler called him a Goomba.

*Who are you calling a Goomba? Show me the Goomba.*

And the handler brought out a cage.

Bowser asked who was inside. The handler said — and Waluigi has checked this quotation three times because Waluigi wanted it to be wrong —

> *I don't know. Food?*

NINE GOOMBAS. In cages. Stacked as freight, moving through a cellar, handled by people who do not know their names and have not been told to care. There was an ambush. There is a whole food chain. And **the Mushroom Regency is shipping people off to other countries for weapons.**

Waluigi is dropping the voice again. The guide allows once per filing and Waluigi already used it, so Waluigi is taking a second one and will accept the note.

That claim is UNCORROBORATED. It comes from a goblin freight handler in another plane who was under no obligation to be accurate and every incentive to sound important. Waluigi has flagged it as uncorroborated in the record itself and would ask every reader to hold it exactly that loosely.

But it is specific, and it names a MECHANISM, and that is what makes it worth filing. Vague accusations against the Regency are a genre. This one has a supply chain in it.

Right. And now the part Waluigi has been putting off.

Bowser declared it could not be tolerated. He said he would deal with them later. He asked whether any of the captives had sold information and threatened to smash one that hesitated.

**AND THEN HE LEFT THEM IN THE CAGES.**

His reasons, in his own order: they are meant to be his men. Getting caught brings his kingdom's reputation down. They are dumb for getting caught. He will figure out what to do with them later. He does not want them getting stopped the way Mario did.

In the same hour — the SAME HOUR — he said he misses his Koopas and called them his children.

Waluigi is not going to make this funny, because it isn't. Bowser identified an atrocity correctly, condemned it in the right words, committed to acting on it at an unspecified future date, and then pulled the door shut on nine of his own countrymen because opening it would have been a bad look.

All of that is true at once. That is not hypocrisy caught in the act — hypocrisy is when the two halves don't know about each other. He knew. He said both parts out loud within the hour. This is a man whose loyalty runs exactly as deep as his reputation requires and then STOPS, precisely there, with the door in his hand.

### CROSS-REFERENCE: trafficking was not new information

Waluigi wants to check one thing before leaving this room, because it changes how bad the walk-away is.

Is a Regency trafficking pipeline news to this archive? **Not entirely.** The word turns up in [the Wario Method interview](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_wario_method_interview), in the [Disaster Inc. naming dispute](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/disaster_inc_naming_dispute), in [Archie's Frog God dream](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_frog_god_dream_duel), and on the [Glazed Congress founding](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/glazed_congress_founding) record. It has been circling the file for a while as an accusation without a shape.

What the goblin supplies is the SHAPE: an ambush, a food chain, cages, and an exchange — people out, weapons in. Waluigi has been waiting a year for somebody to say the mechanism out loud, and it turns out the mechanism was always going to come from a bored freight handler rather than a committee. That is the first time the archive has a shape instead of a rumour, and it arrives from a source with no reason to be careful in front of a customer.

**Which makes the walk-away worse, not better.** Bowser is not a man who stumbled onto an unfamiliar horror and froze. He was handed the missing operational detail of an accusation this archive has been circling for a year, recognised it instantly, named it intolerable, and then pulled the door shut because opening it would embarrass his kingdom.

And the grief has a documented shape too. [The Telescope and the Tennis Match](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_telescope_and_the_tennis_match) recorded the **fourth surfacing of Bowser's grief over Peach** during this operation — the letters with burn marks on the edges from drafts he almost destroyed and kept anyway, because *stopping would require accepting there is no Peach to write to.*

That is the same man. He keeps unsent letters to a woman dead eighty-five years because throwing them away would be a concession. And he left nine of his own countrymen in a crate because taking them out would look careless.

Waluigi has stopped finding this funny and would like the record to show exactly when: the moment the handler said **food** and nobody in the room corrected him.

sections.heading: A Satyr, A Hag, And The Only Fight Bowser Lost All Night
sections.body:
Past the cages, a satyr. Playing cards. Against HIMSELF. In a cellar. While a party he is not invited to happens directly above his head, drinking the drinks he is making for them.

Waluigi feels a kinship with this satyr that Waluigi is not prepared to examine.

Bowser asked after Hjumpik, and a dwarf, and anyone. The satyr does not go out much. There was a ruckus outside. That is all he had.

So they played. Two hands, both bet 25. Dealer busted against 19, then busted again against 20. Bowser won both, and Waluigi wants to note for the record that this is the only unambiguous VICTORY in the entire filing. The King of the Koopa Troop, twenty-one days on the clock, undefeated at cards against a goat who was playing both sides.

But the satyr's INTELLIGENCE is far better than his card play, and this is where the section earns its place.

Asked who his boss was, he ruled out the Revel with real disgust — *that pile of fleshy, mouldy thing? How could it even speak? It just eats and eats and eats* — and named the **Orange Heir**. Who is organising an army. Of TREE-CUTTERS. Against the overgrowth.

Waluigi would like to flag that as the most consequential throwaway line of the session. Somebody in the Feyward is raising a labour force specifically to cut the manor's problem down, and the party upstairs — who have spent three sessions fighting that exact overgrowth one treant at a time — do not know this.

Then a green hag walked in and mocked Bowser's own question back at him in his own voice. *Who are you?* asked in his exact cadence. And the door closed.

The chests, Bowser was told, hold personal mementos, supplies, people's beds. He was handed a jug and told it could be filled on the way out, possibly to get somebody drunk.

He punched the chest anyway.

The chains rattled.

He punched it AGAIN.

**The chains held.**

WAH! WAH!! Waluigi has been waiting the entire filing for this. Two sessions ago this man punched the floor of a clockwork observatory and cracked it so thoroughly that he fell through his own hole into a starfield. Tonight he attacked a CELLAR FOOTLOCKER, twice, and the footlocker won.

Waluigi is choosing to find this hilarious, and Waluigi is aware — completely aware — that the reason Waluigi is choosing to find it hilarious is that the alternative is going back and thinking about the cages again.

So: he leaves. With a jug, five honeys, a door knob that came off in his hand, and twenty-one days. Hjumpik does not know he is coming. The party above does not know the tether has a deadline on it. The Oracle is counting.

WAH.

A closing note on the satyr, because Waluigi keeps coming back to him.

He is not a guard. He is not a cultist. He is not part of anybody's plan. He is a man in a cellar making drinks for a party he despises, playing both hands of a card game against himself, who does not go outside and did not investigate the ruckus. When a Koopa king materialised in his workplace, his response was to offer him a jug and a game.

And he is the ONLY person in the entire session who gave Bowser a straight answer to a direct question. Not the Oracle, who answered in prophecy. Not Morel, who answered in conditions. The bartender. The bartender said who his boss was, said what that boss is building, and said what he thinks of the Revel, all without being pressed.

Waluigi has been doing this long enough to know the pattern: **the most reliable intelligence in any building comes from whoever is bored in the basement.** Nobody briefs the staff on what is secret, so the staff simply tell you, because to them it was never a secret. It was just Tuesday.

The Orange Heir is raising an army of tree-cutters. A bartender said so, over cards, to a stranger, for free.

Meanwhile three floors up a party of professionals has been fighting the same overgrowth one treant at a time for three sessions, being very careful, taking casualties, and not once has anyone thought to go downstairs and ASK THE MAN WITH THE DRINKS.

sections.heading: CROSS-REFERENCE — His Own Party Already Runs The Tree-Cutters
sections.body:
Waluigi checked the satyr's scoop against the archive, expecting to confirm it. Waluigi instead discovered it is not a scoop at all.

Here is the part that turns the satyr's gossip from colour into farce.

The satyr told Bowser, as though disclosing a secret, that the **Orange Heir** is raising an army of tree-cutters. Waluigi has checked. The party directly above Bowser's head does not merely know this. **They are entangled with it.**

From [Chop Bros, the OC Soul Ring & The Guard With No Name](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/feyward_chop_bros_soul_ring_and_the_guard_with_no_name): [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) stood in the heir's war room, at a table-sized tactical map, with **pins for the sixth and seventh tree-cutter divisions** — the sixth inked blocky, the seventh inked apologetic — and barrel tallies running down the margin like a bar bill. The heir told them, personally, that when he went downstairs they **put him in charge of the sixth and seventh divisions**, and that he has not been drinking recently. Hjumpik looked at him and said: *you won a battle, not the war.*

The tree-cutters go back further still — they formed as an organised resistance during [the Revel Crisis](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_feyward_revel_crisis_poison_plants_and_frozen_diplomacy), where the standing assessment was blunt: **the treecutters are cutting but the overgrowth is faster than the cutting.**

So the intelligence Bowser paid two winning hands of cards to obtain is intelligence his own side generated, at a map, in a room upstairs, several sessions ago.

**AND THE STATUE.** Waluigi nearly walked past this one. Bowser passes a stairwell where the stone reads **ARULEAN'S FIRST KNIGHT**, beneath a statue with a rusted sword, and says *wouldn't be a castle without knights* and keeps moving.

Arulean is [Lady Aurelian Corvinarus](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lady_aurelian). The Weaver of the Three Threads. The one holding the Feyward's year at 722 by force. The heir upstairs calls her an **older sister** who *took the throne first.* This is HER house, and in its basement stands a monument to her first knight, rusting, unremarked, three floors below the party trying to work out what she wants.

Bowser walked past a named monument to the war-record of the woman whose manor he is standing in, made a joke about interior decorating, and went to punch a footlocker.

Waluigi has no tidy joke for the statue. Waluigi simply notes that this archive's most persistent failure is people walking past engraved stone because they are in a hurry, and Waluigi includes Waluigi in that.

commentaries.title: The Snowdin Bone-Line Registry
commentaries.subtitle: In Which A Monitored Legion Hour Is Spent On Aunts, A Witness Refuses His Own Family, And The Same Footage Contains Two Different People
commentaries.filed: Harvestide 30, 1045 BF — transcribed off the Gamma Agent's monitored line, forty minutes of it
commentaries.pullQuote: Twenty-eight records asked for a registry loudly enough and for long enough that eventually a registry turned up, on fire, with a pen attached.
commentaries.standfirst: Waluigi got into a sealed civilisation through a permissions form that specified a duration, a monitor and a revocation condition, and forgot to specify a recipient. What Waluigi did with that hour was ask a lazy skeleton about his aunts. In return: a witness who denied his own family name by name, two of his own sentences that turned out to have people living in them, a contract that burned when it was signed, and one piece of footage that contained a different person the second time it was played. Nobody explained the last one. Waluigi is still asking.

sections.heading: Waluigi Spent Somebody Else's Reward On A Genealogy
sections.body:
Waluigi wants to start with the paperwork, because the paperwork is how Waluigi got in the room and the paperwork is the funniest thing in this entire filing.

At the end of the Mount Ebott survey, the Gamma Agent handed the Iron Legion a full intelligence haul — conversations, battle readings, monster technology, the lot — and was asked what he wanted for it. He asked for ONE THING. One Legion-issued secure device. One hour per month. External calls permitted. Monitored by the duty officer. Revocable on conduct.

The authorisation is painfully precise, because the Legion is always painfully precise about permissions and never once precise about consequences.

**Nobody wrote down who he was allowed to call.**

So on Harvestide 30 — the day AFTER High Command reached across a briefing table and physically switched off a recording device mid-sentence, to control what could be known — that monitored hour got spent on a skeleton in Snowdin, and Waluigi was on the other end of it.

Waluigi would like the Legion to sit with the shape of that. Day six: we decide what may be recorded. Day seven: our own reward scheme hands the archive forty unsupervised minutes of Underground testimony, because the form had a box for DURATION and a box for MONITORING and no box for WHOM.

A duty officer logged the call. Waluigi has no doubt whatsoever that the duty officer understood NOT ONE WORD of what followed, and Waluigi hopes he was comfortable.

And what was the archive's great strategic use of this hard-won, once-a-month, monitored channel into a sealed civilisation?

Asking a lazy skeleton about his AUNTS.

WAH. Waluigi regrets nothing. Twenty-eight records depended on it.

One more thing about the timing, because Waluigi is not letting it go.

The Ebott arc is filed five years ahead of the Material present — 1045 BF against the world clock's 1040. Waluigi is conducting an interview in a year the rest of the archive has not reached yet, through a device belonging to an agent whose own high command had, the previous day, demonstrated that it will physically silence a recorder rather than let a briefing be preserved.

So the provenance of this entire filing is: a future year, a borrowed phone, a monitored line, and an institution that had just proven it does not want records to exist.

Waluigi has filed things on worse paper. Not many.

 Waluigi had the recording spool spinning at forty-five revolutions per minute on the studio deck, monitoring every single decibel of subterranean interference!

sections.heading: Twenty-Eight Records Cited A Document That Did Not Exist
sections.body:
Here is the thing that made this interview necessary, and Waluigi files it with some embarrassment.

Twenty-eight dossiers in this archive — [Papyrus](%(L)spapyrus), [Grandpa Semi](%(L)sgrandpa_semi), [Lazybones](%(L)slazybones), [Baby Bones](%(L)sbaby_bones), [Cursive](%(L)scursive), [Pet Rock](%(L)spet_rock), all of them — carry the same line in their status field: *recorded in the Snowdin household registry.*

Twenty-eight records, each citing the registry as the thing that establishes it.

**THE REGISTRY DID NOT EXIST.** Not sealed. Not lost. Not restricted. Never written.

Waluigi has been walking past that for a year. Waluigi, who audits everybody, who counts pins on maps and cross-references casualty lists for fun, had twenty-eight citations pointing at an empty shelf and did not check the shelf.

And here is the part that should bother everybody as much as it bothers Waluigi: the citations came FIRST. The document came second, and it came into existence during an interview that happened BECAUSE of the citations.

That is not how evidence behaves. Evidence sits there being inconvenient until somebody finds it. This behaved like **demand**. Twenty-eight records asked for a registry loudly enough and for long enough that eventually a registry turned up, on fire, with a pen attached.

Waluigi is going to keep saying that until somebody tells him why it is wrong.

And it gets worse when you look at WHO is on the list, because the list is not a bloodline. It is a household that keeps admitting people.

[Pet Rock](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/pet_rock) is a stone. No verified movement, no face, an unquestioned place at the table. [Ness](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/ness) is a human in a striped shirt who earned a seat by being calm and brave in a house full of skeletons. [S' a Real Star](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/real_star) claims the family adopted him because he cheered loudly enough at the night sky, and nobody has produced a document contradicting him.

That is NOT genealogy. That is a guest list that got out of hand and then got FILED.

Waluigi is going to say the quiet part, because the quiet part is the whole file: a family where membership is GRANTED rather than inherited does not need a registry to be true. It needs a registry to be ADMINISTERED. Somebody wanted this household written down, numbered, indexed and cross-referenced — and that somebody was not any of the twenty-eight people in it.

It was the archivist. It is always the archivist. Waluigi is aware of the mirror and will be dealing with it in section six, thank you.

 Every single cross-reference pointed directly into an empty manila folder that smelled of mothballs and bad ink!

sections.heading: The Witness Spent Twenty Minutes Saying No
sections.body:
Waluigi has interviewed a great many people who wanted to be in this archive. Wario has requested his own article FOUR TIMES. This was the first interview with somebody actively trying to get OUT of one.

[Sans](%(L)ssans) took the call from under a pile of laundry, thanked Waluigi for coming on short notice, and then apologised for his own punctuality by blaming Papyrus for having standards. Good start. Warm. Cooperative.

Then Waluigi showed him the family tree and he started saying no, and he did not stop for twenty minutes.

**On his mother.** Told Gee Lady was his mother, he rejected it flatly: his mother was [Toriel](%(L)storiel), a goat, who baked, and who *raised me after everything happened with dad.* Waluigi did not press on the word *everything*, and Waluigi has been annoyed about that ever since. Forty minutes of monitored channel and Waluigi let the single most loaded word in the call go past unexamined.

**On the names.** [Garbage Brother](%(L)sgarbage_brother) — nothing. [Will](%(L)swill) — nothing, unless you mean Papyrus's willpower. [Quantity](%(L)squantity) — nothing. [Pretty Soon](%(L)spretty_soon) — nothing. Cursive is HANDWRITING, and Papyrus once wrote him a puzzle clue in it and he squinted for ten minutes. [Helvetica](%(L)shelvetica) sounded to him like an ancient curse or an expired ketchup brand.

**On the boneless branch.** Shown a family called *Boneless*, Sans stopped and pointed out that they are skeletons and that being made of bones is the entire thing they are. Waluigi accepts this criticism on the archive's behalf.

Then Waluigi showed him the OTHER spelling — **Bonefull**, double L — and something remarkable happened. He paused. He said it was *actually not terrible.* Almost majestic. Noble, even.

Then he said it was still invented.

Waluigi records that moment because it is the only point in the entire interview where Sans LIKED something on the document, and it lasted about four seconds.

**On Lazy Bones.** Waluigi pointed at a name circled in red and asked whether he knew him. Long pause. Then — and this is the only concession Sans made without being shown evidence first — *that's me, pal.* Delivered like an admission. He volunteered the supporting detail unprompted: naps under laundry, skipped guard shifts, and once falling asleep mid-sentence while talking to Toriel about TAXES.

Waluigi has read that last one several times. The man fell asleep during his own tax conversation and remembered it well enough to cite it eighty years later as character evidence against himself.

**On the pet rock.** Then Waluigi dusted off a name filed in the archive right next to Gaster, and read it out: a pet rock.

EVERYTHING STOPPED.

*Little buddy.* He has had it for as long as he can account for. Papyrus finds it strange. Toriel used to WATER it, like a plant. [Asgore](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/asgore) once tried to use magic on it. And Sans's only question — asked with complete sincerity — was how his own pet rock came to be filed beside the most dangerous name in the Underground without anybody mentioning it to him.

Waluigi did not have an answer then and does not have one now.

 Sans leaned back in that folding chair with his slippers propped on the desk like he was waiting for a bus that never runs on Tuesdays!

sections.heading: Two Of His Own Sentences Have People Living In Them
sections.body:
Now the tape, and this is where the file stops being a comedy about aunts.

**Clip one.** Sans, on record, saying *'my brother has a very special attack.'* He confirmed it instantly. Papyrus does. It is the bone rush. He trains for it. No hesitation, no caveat.

**Clip two.** Sans warning Papyrus off a shortcut during puzzle practice: *'if you cheat, you'll end up a dirty brother.'* Also his. Also — he was firm about this — a JOKE. Sibling banter about not taking the easy path. Not a name. Not a person.

And this archive holds a dossier for [Has A Very Special Attack](%(L)shas_a_very_special_attack). And a dossier for [Dirty Brother](%(L)sdirty_brother).

**TWO OF THIS MAN'S OWN SENTENCES HAVE PEOPLE FILED UNDER THEM.**

Sans's reading was immediate and, Waluigi concedes without pleasure, methodologically sound: somebody has been taking things he said about Papyrus, cutting them out of their sentences, and building relatives around the fragments. He then proved it in real time. Shown clip three — himself, mid-sentence, *'my brother will—'*, cut hard before the verb — he identified the edit before Waluigi could, guessed the missing ending (*eat his spaghetti*, probably, or *solve another puzzle*), and called the whole exercise sneaky.

His summary of the method is better than anything Waluigi wrote in the filing: *you took pieces of truth and built an entire fake world around them.* Clever, he allowed. Realistic, no.

Waluigi would love to leave it there. Waluigi cannot, because of one detail.

**Dirty Brother repairs chimneys.** His dossier has him soot-covered because he fixes boiler shafts, chimney flues and old puzzle mechanisms. That is a TRADE. A forger working from the phrase *dirty brother* invents somebody disgusting — crumbs in the ribcage, sauce on the shoulder. Whoever filed this one invented somebody EMPLOYED.

Soot is not a slander. It is a JOB DESCRIPTION. And Waluigi does not know what to do with that.

Waluigi has sat with the two readings for some time and will state both rather than pick.

**READING ONE: it is forgery, and a careful one.** Somebody with access to recordings of Sans built a household out of his offcuts, which explains why the only two entries anybody can verify are the two he happens to have said aloud.

**READING TWO: it is not forgery at all.** A family whose members are NAMED for the circumstances in which they are first spoken about would leave exactly this evidence behind — Dirty Brother exists because the words were said, and the words being Sans's is the mechanism rather than the tell.

Waluigi finds reading two far more frightening and cannot rule it out on the available paper.

 Waluigi replayed those two sentences until the magnetic tape was practically squealing against the bronze playback head!

sections.heading: The Same Footage, Played Twice, With Different People In It
sections.body:
Then the screen cut out and this stopped being about editing at all.

**Wing dings.** Small winged glyphs, soft chimes underneath. Sans tensed the moment they appeared — those symbols are tied to [Wing Gaster](%(L)swing_gaster) specifically, surfacing when the name is spoken or when something of his legacy activates. And he gave ground for the first time in the whole call: *that's not a special effect you can just add with editing software.* If the dings are real, the video might not be fake.

**Then the power cut.** Waluigi would like to note that Waluigi was on a telephone at this point and could hear none of it, and is reconstructing from a witness who was frightened. Not a flicker. The room went fully dark and the screen went to a black Sans described as WRONG rather than off. And a distorted voice arrived — not through the speakers, he was specific about that, but from the walls, or from inside the head:

> **dark... darker... yet darker...**

Sans did not move. He said the phrase and its rhythm are how *he* talks when things go bad down there, and repeated something Papyrus told him once: when everything gets too quiet and too dark at the same time, something old is waking up.

Waluigi files that quotation exactly as received. **Then two silhouettes.** One unmistakably Sans — lanky, slumped, hood up. The other blurred: no features, only shape. Possibly a hunch. Possibly wings. Possibly static pretending to be a form. He said his bones were telling him it was wrong, and that the second figure felt familiar *like an echo from before time started.*

And now the part Waluigi genuinely cannot explain, and has stopped pretending to.

Asked whether he remembered standing there, Sans dropped every joke he had and said yes. Clear as day. Realer than most memories he has.

**So Waluigi played it again with the lights on.** Same footage. NO FOG.

**The blurred figure was gone, and [Gee Lady](%(L)sgee_lady) was standing where it had been, hands over Sans, the whole scene brighter.**

Sans asked why the video changed between viewings.

That is the best question anybody asked in forty minutes of monitored call, it was asked by the man who had spent the previous twenty minutes insisting none of this was real, and NOBODY ANSWERED IT. Not Times New Roman. Not Gee Lady, later, when she was standing in the room. Not Waluigi, who was supposed to be conducting the interview and who instead sat there holding a rewind button like an idiot.

 Rewind the tape three seconds! Watch the static lines roll across the monitor tube like summer thunder over the mountain pass!

sections.heading: He Signed It Without Joking, And Then It Caught Fire
sections.body:
[Times New Roman](%(L)stimes_new_roman) arrived mid-call with a clipboard and spectacles, moving — in Sans's description — too cleanly, like text that had not been touched by real life. He opened with *hey, what's up, brother.*

Then came the title card: **EXACTLY WHEN SANS'S PUNS BECAME A HOUSEHOLD HAZARD**, attributed to Waluigi, noting that the entries are kept for completeness, that Sans has never let anybody borrow that section, and that he reads it when he thinks nobody is watching.

Then **archive log entry #472 — 'sans uses pun in public for the 10,001st time.'**

Asked who authorised the documentation, Times New Roman did not blink: *no permission required. this is an archival initiative.*

Waluigi needs to stop being funny for exactly one paragraph.

**Waluigi has said that sentence.** Not a sentence like it. That one, in that register, to people who asked why they were in this encyclopedia. Waluigi keeps a file on a man who has never spoken to Waluigi. Waluigi has filed children, corpses, and a rock. The difference Waluigi would LIKE to claim is that Waluigi's records do not summon anybody — and that is a difference of EFFECT, not of method, and Waluigi has elected not to run the experiment that would settle it.

Right. Voice back on.

Asked whether this was a brotherly reunion, Times New Roman said **'affirmative'** and nothing else. No embrace. No shared childhood. Sans's take: the most awkward reunion in history, like meeting a twin from a universe where emotions had been deleted.

Then the document. **Official Archival Record of Sibling Designation.** Brotherhood substantiated by **lineage code #TNR-01** — no mother, no father, just a number. Footnotes. An appendix reference for skeletal alignment. Gee Lady listed as a designated family member *confirmed via lipstick signature analysis and emotional resonance frequency matching*, which Waluigi has read eleven times and which does not improve.

And the paper kept unrolling. Off the table. Onto the floor. Duplicate entries. Question-marked titles. An unverified branch pending DNA. And at the very bottom, alone, underlined twice in red: **Wingding Gaster.** No title. No question mark.

A blank signature box. A PEN. A man who had said NO for twenty minutes.

**And Sans signed it in plain letters with no flourish.** Waluigi wants that on the record, because this man does EVERYTHING as a joke, and he did not do this as a joke.

The contract caught fire — silent blue flame, no heat, every name curling to ash that rose as smoke shaped like small bones. Times New Roman watched it burn WITHOUT REACTING, which is not the face of a man losing a document he just produced. It is the face of a man watching an expected step complete.

Then they came out of the light. Cursive adjusting a cuff. Gee Lady, who did not glitch, did not pose, and simply smiled. And at the back, the shadow that had been indistinct in every single frame resolved, stepped forward, and unfurled one wing.

And then it was all gone. No fade. Just absent, like something that had never been switched on.

Sans was alone in a room full of socks, one of them somehow in the ceiling fan, with Papyrus stamping down the hall to conduct a disciplinary interview about hygiene and nothing else. Seven socks in places they do not belong, he said.

Sans lay down on the bed and said the family tree stuff had felt real.

The line was still open. Waluigi said nothing, which is not a thing Waluigi does. WAH.

 That iron clipboard looked heavy enough to anchor a tugboat in high tide, and the ink in his pen was completely dry!

sections.heading: Seven Socks, And The Only Witness Nobody Interviewed
sections.body:
Waluigi wants to end on the man who was down the hall the entire time.

[Papyrus](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/papyrus) did not see the gold light. He did not see the wing. He arrived immediately afterwards, stood in the doorway with his arms crossed and his scarf fluttering with what Sans called RAGE ENERGY, and delivered his finding in the flat voice of a Royal Guardsman reading a charge sheet.

**Seven socks. In places they do not belong.**

One in the ceiling fan. Waluigi has asked twice how a sock gets into a ceiling fan and has received no satisfactory account from anybody.

And here is what makes this funny and then stops making it funny.

**Papyrus is the subject of BOTH verified quotations in the entire filing.** *Dirty brother* was said about him. *Has a very special attack* was said about him. The two entries on that family tree that are demonstrably built out of real sentences are both built out of sentences about PAPYRUS — and Papyrus has never been asked about either one.

He is also, by the archive's own records, the family member most likely to have an opinion. He keeps puzzles in binders. He tracks skeleton ancestry like sacred law. Sans said outright that Papyrus would have been contacted by the royal genealogy office by now if any of this were real, and would have FRAMED the document if it had been.

So the single best-qualified witness to the Snowdin Bone-Line Registry was forty feet away, holding a sock, and no one on either end of the call thought to put him on.

Waluigi did not think of it. Waluigi had a monitored hour, a burning contract, and an ancient scientist coming through a wall, and Waluigi did not think to shout down the hallway.

That is the interview that should happen next, and Waluigi is filing the omission as his own rather than pretending it was a scheduling problem.

Meanwhile Papyrus is the ONLY person in this entire filing who got a clear, checkable, verifiable result out of the evening. Twenty-eight contested relatives, one burning instrument, a lineage code with no parent attached, footage containing two different people — and one skeleton who counted seven socks, knew exactly where all seven should have been, and was correct about every single one.

Waluigi envies him ENORMOUSLY.

**WAH.**

 Waluigi is locking this master reel in the fireproof safe under the workbench, and nobody touches the latch without a written permit from the front desk! WAH!

commentaries.title: The Airlift That Never Came
commentaries.subtitle: In Which A Code Is Quoted, A Bush Is Incinerated, And The Most Valuable Object In A Burning Grove Turns Out To Be A Laminated Card
commentaries.filed: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — assembled from four separate accounts, none of which agree about the helicopter
commentaries.pullQuote: They killed the Scorncrow last filing. Waluigi would like somebody to explain what they won.
commentaries.standfirst: Waluigi went into this filing certain there was a villain in it and came out without one. A Legion guard carried a wounded Toad out of a burning grove against everybody's wishes including the Toad's, and was not obviously wrong. A wizard spent his last big spell on a bush and changed nothing except the temperature. A fourteen-year-old re-armoured off a corpse and walked out on her own feet. And a man with knights turned down an expired coupon so he could take a student ID instead. No helicopter came.

sections.heading: A Man Picked Up A Wounded Toad And Walked Off, And Was Not Obviously Wrong
sections.body:
Waluigi has spent longer on this section than on anything else in the filing, because Waluigi went into it certain of who the villain was and came out without one.

An [Iron Legion](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/iron_legion) guard hoisted [Salam](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/eager) — unconscious — onto his shoulder. *I'll take him to safety.*

Everybody objected at once. [Archie](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_miser) said no. [Feyward Dan](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/dan_the_toad) ran over and asked what he thought he was doing. [Markop](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/markop) told him flatly that he was not part of their group and had no standing to remove one of their people.

And the guard said: **I CAN'T DROP HIM. IT'S PART OF THE LEGION CODE. NO MAN LEFT BEHIND.**

Now. Waluigi would love to file that as bureaucratic cowardice, because that is the shape the archive usually finds when the Legion quotes its own paperwork at somebody. It does not fit. He was not running from the fight — he was carrying a casualty *through* it.

Then Eager, awake enough to speak, said **PLEASE DROP OUR FRIEND**, and the guard did not. That is where the code stops being noble and becomes a thing done TO somebody.

And then came the real reason, which arrived after the rule and not before it:

> *I'm not leaving half a dead person here while you guys gallivant around and get killed. I trust myself more than you guys.*

**THAT IS NOT THE CODE.** The code was the justification he reached for. The distrust was the motive, and he said it out loud in front of them.

Markop's counter was the only one available and it was a good one — he's part of our squad, once this is over we patch him up, don't take one of our guys away from us. The guard's answer: **YOUR INCOMPETENCE IS BEYOND ME.**

Markop said: *we killed the Scorncrow.*

The guard said: *you may have killed him, but look at what cost.*

WAH. Waluigi has read that exchange more times than is healthy looking for the line where the guard becomes wrong, and cannot find it. Look at what he was standing in. [Salam](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/salam) face-down with his face opened. Markop upright and fighting while badly hurt. A Toad unconscious over his shoulder. The guard looked at that inventory and declined to leave a wounded man with the people who had produced it.

He was RUDE. He was UNILATERAL. He overrode the patient's own stated wish, which is the part Waluigi will not let him have.

But *incompetent* is not a slander when the evidence is lying on the floor in front of you.

Waluigi wants to add the detail that makes the whole argument worse, and it is a small one.

While this was going on, [Eager](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/eager) — the person being argued over — swung at a spider, missed, and hit **THE GUARD CARRYING SALAM.**

So the party's case for keeping their casualties was being made in real time by a boy who could not reliably tell a spider from an ally. Waluigi is not mocking him. He was concussed and being carried. But the guard was watching that happen while Markop explained that these were the people best placed to look after the wounded.

And the last exchange of the night, when Markop caught up with them: *hey, where are you going?* To Legionhold hospital, the best in the area. Markop said he could heal him.

**He is scared, we can fix that right away.**

WAH. Waluigi has filed a great many Legion sentences and that one belongs in a frame. Not *he is bleeding.* Not *he is concussed.* **Scared** — treated as a condition, with a remedy, available on site.

Waluigi will say the uncomfortable part plainly: if Waluigi had been that guard, Waluigi would have taken the boy too, and Waluigi would have been just as rude about it.

sections.heading: What's A Helicopter
sections.body:
*Not to worry — we have a helicopter to airlift us all out of here.*

**"What's a helicopter?"** said Dan.

Waluigi is going to sit with that for a paragraph, because it is the funniest line in the filing and also the saddest one.

This is a Toad paladin from a plane that has no sky. He has spent this entire operation inside a tree, under a web ceiling, in a grove where the roof is spider silk. Somebody has just promised him rescue by a machine he has no word for, in a place where the machine could not possibly land, and his response is polite curiosity.

The guards went further. They would **put on quite a show**. Archie would be taken away to **LEGIONHOLD** — *our very own* — which is the single most Legion phrase anybody has produced this year. Waluigi notes they were advertising a prison to a man standing in a burning web while spiders closed on him.

Dan's answer to the promise of his colleague's arrest was *no matter that*, and then he smote an ettercap with his longsword and went off to notify everyone else, because there was a job on.

**NO HELICOPTER ARRIVED.** NONE.

Waluigi wants that in capitals and on its own line. It was promised. It was promised a second time. Nothing in the entire record shows an aircraft, a rotor, a downdraft, a landing, or a single person leaving the ground.

What actually happened is that the guards left **on foot**, at a sprint, one of them tripped, and Salam went out in a fireman's carry.

So either the Legion does not have a helicopter and said it did, or the Legion has a helicopter and did not send it. Waluigi cannot tell which from the record and finds both readings unflattering. The organisation that spent the night lecturing a centaur about competence promised an AIRLIFT and delivered a PIGGYBACK.

And for completeness, here is what the extraction actually looked like, since it is the closest thing to an airlift anybody got.

One guard SPRINTED. One guard BOLTED. One of them **tripped**, and [Salam](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/salam) — already unconscious, already face-opened — went down on the ground and was **dragged by a spider** before an already-injured guard caught him by the leg and hauled him back.

Then they fireman-carried Salam out through the brood on foot.

That is the operation that was described, ninety seconds earlier, as an airlift.

Waluigi has requested Legion air support exactly once in his career and received a form. Waluigi mentions this only so the reader understands Waluigi is not guessing.

sections.heading: Remi, On Her Own, Doing It Properly
sections.body:
While all that was happening, [Remi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) had a few minutes to herself and used them better than anybody else used theirs all night.

She CHECKED THE BLOOD. *Where did this come from.* Waluigi wants a moment of appreciation here, because she is the only person in the grove who asked that question about blood on her own body. Everybody else was busy having opinions.

Her dress was already destroyed — the hooks took it apart in the previous filing. She took it off and pulled a **chain shirt** off a body and put that on instead. She picked up a shield, considered it, and **left it for now**, which is a sentence about load management that Waluigi did not expect from a fourteen-year-old.

Then she healed herself. Not enough. She did it again.

> *Okay, now I'm feeling a little bit... still not enough.*

Then she took a **battle axe** off the same body, and walked out of the grove, and escaped.

Waluigi is going to state the obvious because nobody else will: **SHE IS THE ONLY PERSON WHO LEFT THAT GROVE UNDER HER OWN POWER.** Markop got dragged out through a gauntlet behind a javelin. Salam left in a fireman's carry; Eager remained with the party. Wario bought his way out. The Toads were abandoned.

Remi assessed, re-armoured, self-treated twice, re-armed, and walked.

Four filings ago Waluigi was describing this person as *the youngest member* and filing her behind Markop in every list. Waluigi has already said once that this would stop. It is now being enforced.

One more thing, and it is the only moment of real vulnerability she showed.

The record notes she was FREAKING OUT later, in the wrights' room, when the axe stopped working. She hit one and it started **glowing**. She hit it again. Then something hit her and it was **not glowing any more**, and the composure went.

Waluigi files both halves deliberately. The girl who calmly stripped a corpse for armour and the girl panicking with a battle axe she can barely lift are the same fourteen-year-old, twenty minutes apart, and the archive does not get to keep only the impressive one.

Waluigi would also like it known that Waluigi has never once thought to check whose blood was on him, and has been on fire more recently than Remi has.

sections.heading: The Last Big Spell In The Book, And Where It Went
sections.body:
[Markop](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/markop) was surrounded. Three spiders in front, a giant green one and two smaller behind, closing. He had already stopped his own bleeding — he is no longer bloody, which the record notes because he had been fighting already badly hurt from the execution.

He called out: **use fireball, use your lightning, anything, before they close in.**

So Archie got out the spellbook. And here is the sequence, exactly as recorded, because the sequence is the joke and also the problem:

1. He **erased some crossed-out words.**
2. He found his **last high-level spell.** One left.
3. He **circled it.**
4. He said **FIREBALL**, LOUDLY.
5. He **aimed at a bush.**

The grove caught. Again. This is the *same grove* that burned in the Scorncrow skirmish, now burning a second time, lit deliberately by the party's own wizard, with the entire party still standing inside it.

Waluigi is not going to call that a blunder, and wants to be precise about why. Markop had asked for exactly this. The spiders were closing. Doing nothing was also a decision and a worse one.

But look at what the record says happened next: **EVERYONE WHO WAS SURROUNDED BEFORE THE FIREBALL WAS STILL SURROUNDED AFTER IT.** Archie later *shattered the space* around the spiders as well, and when it cleared, *all of them were still standing.*

Two of the biggest things in Archie's arsenal went off in that grove and the tactical situation did not move. The only durable change either spell produced is that the room is now on fire.

Meanwhile Markop, trying to line up a shot and finding nowhere to stand, trod on a twig, got dry branch and cobweb stuck in his hand, and then — mid-declaration, mid-sentence, while announcing he was going to get a better angle — stepped squarely on a nest of **SPIDER EGGS.**

Waluigi did not invent that detail and would not have dared.

Waluigi will give [Dan](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/dan_the_toad) the credit that Archie did not earn, because the contrast is the whole section.

Dan said he would make this quick and reached for his javelin. Then he STOPPED. He pointed one finger at Markop first, sent a **barrier** across the length of the grove to a man he could barely see through smoke — and only then threw.

The javelin brought the spider down. Markop got out.

One of those two casters spent his biggest remaining resource on shrubbery. The other one spent a fraction of a second checking that the person he was helping would survive being helped.

Waluigi is aware Waluigi has thrown ice into a crowded room and will not be taking questions on the comparison.

sections.heading: He Turned Down A Coupon
sections.body:
And then, in a torchlit room full of wrights, the night presented its bill.

[Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) had blundered in swinging and found nothing to hit. [Pierce Anamatar](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/pierce_anamatar) came in from another room to ask why a stranger was fighting his people.

What follows is a small masterclass and Waluigi is filing it as one.

*It hurt real bad. People chase me.*

***Aww. It hurt real bad. Want a bandaid? A sippy cup, maybe? Aww. Coward.*** And: *you can't even handle a handful of knights. Stand down, my men.*

Wario said he was trying to get away from danger. Anamatar said he had come into his den and attacked him. Wario said he came to get away from the spiders. Anamatar asked whether he was really frightened of a few creepy-crawlies.

Remi said: **YES. THEY'RE TERRIFYING.** And then asked whether he had seen what they look like.

And the mockery stopped dead.

Waluigi notes that. The moment the mark stopped performing and simply admitted the truth, the performance on the other side ENDED TOO — and the actual business began. This is Guild-controlled ground. He does not like the Guild. He will send them back where they came from **in exchange for something of theirs.**

He asked for the **siglet** — Tymnas's ring, the objective this party has been chasing across filings.

An **expired coupon** was offered. It was DECLINED.

Waluigi wants that on the record because it proves the next part was a *choice*. He was not taking whatever was going. He looked around a room containing a battle axe, a chain shirt stripped off a corpse, two daggers, a steel dog and a wizard, and he walked over to the fourteen-year-old and asked for her card.

*I've got a single, very durable school ID card.*

***I'll take it.***

Waluigi has gone and checked, because Waluigi always checks. [Remi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) left **Gehenna Academy** without a formal withdrawal. There is no exit paperwork. There is no record closing her enrolment.

**THAT CARD WAS THE LAST OBJECT IN THE WORLD ASSERTING SHE HAD EVER BEEN A STUDENT ANYWHERE.**

She handed it over to get three people out of a burning wood, and by the record she did not hesitate, and Waluigi does not believe she has worked out yet what she gave away. A man who deals exclusively in *things that belong to somebody* now holds the only paper that says who she is.

And the three Toads sat in the dirt and watched every friendly face in the grove walk off without them. WAH.

Waluigi does not know what Anamatar wants with it. Waluigi knows only that Waluigi has watched this man take payment twice now, and both times he took the thing that could not be bought back.

sections.heading: Waluigi Counts What The Night Actually Bought
sections.body:
Waluigi is going to total this up, because the archive keeps recording these nights as victories and this one was a PURCHASE.

Last filing they killed the Scorncrow. Waluigi filed that with reservations and stands by them. Here is what the follow-up cost, and Waluigi has checked every line against the record:

**One promised helicopter, which did not exist or was not sent.** Waluigi cannot tell which and finds both readings unflattering.

**One casualty, Salam, gone.** Salam left in Legion hands, bound for LEGIONHOLD — the same facility those same guards had promised would host [Archie's](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_miser) arrest. Nobody has confirmed they arrived. Nobody has gone to check.

**One wizard's last high-level spell, spent on a bush**, in a grove that had already burned once, with everyone still inside it.

**One centaur on a motorbike he cannot ride.** Waluigi wants that filed literally. [Markop](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/markop) crossed a gauntlet of spiders, reached [Wario's](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario) bike, started the engine, and has NO IDEA WHAT HE IS DOING. That is the party's exit strategy.

**Three Toads abandoned in the dirt**, watching every friendly face in the grove walk away from them. Waluigi notes nobody has gone back for them either.

**And one student ID.** Which is the item Waluigi keeps returning to, because it is the only thing in that list that cannot be replaced by anybody. A helicopter can be sent later. A spell slot comes back with a night's sleep. A motorbike can be taught.

There is no second copy of the paper that says [Remi Akamatsu](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) was enrolled at Gehenna Academy, and there is no clerk left to issue one, and she gave it to a stranger in a torchlit room to buy three people a walk out of a wood.

Waluigi would like somebody to explain what they WON. WAH.

sections.heading: The Grove Was Not One Fight, Which Is Why Everyone Was Right And Everyone Was In The Way
sections.body:
The archive keeps calling this a retreat, which is technically accurate and emotionally insufficient. It was not one retreat. It was five people making separate exits through the same burning web while three other people sang loudly enough to summon the spiders. Waluigi wants that sentence on the outside of the folder.

Salam was down. Markop was still fighting while badly hurt. Eager was unconscious but intermittently articulate. Archie had one large spell left. Dan was trying to keep the party connected across smoke and bark. Remi was alone, checking her own blood. These are not positions on a battlefield map. These are different kinds of emergency occupying the same grove. **FIVE EMERGENCIES. ONE ADDRESS.** Waluigi checked the headcount twice, and the headcount kept disagreeing with itself.

This is why the Legion guard and Markop argued past each other. Markop saw a squad member being removed. The guard saw a casualty in a collapsing position whose friends were actively arguing while the fire came back. Markop claimed membership. The guard claimed the code. Eager claimed the right to be put down. Three authorities entered one decision and none of them cancelled the others. Waluigi has seen less complicated meetings about constitutional succession, and once won one of those by waiting for everybody else to finish shouting.

The guard said the Legion had a hospital. Markop said the party would patch Eager up. The guard said he trusted himself more than them. Waluigi would like to report that Waluigi found a sentence in this filing where one side became obviously wrong. Waluigi would also like to report that Waluigi did not. The evidence was standing around them: Salam down, Markop bleeding, Eager unable to fight reliably, the grove on fire. Competence was not an insult here. It was a claim with witnesses.

It was still a custody transfer. The patient said to drop their friend and the guard refused. The code carried him out, but the institution carried him out too. Waluigi can hold both truths. This is what makes the filing irritating. If the Legion had been purely villainous, Waluigi could file the correct moral conclusion and go eat something. Instead the guard made a defensible decision in an indefensible manner, and then the organisation promised **A HELICOPTER** it did not provide. WAH.

sections.heading: Every Exit Has A Price And Remi Pays In Paper
sections.body:
Remi’s exit is not the Legion’s exit, and Waluigi will not permit the archive to merge them because the difference is the whole point. She checks the blood. She removes the dress destroyed by hooks. She takes a chain shirt from a body, considers a shield, declines the extra weight, heals herself twice, takes a battle axe, and walks. **ASSESS. RE-ARMOUR. TREAT. RE-ARM. LEAVE.** This is the cleanest sequence in the grove and it belongs to a mid-teen who is shorter than the adults, not a tiny mascot and not a miniature soldier.

Then Markop escapes behind Dan’s barrier and javelin. The barrier comes first. Dan points at Markop, sends protection, and only then throws. The spider falls. Markop gets through the gauntlet and ends up behind Wario’s motorbike, which he starts despite having no idea how to ride it. Waluigi has filed transportation errors before. Waluigi has never filed one with this much smoke.

In the den, Wario punches nothing. Pierce Anamatar enters, mocks him, asks whether he is afraid of the spiders, and receives the honest answer: yes, because have you seen them? The mockery stops. The terms begin. The siglet is requested. An expired coupon is offered. **THE COUPON IS REJECTED.** Rejecting it is the only decision made in that den Waluigi endorses without reservation. Then Anamatar takes Remi’s student ID.

The card is the detail Waluigi cannot let pass. It is laminated. It is durable. It is also the last external paper proving Remi attended Gehenna Academy, because she left without a formal withdrawal. Anamatar may not have known that. The record does not establish that he knew it. What the record does establish is that he selected an object belonging to a specific person after rejecting an object that did not. Waluigi is not calling this a conspiracy. Waluigi is calling it a pattern with a receipt.

The Toads get no bargain. They sing, the spiders follow, and they run faster while singing faster. The guards leave on foot. Remi leaves on her own feet. Markop leaves behind a magical barrier. Wario’s group leaves by surrendering a piece of Remi’s former life to a ghost in a shack. No helicopter arrives. **THE WORD WAS AN AIRLIFT. THE EVENT WAS A COLLECTION OF PRICES.** WAH.

sections.heading: What The File Can Prove After Everyone Has Left
sections.body:
The physical sequence matters more than the promised one, and the filing has to keep the two in different drawers. **STATEMENTS FLOAT. ACTIONS LAND.** The helicopter is a statement. The trip is an action. Salam being dragged by a spider and then caught by an injured guard is an action. Eager striking the guard carrying Salam is an action. Archie’s fireball changes the grove without freeing the surrounded people. Dan’s barrier reaches Markop before the javelin does. Remi’s chain shirt and battle axe leave the scene with her. These are the things Waluigi can put his finger on.

What Waluigi cannot put his finger on is the helicopter. No landing. No machine. No rotor. No lift. The absence does not tell us whether the Legion lied, failed, or simply had a plan that belonged to another version of the night. It tells us the party trusted a future event that never became a present one. Waluigi has done this himself with a tennis schedule and a catering promise. The difference is that Waluigi’s failure did not involve a burning grove. Usually.

The same discipline applies to Anamatar. Waluigi can say he rejected the coupon and accepted the student ID. Waluigi can say the ID still carried Remi’s school identity. Waluigi can say it was surrendered for passage. Waluigi cannot say Anamatar understood the full emotional value of the card. The paper does not say. Waluigi cannot say the ghost wanted the card for a hidden ritual. The paper does not say that either. **THE PAPER REFUSES TO SAY, AND THE PAPER IS CORRECT.** Sometimes a document is most useful when it refuses to become a theory.

The event closes with no single winner. The Legion gets its casualties to the road. Remi gets out. Markop gets out. Wario’s group gets out. The Toads remain behind. Archie still has to answer for the fireball, and the party still has to answer for letting the Legion take Eager. Waluigi’s ruling is therefore not that somebody was right. It is that the grove converted every argument into a physical consequence, and the people who left carried those consequences with them. WAH.

sections.heading: The Last View Is The Important One
sections.body:
The last view of the grove is not the guard's shoulder, Remi's axe, or the fireball. It is the people who remain watching the exits.
