The Toads sit in the dirt, under a roof that has now burned twice, while every route around them fills with motion that is not theirs: guards carrying casualties, Markop squeezed through behind a barrier, Remi walking, Wario bargaining indoors.

Waluigi wants this noted, because the exits in this filing keep being recorded one at a time and they should not be: **NOT ONE OF THOSE ROUTES WAS SHARED.** The guards' route did not include the Toads. The barrier covered Markop. The bargain covered Wario's group. The chain shirt covered Remi. The Toads' route is their own legs and a song, and the spiders have already demonstrated what they think of the song. Five plans in one grove, and none of them with a spare seat.

Waluigi has written this as a rescue because people did get out. Waluigi has written this as a failure because nobody got out together. Both descriptions survive the evidence, and the second one is truer. Between the two, the party's shape changed in a single night. Loyalty remains, but logistics won the argument. The person who can carry a body decides where that body goes. The person with a card decides what she can afford to lose. The person with a javelin decides who gets one more step.

And here the record does the thing Waluigi hates most in a filing: it goes quiet where the last line should be. The paper does not say the Toads got up. The paper does not say they got out. The paper does not say they didn't. The account keeps moving because the people telling it were already leaving, and Waluigi resents this filing for making Waluigi type all three of the sentences above.

That is the story, and the commentary is not allowed to make it tidier. The grove was not tidied. It burned, the spiders moved, and the promised aircraft stayed absent. If a helicopter had come, it would have seen the whole grove at once, which is the only angle from which the night ever adds up. No helicopter came. **THE VIEW FROM THE DIRT WILL HAVE TO DO.** WAH.

commentaries.title: The Assault on Bowser’s Throne Room: The Dragon at the Window and the Castle That Would Not Surrender
commentaries.subtitle: In Which The False Heir Opens The Inside, A Dragon Breaks The Outside, And Bowser Evacuates The People Before The Throne

commentaries.pullQuote: The false heir opened the inside, the dragon broke the outside, and Bowser still had to explain the switch.
commentaries.standfirst: Waluigi retells the full recovered assault on Bowser's throne room: the false Bowser Jr. infiltration, the dragon through the window and wall, the retreat order, the traitors, the evacuation route, the switch nobody could identify, Fawthful's ruler-then-god claim, Sir Frankfurt's impossible family history, and the surviving force trying to decide where a kingdom goes after its castle stops being one place.

sections.heading: The Inside Was Already Open, Which Is A Terrible Way To Begin A Castle Assault
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

*The second half of the record is what happens after the fake Bowser Jr. session has already done its work. The attackers did not begin at a distant wall: they used the false heir to infiltrate Bowser’s throne room, then brought the dragon into the room that represented his command. Saying that Bowser’s Castle was merely lost is an understatement. The throne room was breached from inside and then physically broken open while Bowser was still standing there. The enemy has a dragon. The defenders have Goombas, Koopas, a few Magikoopas, one Hammer Bro who knows when to leave, and a king who is still trying to decide whether the self-destruct switch is a weapon or a joke. WAH.*

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

## The Throne Room Was Breached

The recovered assault took place in Bowser’s throne room. The first breach was the false Bowser Jr. session: the fake heir gave the infiltrators a plausible reason to enter and kept Bowser looking at a family performance while Fawthful, Mimbus, and the hostile operation gained access to the seat of power. That is why the throne-room compromise is Session I and this assault is Session II. The second breach was the dragon breaking through the throne-room window and wall.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

This is more severe than saying that the castle was lost. A castle can be abandoned, retaken, or described as a military position. The throne room being breached means the king’s actual command space was penetrated, its doors and routes were turned against him, and the invaders could make their claim in front of the throne while Bowser was still fighting. Bowser did not surrender the castle. He ordered the garrison away from the dragon so there would be survivors to carry the kingdom forward, then came back to challenge the occupation.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

The dragon came through the smoke with the sound of stone being dragged across stone. Its head cleared the outer wall first. Then one claw hooked over the battlement and the wall began to shed blocks into the courtyard.

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

Bowser saw his troops turn toward it. He also saw the shape of that turn: Goombas bunching under the gatehouse, Koopas lifting their shields, and three defenders looking over their shoulders for the corridor they planned to use when the king stopped watching.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

**“Back!”** Bowser roared. **“Get away from the dragon!”**

The command moved faster than the fear. Koopa shells locked into a line and rolled sideways across the yard, making a low barrier between the dragon's reach and the barracks door. Goombas dropped flat, ran beneath the swinging edge of the dragon's jaw, and hauled wounded soldiers by their belts toward the stairs. It was not a beautiful formation. It worked because the small bodies went where the large body could not.

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

The retreat order is filed as [[prop:prop_bowser_retreat_order|Bowser’s order to pull the line away from the dragon]]. It is short, direct, and written for troops who have no time to admire the king's phrasing.

## Fire, Stone, and the First Retreat

Bowser planted both feet in the courtyard and breathed.

Fire rolled out of him in a broad orange sheet. It struck the dragon's throat, lit the broken masonry, and turned the rain of dust into sparks. The dragon recoiled just far enough for the front line to move. Bowser followed with a ground pound that travelled through the courtyard like a dropped bell. The flagstones buckled. The dragon's hooked claw slipped. Two Goombas shouted in triumph and immediately remembered they were supposed to be retreating.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

A Magikoopa snapped a wand toward the eastern stair. Purple light caught six Koopas and moved them three floors upward in a single blink. Another Magikoopa teleported the wounded behind the kitchens. A third tried to move a supply cart, lost the cart, and delivered only the wheels.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

sections.heading: Bowser Says Get Away From The Dragon And Waluigi Says LISTEN TO HIM
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

The useful magic was not elegant. It was distance. Every teleport made a few bodies harder for the dragon to reach and a little easier for the traitors to count.

The traitors showed themselves when the inner gate opened from the wrong side. A Koopa with a red armband waved the attackers through. A Goomba pulled the chain on the second portcullis and then stood aside as if the motion had been an accident. The castle's own corridors began sending people toward the breach.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

Bowser saw the red armband. He saw the dragon behind it. He did not have time to ask how many more there were.

## The Hammer Bro Knows When to Leave

The Hammer Bro held the west passage until the ceiling shook. He threw a hammer into the dragon's eye, missed, hit a traitor, and did not stop to find out whether the result was politically complicated. When the second wall cracked, he backed toward the evacuation stair.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

Bowser shouted for him to hold.

The Hammer Bro shouted back that he had held.

Then he retreated.

The retreat was not cowardice. It was the first honest order anybody had followed all night. The west passage was no longer a position. It was a place where the ceiling was about to become a floor. The Hammer Bro took the surviving Goombas with him, and the Koopas closed their shells behind them long enough for the Magikoopas to teleport the last wounded defender out.

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

Fawthful's forces followed through the broken gate. Mimbus came with them. The Jester was nowhere in the smoke. Cackletta's magic flashed above the inner wall, turning the stone red from the inside.

## The Evacuation Plan and the Switch

Bowser reached the lower command room with the dragon's roar shaking dust from the map cabinets. He wanted a counterattack. The remaining officers wanted a route. Both positions were honest. Only one of them kept the troops alive.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

The evacuation plan spread across the table: barracks first, wounded by Magikoopa teleport, stores through the lava tunnel, rear guard at the inner stair, and nobody touching the switch until the last defender was clear.

The switch sat beneath a metal cover beside the map case. A painted label above it read **SELF-DESTRUCT**. A second, smaller label underneath read **DO NOT USE FOR LIGHTING**. A third label, written in a different hand, said **THIS ONE MAY BE THE LIGHTING**.

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

The label is filed as [[prop:prop_castle_self_destruct_switch_label|the switch plate that could not agree with itself]].

Bowser stared at it.

A Goomba said the switch destroyed the castle. A Koopa said the switch opened the emergency lamps. A Magikoopa said teleporting the switch would be safer. Somebody had already tried, and the switch had teleported back into its bracket.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

Bowser lifted the cover and found two identical red toggles.

Nobody knew which one was the real switch.

That was the joke. It was also the evacuation plan's worst possible ending.

Bowser closed the cover without touching either toggle and ordered the troops out through the lava tunnel. The castle could be rebuilt. A castle full of defenders who had been blown up by their own labelled furniture would be harder to explain.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

## The Breach and the Claim

The throne-room wall gave way before the last line cleared the lower hall. The sound was not an explosion. It was a long stone groan followed by the collapse of everything that had been pretending to be one wall.

Fawthful walked through the opening in the throne-room wall with dust on the shoulders and the dragon behind him. Mimbus came at his side. Cackletta's spellwork crawled along the broken masonry in green lines. The traitors had stopped hiding. The remaining loyalists had stopped pretending there was a clean way to win.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

sections.heading: The West Passage, The Hammer Bro, And The First Honest Retreat
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

Bowser came back up the stair instead of leaving with the first group.

Fawthful looked over the breached castle, the retreating troops, the open corridors and the throne room being torn open around them. Then Fawthful described the future as if it had already been signed: Bowser's kingdom would become the first piece, the world would become the estate, and the name on the throne would eventually be the name people prayed to.

**“Ruler first,”** Fawthful said. **“God after.”**

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

Mimbus stood beside the claim. The dragon lowered its head behind them. Bowser answered with fire, not because the fire could close the breach, but because the alternative was letting the invader mistake evacuation for surrender.

The flames filled the broken gate. Fawthful did not step back.

The throne room was breached. The castle’s troops were moving. The switch remained untouched. The battle was not over.

## The Dragon Changed the Geometry

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

The dragon was not merely a stronger soldier at the gate. It changed which spaces counted as safe. A wall that had protected the courtyard became a source of falling stone. A straight line toward the barracks became a path through a creature’s reach. The defenders could not meet the dragon on the terms the dragon offered, and Bowser’s first useful command was therefore a refusal to let the garrison perform bravery in the most convenient place for the attacker.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

The retreat order is short because the order is a map. Goombas moved wounded troops under the gatehouse and through the spaces the dragon’s head could not occupy. Koopas locked shells into a barrier, not to defeat the dragon, but to make one more body-length of time. Magikoopas spent teleportation on living defenders and equipment that mattered to the evacuation. None of these actions looks like a heroic charge when separated from the whole. Together they kept the assault from becoming an immediate collapse.

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

Bowser’s fire breath did not end the dragon. It did something more practical: it forced the attacker to react while the smaller bodies moved. The ground pound did the same on the ground. Stone broke, dust rose, and the courtyard became harder for a large enemy to read. The king was not trying to make the battlefield beautiful. He was buying a route through it.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

## The Order That Saved the Line

The most important sentence in the retreat order is the first one: pull back from the dragon. It rejects the instinct to hold the wall because the wall is there. A compromised castle creates a dangerous loyalty test. Soldiers want to prove that they will not abandon their post, commanders want to prove that the fortress is still theirs, and an attacker wants both impulses to remain fixed long enough for the dragon to do the work.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

Bowser’s order breaks that test. The line is allowed to move. Koopas protect the withdrawal, Goombas carry the wounded, and the Magikoopas move people rather than wasting their limited teleportation on objects that can be replaced. A Hammer Bro retreats when the wall becomes a ceiling. The filing records that departure without turning it into betrayal: knowing where the floor is can be a form of discipline when the alternative is being buried under the command to stand still.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

The loyalists do not leave because they have stopped caring about the castle. They leave because the evacuation route is the part of the castle that can still be made to answer. The order converts a lost outer wall into a chance to keep the interior from becoming a mass grave.

## Traitors, Corridors, and the Breach

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

sections.heading: The Command Room Has A Route, A Dragon, And A Switch Nobody Trusts
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

The assault has two forces moving at once. The dragon and the visible troops break the outside. Traitors and compromised routes make the inside unreliable. Goombas and Koopas therefore fight two battles: one against the attackers in front of them and another against the uncertainty behind the next door. A corridor can be a shelter, a trap, or an evacuation lane depending on who reached it first.

That is why the Magikoopa teleportation matters beyond spectacle. Every moved defender is a person removed from a corridor that may already belong to the traitors. Every wounded soldier carried under the gatehouse is a witness who can later say which route opened and which order was obeyed. The evacuation does not restore the chain of command, but it keeps enough of the chain alive to make the investigation possible.

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

When the wall gives way, the breach is real and the castle is not surrendered. Fawthful’s forces reach the inner routes, but the operation has not yet become a settled government. Bowser’s troops have been pulled toward survival, the Hammer Bro has withdrawn with the surviving line, and the self-destruct control remains untouched because nobody can prove which red toggle does what.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

## The Switch Nobody Trusted

The self-destruct-switch gag is funny only because the timing is terrible. The plate says SELF-DESTRUCT. It also says not to use the switch for lighting. Then it adds that one of the two identical red toggles may in fact be the lighting. A castle under assault does not need a philosophical problem above its evacuation controls. It needs a confirmed control and a person authorised to use it.

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

Bowser leaves both toggles alone. That choice is not cowardice and not indecision in the simple sense. A wrong press could kill the troops he is trying to move, destroy evidence of the internal compromise, or hand the attackers a ruin they could claim as a victory. The switch remains a live question because the label cannot tell the truth consistently enough to justify a hand on it.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

The plate is consequently filed as an exhibit rather than a punchline. It shows the state of command at the exact moment the castle needs command most: a royal fortress with a dragon at the wall, a split garrison, and an emergency control whose warning label has become another source of uncertainty.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

## Fawthful and Mimbus at the Broken Wall

The confrontation after the breach is not a clean victory speech. Fawthful and Mimbus appear where the castle’s physical damage and political damage meet. Bowser has not been removed from the throne by a formal vote, but the attackers are speaking as though occupation and legitimacy can be made identical by standing in the right room.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

Fawthful’s ruler-then-god plan gives the assault its scale. The castle is not the final prize. It is the first seat, the proof that a throne can be taken, held, and converted into an argument for worship. Mimbus’s presence keeps the earlier deception attached to the later claim. The false heir was not an isolated performance, and the dragon was not an isolated siege weapon. They were parts of one attempt to make the castle consent after its king had stopped consenting.

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

Bowser answers from the breach rather than from a secure throne room. That is the important image in the historical record. He is still the ruler of the castle in the sense that matters to the defenders, but he is defending a place that no longer behaves as a single body. The battle ends its recovered section with the plan exposed, not completed.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

## Limits of the Recovered Record

sections.heading: The Wall Gives Way And The Claim Arrives With It
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

The archive does not have a complete traitor list, a confirmed identity for every attacker, or an exact hour for either filing. It does have the retreat order, the altered route sheet, the switch label, the sequence from false heir to breach, and the ruler-then-god statement. Those pieces support a careful conclusion: the castle was compromised from inside, the evacuation was deliberate, and Fawthful’s campaign was aimed at succession before divinity.

The current 1040 BF record places Bowser elsewhere, operating in the Shadow Estate. This article is therefore a historical reconstruction of the 1035 BF assault, not a report that the dragon is currently at Bowser’s wall.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

## Recovered Scene: The Castle After the False Heir

The assault record begins after the false Bowser Jr. session, not before it. The fake heir had been used to infiltrate Bowser’s throne room; this was the same room where Fawthful was already standing when the defenders understood that the castle had become a battlefield. The room was not merely occupied in the abstract. The throne, the window, the command routes, and the king’s own soldiers were all inside the fight. A Hammer Bro kept throwing hammers because that was the order he had been given. Another voice warned that there were too many attackers to count.

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

“Are you sure?” Bowser asked, looking past the hammer flight toward Mimbus.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

The answer came from the window.

The dragon broke through the throne-room window, scattering glass and black stone across the hall. Bowser answered with a ground pound that shook the floor under everyone’s feet, then filled the broken opening with fire breath. The impact did not defeat the dragon. It gave the defenders a second in which to move, and Bowser used that second to run straight at Mimbus.

Fawthful stood between the broken window and the throne-room route. “Your castle falls soon. It belongs to us.”

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

“Over my dead Koopa shell,” Bowser said. “You are not taking my place without my permission. If I am not the Koopa King, no one is. This is my castle.”

Then Bowser turned away from the argument and shouted to the garrison.

“Get out of here! The dragon is coming! I do not want you getting smooshed!”

That order is the centre of the recovered battle. Bowser was still fighting for the castle, but he was no longer asking every defender to prove loyalty by standing in front of the dragon. He wanted the troops alive enough to be troops somewhere else.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

## The Magikoopa Method

The Magikoopas made the evacuation stranger and faster. They teleported Goombas around Mimbus so the small soldiers could flank the compromised route. One Goomba asked whether they were afraid. Goombas, after all, were always being stepped on by Mario.

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

“Nah,” the Goomba said. “It is just some dragons.”

At the window, a Hammer Bro protested that Bowser had ordered him to stay.

“I retract the order now,” Bowser told him. “Move.”

The Magikoopas began turning Goombas into blocks and tossing the blocks away from the line of attack. The defenders objected to the sight of their own troops being converted into masonry.

“We are transporting them,” a Magikoopa explained. “It is safer this way.”

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

The explanation did not make the method look safer. A flanking Goomba refused to cooperate. A hypnotised Koopa jumped for a flying brick and failed to catch it. Another Magikoopa, still loyal to Bowser, shouted that they might take the castle but they would not take their boss. The Magikoopas hovered, laughed at the confusion, and retreated with the people they could carry.

The evacuation was not clean. It was a series of bodies, blocks, teleports, and shouted corrections that kept the dragon from getting one uninterrupted target. That mattered more than dignity.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

## Mimbus, Cackletta, and the Claim

sections.heading: A Self-Destruct Switch Is Not A Strategy Just Because It Has A Label
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

Bowser swiped at Mimbus. Mimbus fell. The king looked at the breach and called for a retreat.

“What do you mean? We got this!” a Goomba protested.

“Have you ever fought a dragon before?” Bowser asked.

The Goomba had not.

Fawthful laughed, then sucked Cackletta into the vacuum apparatus as though removing a dangerous guest from a room. Fawthful climbed onto a hoverpad and rose above the broken floor.

“When people come to the castle, they will see me as the king,” Fawthful said. “I will be this world’s god.”

Waluigi's archival objection is simple: do NOT confuse occupation with surrender. The record does not make that mistake, WAH.

Fawthful claimed that half the castle had already been infiltrated and that Peach’s Castle was already under control. Bowser demanded to know why a bean wanted his castle.

“Power,” Fawthful answered. “I control the capital. You do not. I control the big Bowser Castle. You do not. Simple.”

Bowser’s answer was not reverent. It was administrative. Fawthful was not a king. Fawthful was renting a title without permission, and Bowser intended to take it back. Fawthful threatened to suck him up too.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

The dragon struck the throne-room wall again.

“OWW! My head!”

The wall did not break. Fawthful stared at the dragon and demanded to know what kind of incompetent dragon had been supplied for the operation. The dragon tried to explain. Fawthful answered with the only management principle Fawthful seemed to possess: there would be consequences.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

## The Retreat Through the Broken Castle

The remaining Hammer Bros began to retreat while they argued about the order. The hostile Koopas threw spears at them. One damaged a Koopa badly enough to make the difference between an orderly withdrawal and a rout visible to everyone in the courtyard.

“Do not kill them,” Bowser said. “They have caused me too much trouble to deal with. We are taking out the trash for now.”

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

The loyal Koopa troops paired their tactics. Shell barriers created a lane. Goombas pulled at legs and belts. The hypnotised soldiers were defeated by coordination rather than by one heroic strike. One Goomba tried to convince another that returning with him was better than being crushed alone.

“You will listen to me. I am the boss.”

The Goomba ran anyway.

The injured betrayer Koopas attempted to retreat with the rest. Bowser stopped them at the edge of the route.

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

“You cannot come.”

“Why?”

“You are traitors. You are lucky I am not killing you where I stand.”

The throne-room wall burst open before the argument could become a sentence. The dragon came through at last, wings sweeping the two traitors off the building. Bowser bolted into a side room with two Hammer Bros under his arms, carrying them the way a king carries equipment that has become unexpectedly alive.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

The Hammer Bros gave their names as Fred and Ed. They had a question for him. Did the castle have a self-destruct switch? If the dragon was going to take the fortress, perhaps they could blow it up and move the survivors toward Neo Bowser City.

Bowser stopped.

“You want me to blow up my own castle?”

The Hammer Bros tried to explain that Mario had once pressed a switch and collapsed a castle. Bowser had not built that switch. If there had been one here, perhaps somebody had sabotaged it. The argument drifted toward the axe at the end of the river and the general problem of old castles containing controls nobody remembered installing.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

Bowser rejected the plan. He wanted to leave before the dragon chomped them, but he also wanted Peach’s Castle checked and every survivor accounted for.

“Not just you imbeciles,” he clarified. “Everyone.”

## The Hag and the Switch

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

Bowser ran into a hag at exactly the wrong moment. She had made a self-destruct switch and was pleased to present it.

“Who hired you?” Bowser asked.

sections.heading: Sir Frankfurt Gives The Dragon A Family History And Then Leaves The Building
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

“A green bean,” she said.

Bowser informed her that the castle was under siege and her duties had been relinquished. He asked what the switch controlled.

“I could have sworn it was the door,” she said.

Bowser pushed past her.

The switch therefore remained the same kind of exhibit as the earlier label promised: something that looked like a solution while making the evacuation more dangerous. Nobody could prove whether it destroyed the castle, opened a door, or merely added another joke to a room already full of them.

Waluigi counts the bodies that get a route instead of a speech. THIS is the useful kind of courage, and Waluigi is filing it, WAH.

Outside, the dragon jumped on a brave Goomba and played with it until the play stopped being survivable. A small tear fell from one of the departing Magikoopas. The Magikoopas flew toward Neo Bowser City to carry the message that the castle had been breached and that the surviving force was retreating.

## Sir Frankfurt and the Dragon’s Question

The dragon grew bored of the Goomba and turned its head toward another room. A Hammer Bro was still there, stiff with fear.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

The dragon asked where Bowser was. The Hammer Bro answered that he was not the target. He was only guarding the room because Bowser had ordered him to stay, and then Bowser had retracted that order too late for the Hammer Bro to know where safety had gone.

The dragon admitted that it had been sent to kill Bowser in Draconic. The Hammer Bro answered in the same language that, since he was not the target, perhaps he could be released. The dragon considered the request. It had a bargain with the bean, but that did not mean it liked the bean. If the Hammer Bro could become useful to Bowser, that might be a better use of the dragon’s time than killing him.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

The Hammer Bro did not want to die. He wanted to elevate Bowser’s kingdom. He said that Bowser had raised him when nobody else would. The dragon asked his name.

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

The Hammer Bro introduced himself as Sir Frankfurt, the fourteenth—or the fiftieth, depending on which part of the family count he reached first—and the tenth child of twenty-four. His father had charged Mario and died before the third world was over. His mother had died of grief a few days later. Bowser had taken in the surviving children. Bowser could be harsh, Sir Frankfurt said, but he had done right by them.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

The dragon had heard enough family history. It called the speech nonsense and began to suck the Koopa into its vacuum. Sir Frankfurt grabbed the intake, curled into his shell, and spun. The shell struck the machine, vaulted upward, overshot the landing, and fell from the fifty-foot castle into the unknown.

The dragon looked after him, more shocked by the story than by the escape.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

## The Army That Was Not Bowser’s

Elsewhere, a Goomba who had been watching the dragon talk to the Hammer Bro ran. He reached the route toward Toad Town Station, where the surviving force began making plans without the king.

There were nine Goombas and two Koopas. There were no magic users. One proposal was to raid Toad Town and turn it into Neo Bowser Town. Another was to go to Shy Guy Falls, because Shy Guys might be on Bowser’s side. A third involved stopping at Cheeseland for food because one of the Goombas liked cheese. The route was less an army plan than a frightened argument held over an empty train track.

Waluigi marks this as the part where command becomes route planning. THIS is what keeping people alive looks like, WAH.

“What if Mario comes and steps on us?” one Goomba asked.

Nobody knew where Mario was. Since Peach had died, the answer had always been that Mario was moving, missing, or both.

Waluigi would like the file to acknowledge that a labelled switch is NOT a plan. Waluigi acknowledges the joke and fears the wiring, WAH.

sections.heading: Nine Goombas, Two Koopas, And The Question Of Who Is The Boss Now
sections.body:
Waluigi opens this cut by insisting on THIS sequence before the jokes. Waluigi is insisting because the order matters. Waluigi files the sequence before the punchline. WAH.

A small Fawthful drone appeared in the next room. The group had sent someone to tell Bowser that they had survived the dragon. The messenger had not returned. The drone had.

Then the other boss arrived: Koopa Killer Killa. The Goomba objected that Killa was not Bowser. Killa answered that Killa was the boss. Nobody had appointed Killa, but the empty space left by a retreating king was apparently enough to encourage the claim.

The group settled on Toad Town, then Shy Guy Falls, then Toad Town again, with the final decision depending on which sentence had been heard last. Everyone climbed toward the empty track.

Waluigi interrupts again because apparently everyone else is busy fighting a dragon: the story is NOT one charge, but a chain of choices, WAH.

A Hammer Bro remained behind the door because Bowser had ordered him to guard it. Killa demanded to know why he was still there. The Hammer Bro answered with the only command he still trusted: no one left behind. The Goomba said he would take his chances. The Hammer Bro stayed.

Waluigi's final margin note: the castle stops being one place before the record stops moving. THAT is the whole problem, WAH.

The Goomba walked toward the Fawthful drone. The fight began there, with the surviving army divided between a retreat it could not explain, a boss it had not chosen, and a machine that had been waiting for somebody to come close enough to attack.

## What This Scene Adds to the File

The assault was not one clean charge from the outside. It began with the fake Bowser Jr. infiltration of the throne room and continued when the dragon broke into that same room. It was a chain of bad choices, loyal corrections, frightened improvisations, and competing definitions of who the boss was. Bowser’s retreat order saved bodies. The Magikoopas’ block transport made survival look ridiculous. The traitors were stopped but not erased. The Hammer Bros carried their own names into the evacuation. Sir Frankfurt’s story made the dragon hesitate, and the Fawthful drone found a remnant force that no longer knew which destination belonged to the king.

Waluigi interrupts: THIS is not a graceful retreat; Waluigi files it as survival with the furniture still falling, WAH.

Waluigi's note: the record says MOVE, not pose heroically. Waluigi approves of the distinction, which is NOT a small one, WAH.

The historical record therefore ends on movement rather than victory. Bowser is trying to preserve the people and the castle’s future. Fawthful is trying to turn occupation into kingship and kingship into godhood. The dragon is following a contract it does not respect. The surviving Goombas and Koopas are trying to choose a route. The exact hour is unrecorded, but the sequence is clear: the false heir opened the inside, the dragon broke the outside, and the retreat exposed the people who would keep fighting after the castle stopped being one place.

Waluigi is watching the geometry change and Waluigi is telling you: a wall is NOT safety when a dragon has entered the room, WAH.

commentaries.title: The Cut and the Puppet Master
commentaries.subtitle: In Which The Building Meets The One Word It Cannot Argue With, And Waluigi Meets The Man Holding The Off Switch
commentaries.standfirst: The sequel to the promo account arrived the same night it was corrected, because this studio does not close. A coffee machine that was not an exit, a brother found alive at a blue light, a villain who fights to the music, one word that stops the whole building, applause for an empty room — and, at the end of a dark hallway, a small wired remote. Waluigi is going to talk through every second of it. He has NOT slept. WAH.
commentaries.pullQuote: The applause was for NOBODY. The show is not over. Somebody is holding the off switch.
commentaries.filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — the teaser, the correction, and the sequel, all in one day, because this file does not respect mealtimes

sections.heading: The Sequel Arrives The Same Night, Because This Studio Has Never Heard Of A Credits Roll
sections.body:
Some context first, filed gently, because Waluigi has learned things about this building in the last twelve hours and NONE of them are calming.

This morning Waluigi filed a newspaper clipping as a review. This evening the full account arrived, proved the clipping was a trailer, and Waluigi filed the correction with his teeth gritted and a promise in print that the archive would not let that happen twice. And then the SAME EVENING produced a sequel. Not the next day. Not after a rest. The new account picks up in the break room minutes after the old one ended, which means somewhere in that world a television studio looked at two shell-shocked nobles, one missing plumber, and a producer shaped like a Wario, and said: MORE. Waluigi has been in this business long enough to know what MORE means. It means a sequel, and it means Waluigi works tonight.

So here is the commentary track for the sequel, and Waluigi is going to talk through ALL of it, because the parts that look like an escape story are actually a management chart wearing an escape story as a costume, and somebody in this archive has to say so in a loud voice. That somebody is Waluigi. It is always Waluigi. I have checked the roster and there is nobody else on it.

Where we left them: Lord Darian Marsh of the Dark Shores and his steward, Alistair of the Marshkeepers, sealed in the employee break room of the *Nintendo Mania* studio. Four monitors showing static. One monitor showing a lie. The coffee machine gone cold. And through the walls, the sound of a corrupted Mario beating the real one somewhere out in the corridors — which is the single worst piece of ambient noise Waluigi has filed all year, and Waluigi once filed an event with SCREAMING FURNITURE.

How do we get out of here, though. We have no other leads but this place. That is the sentence the account opens on, and Waluigi wants it on the record that the lord of the Dark Shores said LEADS, plural, about a coffee machine and five monitors, and he was CORRECT, because in this building a coffee machine is a lead. Alistair surveyed the room like the steward he is — back door to the kitchen, air vent big enough to crawl through, monitors showing possible exits — and then found the thing that was new.

A small button by the coffee machine. Labelled EMERGENCY EXIT.

Waluigi has filed entire investigations that began with less. Hold that button in your mind. It is about to be the most honest and the most dishonest object in this whole filing, and it is both AT THE SAME TIME, which in this studio counts as a personality. Waluigi has met appliances with worse ethics.

sections.heading: The Button Said EXIT, The Machine Said Coffee, And The Ceiling Said You're Welcome
sections.body:
Darian pressed the button with, and the account is precise about this, the specific pessimism of a man testing whether the exit is another trap. *Brilliant, let's see how it's not an exit to the coffee machine.* Waluigi has read that sentence four times and respects it more with each pass. That is not cynicism. That is CALIBRATION. Two filings in this building will do that to a man, and Darian has had both of them in a single day.

The coffee machine came to life. Aggressively. Scalding coffee poured out uncontrollably, the room filled with steam, and Alistair coughed out the sentence *it's… not an exit* — and Waluigi is going to stop him right there, because the steward was WRONG, and being wrong in exactly the right direction is the theme of this entire session.

The steam rose. Steam does that. And a ceiling vent popped open from the heat.

Sit with the mechanics of it. The button did not open a door. The button made coffee. The coffee made steam. The steam opened the exit. The building hid an escape route behind an appliance, or the appliance staged a rescue, and Waluigi filed the line in the account and he stands behind every word of it: in this studio those are the same sentence with different fonts. The archive has a shelf now for lying exits. The shelf is getting FULL. Waluigi labeled the shelf himself, and the studio keeps stocking it.

Then the men armed themselves, and the armory was the break room, and Waluigi wants the arsenal read out slowly because it is the most provincial loadout ever carried into a television studio: Darian took a heavy metal rolling pin, and the broken coffee-pot handle with its sharp edge. A rolling pin. A SHARD OF COFFEE POT. Somewhere in the Dark Shores, Waluigi is certain, an armory master felt a disturbance and does not know why.

Alistair shut off the machine before they climbed — the steward turns OFF what the lord turns ON, which is either a marriage or a checks-and-balances system — Waluigi has worked in institutions, and that arrangement is called GOVERNANCE — — the steam cleared, and he boosted his lord up into the duct first.

The steward boosted the king. Waluigi wants that remembered. Not the other way round. The lord goes UP into the dark ceiling of an alien building first, on his steward's hands, holding a rolling pin. Waluigi has filed kings who would not carry their own map. This one goes into the duct FIRST, and the account does not even pause to be proud of it, which is how you know it is habit. Waluigi notices habits. Habits are character, filed under pressure.

sections.heading: The Exit Is Up, The Rat Is Honest, And The Steward Says The Sentence Of The Year
sections.body:
The vent was dark, dusty, cramped. Hands and knees. Faint emergency light from below, small cracks letting in glow. Something scurried past Darian's face.

A rat. An ordinary rat.

And Waluigi confesses he UNDERSTOOD the account at that moment, because the account says the rat was almost reassuring — after the black-eyed thing on Camera Three in the previous filing, an ordinary rat reads like a courtesy. This building has reset Waluigi's standards so thoroughly that VERMIN now scores as HOSPITALITY. Waluigi is filing that about himself honestly, because a commentator who cannot admit his benchmarks have moved is just a narrator with better fonts. The archive has standards. Waluigi simply cannot find them this week.

Then Darian fumbled for the rolling pin, and the metal clanged against the duct walls, and the clang became one long echo rolling through the entire system, and Waluigi would like the acoustics noted: the building heard EVERYTHING. Every duct is a microphone. Every crawl is a broadcast. The studio that lies about exits is perfectly honest about eavesdropping.

And Alistair whispered the sentence this archive would like bronzed and mounted over the door: *careful — noise might draw attention.*

The steward. Whispering. To the king. About noise. In a building where the walls applaud on command. It is the single most correct operational sentence spoken in this entire two-filing arc, and it was whispered by a man lying in a dust duct, and the archive has given it its own line in the notable features because Waluigi SAID SO. Careful. Noise might draw attention. The entire studio arc in seven words. Frame it — and when Waluigi says frame it, he means the archive will be checking the bronze budget at year's end. WAH.

Ahead of them: a faint blue light.

And here is where Waluigi tells you what a commentator does with a blue light, because the last filing taught us all what colored lights mean in this place. A blue light is not a blue light. A blue light is a plot, wearing a bulb. Waluigi has a whole taxonomy now, and every entry is a trap wearing a lamp. The account crawled toward it, and Waluigi crawled after it in spirit, and what was under the light is the single best thing anybody found in this building, and Waluigi includes the churro stick from the previous filing in that ranking. Only just. But he includes it.

sections.heading: Luigi Is Alive, Alone, And Doing MY Job Better Than ME
sections.body:
The vent opened over a maintenance room with a working computer screen, and below it someone was typing fast, muttering *come on… come ON…*

It was Luigi.

ALIVE. The account is exact and Waluigi is going to be exact right back: alive, alone, his face lit blue, exhausted but unharmed. The promo account ended with Luigi missing during a strange tape, and Waluigi filed that loss, and the correction kept it, and NOW — one ceiling vent later — the man is sitting at a terminal two rooms from the fight, running his own investigation.

Look at his desk, because the desk is the story. Security camera feeds. A map of the studio. And notes headed **Wario's corruption.**

Notes. On Wario. The brother of the most famous missing man in the world sat down inside the thing that took his brother and started building a FILE. He typed that he had to find Mario. He typed that he had to fix this. A scared brother running his own investigation with better tools than this archive has ever had, and nobody to tell. Waluigi has run this archive for years on less, and he is NOT proud of how the comparison comes out.

Waluigi has complicated feelings and he is going to file all of them. Pride: that is a MARSHKEEPER-grade work ethic and Luigi does not even work here. Envy: the archive has been chasing the Mario disappearance with newspaper clippings and a charred note, and Luigi walked in and got security feeds, a MAP, and a corruption file. Alarm: because the maintenance computer is the best evidence this case has ever been handed, and it is sitting in a building that RESETS ITS OWN ROOMS, which means the file is a candle in a house fire.

And caution — because the archive has already filed one Luigi that was not Luigi. The blue Luigi. The lava bridge. Waluigi has a whole shelf of things that wore a friendly face, and Darian — watching from the vent, shushing his own steward — said *let's see if he does anything rash; we don't know how dangerous he is.* That is the CORRECT instinct in this building and Waluigi has said so in ink and he will say it again here in a bigger font: VERIFY FIRST. Waluigi said it yesterday about a different brother. The ink is barely DRY. The man at the blue light zoomed cameras, checked door sensors, typed notes, seemed normal.

And then he grabbed a flashlight and stood up to leave. Hold that too. Everything in this filing is a held object that goes off later. Waluigi told you to hold it. He holds things for a living.

sections.heading: The Steward Stops The Kill Shot, Which Is Either Treason Or The Best Staff Work Of The Era
sections.body:
Luigi stood up to leave, and Darian went for the drop. Out of the vent, rolling pin coming down on the head of a man he had decided not to trust.

And Alistair's hand closed on his arm MID-SWING.

Stop the film right there, because Waluigi needs a moment with this. A steward grabbed his king's weapon arm. In the Dark Shores that is probably a hanging offense. In Waluigi's archive it is a PROMOTION. In this maintenance room it is the best decision anybody made all night, and Waluigi has a list, and the list includes ordering a V formation out loud like a general.

The steward stopped his own lord's kill shot on a HUNCH. And the hunch was right — and the account, which Waluigi salutes, also records that it was nearly fatal for everybody. Because Luigi turned, saw an armed stranger descending from his ceiling, and did exactly what a cornered man does. He dodged the second swing and put the flashlight into Darian's shoulder hard enough to numb it. Waluigi has taken a hit like that. It ends the argument.

Alistair shouted that they were not here to hurt him. Luigi was not listening. Full panic, ready to fight or flee or scream — and Waluigi notes, quietly, that this is the most REAL Luigi has ever looked in this entire arc. The copies are calm. The brother is terrified. The archive's whole verification crisis, resolved by a flashlight: terror is hard to fake and this building has never once bothered to try.

*WAH! Two minutes of surveillance undone by one rolling pin.* Waluigi wrote that in the margin of the account and he is keeping it there. Two minutes of perfect instinct — watch, verify, shush the steward — spent in one swing of kitchenware. And in the margin, right beside it, the archive's other margin note: the steward earns his keep TWICE in this filing, and the second time is not this.

The second time involves a window. And a flaming pipe. Waluigi is getting there. Do not rush me — the account did not rush, and the account is a machine for teaching patience, which is a strange quality in something that also turns fights into musical numbers.

sections.heading: The Door Comes Off Its Hinges, And A Man Reading A Seating Chart Walks In
sections.body:
The door went off its hinges.

Evil Mario stood in it — bruised, grinning, glowing red-eyed, fresh from beating the real Mario somewhere out in the corridors. And he looked around the room, and the account gives him the line, and Waluigi gives him the line again because it is the most revealing thing the copy ever said: *Innocence doesn't get you far.*

Innocence doesn't get you far. That is not a threat, Waluigi has heard threats, Waluigi has FILED threats. That is a POLICY STATEMENT. Waluigi has read policy statements before, and this one has MANAGEMENT written all over it. That is a man quoting the employee handbook of whatever this place is. Hold it — it comes back at the end of the filing with a whole different accent.

Three against one, Darian counted. *We can take him… I think.*

They could not. The account is honest about the arithmetic in a way Waluigi respects: Evil Mario moved like a special effect. Dodged the flashlight. Dodged the rolling pin. Shoved Alistair into a desk. Laughed the whole time — the account says he laughed the WHOLE time, and Waluigi believes it, because this thing has never once fought like it was in danger, and the end of this filing is going to explain exactly why. He hurled Luigi into a shelf by the collar.

What actually landed was Darian's rolling pin. A full swing. **CLANG.** Into the shoulder. The first honest hit anyone has put on this thing in two filings — two FILINGS, remember, fireballs and javelins and warhammers have all missed this copy — and the weapon that connects is BAKERY EQUIPMENT, wielded by a provincial lord, and Evil Mario grunted and stumbled back, and for one second the room believed. Waluigi believed too. The archive records its weak moments.

They pressed it. Luigi kicked his legs. Alistair, battered upright, called *GO FOR HIS FACE!* And Darian, somewhere in the noise, produced the sentence Waluigi will now have to live with:

**"A king cannot let his subjects fall!"**

The lord and his steward hit the corrupted Mario together and put him through the computer desk. Monitors shattered. And Waluigi will admit the lower-case truth under the capitals: it worked. The king who said his subjects could not fall, and the steward who catches arms mid-swing, put a special effect through a desk with their combined weight, and for one entire second, the filing believed with them.

sections.heading: The Cape Is The Power Source, And The Studio Has A Rescue Squad On Payroll
sections.body:
And then the floor began to shake, and Evil Mario started to laugh again, and standing up out of the wreckage, he wore a cape.

Not a costume cape. The account is specific and Waluigi is going to be specific with it: a cape of shadowy, pixelated feathers, moving unnaturally, like a living thing. And the shaking, the flickering lights, the cracking walls — the shaking was coming FROM it. The cape was the power source.

Waluigi wants that sentence studied. Not the man. The OUTFIT. Everything this filing has fought — two filings of a corrupted Mario who dodges like a special effect — and the engine of it was a garment. Luigi said it out loud, because Luigi has been reading the room correctly all night: his weakness, it has to be. Destroy the cape. Luigi said it and Waluigi seconded it from the future.

Then the floor fell in.

All three of them dropped into the collapse — and three paratroopas in studio uniforms, with parachutes, caught them by the arms out of the air. Studio crew. Parachute rigs. One of them yelled *HOLD ON TIGHT.*

*WAH!* Waluigi has QUESTIONS and he put every one of them in the investigation file, starting with: since when does a television studio keep a paratroopa rescue squad, and WHO WROTE THEM INTO THE BUDGET? Waluigi asked that out loud at his own desk. Nobody answered. Nobody ever answers. You cannot staff a rapid-deployment parachute team on the same books as a coffee machine that lies about being an exit. Unless — and Waluigi is just going to leave this on the table — unless the budget is not a budget, and the crew is not crew, and somebody further up the call sheet rents both by the hour.

Because look at what the squad did next. They did not fly the party out. There is no OUT in this building; the filing has established this with a coffee machine, and Waluigi checked the exits so you do not have to. There are NONE. They flew the party AT Evil Mario. A flying squad in formation, weapons drawn, non-lethal rounds aimed at the cape. *NEUTRALIZE THE THREAT.* The rescue and the attack were the same maneuver, rehearsed, on standby, deployed the moment the floor gave — which means somebody knew the floor would give, and had a choreographed response READY.

And then, with the squad in the air and the target painted, the studio turned the music on.

The studio. Turned the music. ON. Waluigi has been in show business adjacent circles his whole career and he has never once been handed a soundtrack in the middle of a rescue. Hold the beat, readers. The next section has a melody, and I am NOT going to apologize for it.

sections.heading: Plumber Man: The Copy Fights To The Beat Of A Song That Belongs To The Original
sections.body:
**Plumber Man.**

The song is filed in full in the songbook, lyrics exactly as sung, because what happened next cannot be filed without it, and Waluigi means that as a technical statement about EVIDENCE, not as a joke. The studio turned the music on, and Evil Mario began to fight to the beat.

Dodging on the downbeat. Backflips on the chorus. A villain in a feather cape dancing through a tranq barrage in perfect time, while the paratroopas — who train for many things, the account says, and Waluigi has MET some of them now — could not get their timing to land. The copy was not fighting. The copy was PERFORMING. The fight was a NUMBER. Waluigi has seen numbers; the account still calls it a fight, and Waluigi keeps the account's wording, because the account was THERE and Waluigi was not. The number had a soundtrack, and the soundtrack was provided by the venue, and the venue was aiming at its own performer, and NOTHING about that sentence chain is an accident. Waluigi has re-read that chain four times. It does not improve.

And then the song did the one thing the studio did not plan for: it found Luigi.

Luigi covered his ears. And then he STOPPED covering them. He knew the song. He hummed it — weakly, unwillingly, drawn to it — and the account reaches the conclusion the archive also reached, and Waluigi is going to reach it again, slowly, because it is the emotional center of this whole filing: **the song belongs to the real Mario.**

Read the lyrics the way Waluigi just read them. Four feet ten. The stache. The star that powers him. The pipes. The lass. The kingdom. It is a love song disguised as a jingle, and every word of it is TRUE about a man who is currently bleeding somewhere in this building's corridors — and the corrupted copy of that man was using it as a WEAPON, in front of that man's brother, who could not stop humming along. Waluigi cannot hear this song now without filing a complaint about it.

The studio did not just steal a fight. It stole the fight's MEANING and played it back with the moral removed. Waluigi has heard of sampling. This is DESECRATION with a drum track.

At the final note, Mario appeared behind him. Bruised. Hat askew. Crawled out of the wreckage on his own — nobody rescued him either, notice, the rescue squad had OTHER ORDERS. The paratroopas gasped *Sir, you're alive.* Luigi nearly wept. And the real and the corrupted stood face to face while the song faded, and Waluigi will tell you what that staging is, because staging is the word this whole filing has been teaching us: it is a LIGHTING CUE. The hero enters on the final note. Somebody scored the reveal.

sections.heading: A King Orders A V Formation, A Brother Takes The Cape, And A Steward Comes Back Stupid
sections.body:
Four against one now — *still not scared,* Evil Mario said, and cracked his neck, and the fight resumed. Darian ordered the charge — and Evil Mario STOPPED. Mid-motion. Head tilted, eyes flickering like a screen losing signal, the cape's dark feathers starting to fray. A gust came off it that knocked papers, equipment, and finally Alistair — Alistair, who whispered the sentence of the year about noise — clean off his feet and away down a dark hallway like a ragdoll. Waluigi filed a steward MISSING at that point in the account. The filing was premature. It usually is, with Alistair.

The paratroopas caught Luigi and Darian by the arms and anchored to a broken pipe. And then the statue came back to life and hit the real Mario across the face hard enough to put him through a wall, and it was clear the fight was lost.

Until the lord of the Dark Shores remembered what he is FOR.

**"As a king, I order the troops into formation — a V, like a bird."**

Waluigi has read a great many battlefield orders in this archive. A provincial king, standing in a collapsing studio, ordering a paratroopa parachute squadron into a V formation like migratory birds, is now Waluigi's favorite, and the competition includes a centaur declaring a legal argument against the Iron Legion. The squad SNAPPED into the V. The V cut the wind. And on the next order — *grab Luigi, fly him into that cape* — the lead paratroopa took Luigi into the formation's dive, straight at the fraying feathers.

And Luigi — who came to this studio to find his brother, who hummed his brother's song against his own will, who was thrown into a shelf by this thing not twenty minutes ago — reached out with BOTH HANDS and yanked the cape off.

Evil Mario screamed. And Waluigi notes — carefully, in the margin, underlined — that it is the first sound the copy made all night that Waluigi believes was NOT in the script.

The scream became a smile, because this thing has a costume rack, and the account knows it now: in his hand, a tanuki leaf. The transformation ran through him — fox tail, Wario's wild hair, and then, grotesque on his shoulder, a SECOND HEAD. Wario's. Grinning. Waluigi has filed haunted mirrors, vampire invitations, and a spider the size of a school, and a spare WARIO HEAD sprouting off a corrupted Mario's shoulder is still the single most upsetting accessory in the case file.

And through the broken window behind them came Alistair. Blown away minutes ago. Presumed lost. Crashing back in covered in dust, carrying a FLAMING PIPE, with visible rage, executing a plan his own lord described — accurately, in the account, in the lord's OWN WORDS — as *really stupid.* The Wario head popped off like a balloon and burst into smoke, as if it agreed with the assessment. The flaming pipe met the tanuki tail. The leaf caught fire. Mario tackled the thing off its feet, and Luigi snatched the burning leaf out of the air just as it fully ignited.

The steward earns his keep TWICE. Told you. Waluigi keeps score; it is what archivists do instead of sleeping. WAH.

sections.heading: Fire, Water, Ice — And Then A Provincial Lord Says The One Word The Building Obeys
sections.body:
The corrupted Mario ran out of forms to wear and put on the last one. He erupted into fire — no shape left, a living blaze, the room catching around him.

And Darian went for the fire alarm. Found one — red, smashed-glass, by the shattered door — and went for it through the heat ON HIS BELLY, because the flame whip was overhead, saying *it's too risky, but I must keep going.* Debris under his hands. The whip missing him by inches. He smashed the glass and pulled the handle.

Sprinklers. Water everywhere. The fire form hissed, shrank, flickered. And Darian looked at his hands — soot, scratches, small burns — and the account gives him one word of inventory: ALIVE.

And then Evil Mario pointed at the dying fire, and the room turned COLD. Frost climbed the walls. Breath turned visible. The sprinkler water became icicles, and the corrupted Mario stood remade as a body of shimmering blue ice with glowing eyes. The real Mario punched it and his fist froze STUCK in the surface. Waluigi has filed weapons that break. This is the first weapon that got a RECEIPT.

*How many forms does this thing have?* Darian said. And then answered himself: **this must be all an act.**

The ice sculpture smirked.

Which is how they knew he was right. Waluigi wants that beat preserved exactly as the account timed it, because it is the moment the entire two-filing arc changes genre: the monster is caught SMIRKING at its own review. Waluigi has been smirked at by professionals. This was a CURTAIN CALL. It is not a beast wearing shapes. It is a PERFORMER wearing forms, and a performer can be directed, and anything that can be directed has a director, and the room was about to meet him.

But first, the word. The filing exists for the word. Darian — burned, numb-shouldered, rolling pin in hand, standing in falling sprinkler water with the ice mid-advance — said:

**"CUT!"**

Everything stopped. Waluigi has checked the audio on that word. It is one syllable, and it beat ice. The ice stopped spreading. The paratroopas lowered their weapons mid-breath. The real Mario lowered his fists *like he just remembered something* — that phrase is the account's and Waluigi is keeping it, it is the best stage direction in the archive — and Evil Mario's frozen expression flickered, pixelated, broke apart like a bad signal. The word had reached whatever was running the show, and whatever was running the show FLINCHED.

Theatrical curtains came down from the whole ceiling. Crew voices. Someone shouting *cut the feed.* The curtains closed with a THUD, and when they opened again the studio had reset itself: the original break room, no flames, no ice, no evil copies. *What just happened?* Mario asked. Nobody had it.

Waluigi has re-shelved half of this file accordingly. The question is no longer how to beat Evil Mario. The question is WHO IS AFRAID OF THE WORD CUT, AND WHY. A trap cannot be embarrassed. A STAGE can. Waluigi moved this file from the TRAPS shelf to the THEATRE shelf tonight; the label maker is still warm.

sections.heading: The Applause Was For NOBODY, And Waluigi Cannot Put That Sentence Down
sections.body:
Wario walked in clapping, and applause came out of the dark.

*Bravo! What an entertaining performance!* Oscar-worthy, he said. The ice scene — brilliant special effects. And an audience that WAS NOT THERE roared approval while a television on the wall replayed the fight as security footage. He admitted ALL of it with his arms spread: *Best show on TV!* And then, the one true sentence a producer has ever said in this archive: some of you didn't sign up for it.

The real Mario asked the only question that mattered. *You used me? Like some kind of puppet?* And Wario waved it off as a bit of fun — and Waluigi notes the WAVE, because the wave is a man who has never once been asked to account for anything and has developed the reflexes of somebody who never will be.

And Darian — who has spent two filings, ONE DAY, learning to check this building's work — looked at the audience.

**Every seat was empty.**

Read it again. Waluigi has read it several times and it has not gotten lighter. He checks it every pass, like a tooth. Still not lighter. Beyond the seats, through the windows, the whole studio facility: silent. No crew. No life. Nobody. The applause was a RECORDING for a room of chairs. Waluigi has stood in empty rooms before. They at least had the decency to be QUIET about it. The show has an audience the way the coffee machine has an exit: on paper, in spirit, and NOT IN THE ROOM.

*We're alone,* Mario said. And Wario's smirk finally faltered — and four men who had just survived his variety hour began to close on him with their sleeves rolled.

The empty seats are the part Waluigi cannot file yet, and he told you so in the assessment and he will tell you again on the track: a show needs an audience. The applause track says one exists. The room says it does not. Either the audience is somewhere the windows do not show, or the performance is being recorded for a viewer the building is not prepared to name. BOTH readings have a person at the end of them. And Waluigi has a name he is not writing down until he has to.

He is not writing it down. He is, however, writing down the sleeve-rolling, because four survivors squaring up at their producer is the most honest television this studio has produced all day. Waluigi would watch THAT show. He would rate it highly.

sections.heading: The Man Wario Bows To, And The Small Wired Thing That Runs Everything
sections.body:
They never got to him. A voice behind them said, *since this was all for show, let's see how you like the real deal* — and there stood a figure in a director's cap, holding a script.

And Wario — the showman, the Apparition, the boss of everyone visible, the man who just called this the best show on TV — went PALE. And BOWED. And said: *Boss.* One word. Waluigi has filed confessions longer than that syllable, and none of them were more total.

**Director Mario.** Waluigi is filing that name exactly as the account gives it, cold, calculating, no warmth in him anywhere, and the account's own ledger of the last hour snaps into focus like a focus pull, which is what it was ALL ALONG: the corrupted Mario was an ACTOR. The song was a NUMBER. Wario was the PRODUCER. And the applause, the exits, the reset break room — that was the VENUE, and venues have owners. Waluigi has been asking who profits since the newspaper clipping, and the profit wears a CAP now.

The Director said the show had gone over better than Wario knew. He knew about the results. And then he said the quiet part with his cigar snapping in half in his fingers, and the account censors it and Waluigi will censor it too, because this is a family archive: *you tried to f*** me.*

He took Wario by the collar and put him through a wall hard enough to shake the building. *You betrayed me — you ruined MY show.* One punch, and Wario was unconscious. And then the detail Waluigi files above even the wall: he straightened his SUIT. Like a man who has swatted a fly. He looked once at Darian, Alistair, Luigi, and the real Mario — UNREADABLY — and walked out without a word. Waluigi has met that silence once or twice. It is the silence of a man who does not rate the meeting.

But the account has one more reel, and it is the reel the whole case turns on. Darian — ALONE — noticed that Evil Mario was still there. Half in shadow. Perfectly still. Red eyes tracking the Director to the door. He told NOBODY. He signalled Alistair. He let the room arrive at its own stillness around the thing in the corner. And Evil Mario smiled, slowly, and raised ONE FINGER, and pointed — not at any of them — at the door the Director had left through.

The actor pointed at the man who directs him. Waluigi has waited two filings for a witness to point at SOMETHING. Remember when Waluigi said the *innocence* line was a policy statement? The policy has a SIGNATORY.

Darian stepped into the dim hallway and hid in a dark alcove, and the Director walked past him close enough to TOUCH. In one hand: a folder. In the other, carried with the ease of long habit, a small remote device with buttons and wires running from it. A control unit. For Evil Mario — or for the whole studio. Waluigi has wanted an OBJECT for this case since a charred note on a doorstep. The case finally HAS one.

The account ends on the thought the archive now cannot put down: that remote could be the key to stopping everything — if they can get it.

The recommendation, one more time, from the commentary desk: the REMOTE, before the Director notices it was seen. And somebody collect Luigi's notes on the way out. The show is not over. Somebody is holding the off switch.

WAH.

commentaries.title: The Rot-Zone at Star Hill: A Fired Pilot, a Roof That Was Not a Landing Pad, the Man With Too Many Hands, and the Notebook That Left in a Courier's Satchel
commentaries.subtitle: In Which Waluigi Screens The Flight Recorder, Reclaims The Grimoire, And Witnesses A Courier Dismiss Thirty Years Of Fraternal Tragedy
commentaries.filed: 3 Aethel, 1035 BF — recorded live at the workshop projector
commentaries.pullQuote: He called a courier with a black-powder pistol Mario! And Paulo told him his brother sounded like an absolute bastard!
commentaries.standfirst: Waluigi has loaded the twin reels of the Star Hill flight recorder and street survey onto the 16mm workshop projector. Down in the third row, nobody is permitted to leave until Waluigi establishes that Wario fired our licensed pilot at four thousand feet, that the roof was never a certified landing zone, and that the terrifying green horror in the street addressed a foul-mouthed courier as Mario before stealing Waluigi's leather-bound intellectual property.

sections.heading: ROLL THE REEL — The Rotors Came Up Through Waluigi's Boots And The Cockpit Had The Wrong Man In It
sections.body:
Roll the reel! Right there — start track one on the soundhead! Waluigi has the projector focused directly on the white workshop brick, and Waluigi wants every person sitting on these three folding chairs to look at the screen before anyone asks another foolish question about why our transport helicopter is currently a twisted pile of smoking scrap behind the clinic! Look at the timestamp! Look at the counter on the dial! Two weeks of quiet at the outpost, one signed agreement on the mahogany desk, and thirty seconds later Waluigi is airborne in a five-ton twin-turbine iron bird with the side cargo hatch completely unlatched and a freezing mountain gale whistling through Waluigi's mustache! 

Look at the cockpit camera mounted behind the cargo bench! Waluigi is sitting there, perfectly respectable, minding Waluigi's own business, holding a brand-new leather notebook with both hands like a true scholar of the realm! And then — BAM! Watch the whole frame shudder! The aircraft drops thirty feet into an empty air pocket in half a heartbeat! Waluigi hits the iron bulkhead so hard Waluigi's molars click together! Hear that on the cabin microphone? That is Waluigi screaming at the absolute top of Waluigi's lungs: *"WAH! What are you doing?"* Waluigi scrambles forward on hands and knees across the rattling floor plates, slams a purple fist against the pilot's high-backed steel seat, and expects to see a licensed professional with headphones, an altimeter, and a steady pulse! 

And who is in the chair? Freeze the frame right there! LOOK AT THAT HEAD! That is not an aviator! That is Wario! Wario in a sweaty purple tunic, wrestling two heavy control levers like he is trying to strangle a grease-bear in an alleyway! And look at his mouth on the audio playback! He turns his face around, his jaw turns the colour of an overripe eggplant, and he roars directly into the cockpit microphone: *"I'M FLYING, YOU STRING BEAN!"* Then one thick yellow glove clamps onto Waluigi's shoulder to hold Waluigi upright, and he bellows: *"DON'T TOUCH THE CONTROLS! THAT PILOT IS ON MY TAB, AND I DON'T PAY FOR BROKEN EQUIPMENT!"* 

Broken equipment! Waluigi wants everyone in this room to appreciate this moment! We are four hundred feet in the air over black limestone gorges, travelling at ninety miles an hour in freezing darkness, and the man with his heavy workboots on the directional rudder does not know how to fly a kite, let alone a multi-ton troop transport! He does not have a licence, he does not have a compass, and his entire aeronautical philosophy is based on shouting at the instrument dials!

sections.heading: 'THE PILOT WAS A LIABILITY! HE ASKED FOR A RAISE, SO I FIRED HIM!' — The Pictures In The Manual
sections.body:
Watch the secondary camera mounted inside the cargo hold! Waluigi stumbles backward against the shuddering ammunition crates, scanning the webbing and the vibrating airframe for anyone who actually attended flight school! Nobody! Waluigi has to yell at the top of Waluigi's lungs over the deafening whine of the turbine engines: *"Where did the actual pilot go?"* And without even turning his neck away from the windscreen, Wario barks into the rushing wind: *"THE PILOT WAS A LIABILITY! HE ASKED FOR A RAISE, SO I FIRED HIM!"* 

Look at Waluigi's face on the footage! That is the expression of an educated man discovering his business associate has terminated the contract of an aeronautical navigator while cruising through the stratosphere! Wario keeps right on roaring: *"NOW I'M THE CAPTAIN, AND THE CAPTAIN DOESN'T TAKE ORDERS FROM THE CARGO!"* Waluigi grabs an overhead cable, swaying wildly as the deck pitches, and shouts: *"He was on the plane midair — what-a do you mean?"* And Wario bellows through the engine noise: *"HE'S IN THE REAR HOLD! I PUT HIM THERE FOR ‘CONSULTATION’! HE'LL BE FINE — OR HE'LL GET A VERY LOUD SEAT FOR THE NEXT TWO HOURS! EITHER WAY, HE'S OFF MY BALANCE SHEET!"* 

Off his balance sheet! He latched the only trained aviator on the payroll inside a steel freight locker behind the main fuel cells because the man requested a standard hazard stipend! And when Waluigi asks how Wario proposes to keep five tons of screaming iron aloft without stalling, Wario wrenches a heavy hydraulic lever, tilts the cabin until loose cargo slides across the floor, and roars: *"I DON'T NEED TO KNOW HOW, I JUST KNOW IT WORKS!
