I STUDIED THE MANUAL! WELL — I STOLE THE MANUAL AND READ THE PARTS WITH PICTURES! IT'S ALL ABOUT MOMENTUM, AND I HAVE A LOT OF MOMENTUM!"* 

Momentum! He stole the technical maintenance binder and looked only at the coloured illustrations! Waluigi has watched this man order dinner by pointing at the drawings on the menu, and now he is navigating mountain peaks by the same intellectual method! Look at Wario on the footage, stabbing a greasy yellow thumb at a diagram of the hydraulic pitch control and insisting it was an acceleration button! The pilot who had read the words was locked in the dark, and the man who had admired the sketches was holding the stick while our lives hung by a thread!

sections.heading: 'THAT IS LUIGI IN THE STREET!' — Four Hundred Feet Above A Cobblestone Mistake
sections.body:
Advance the film thirty feet! Waluigi pulls the seat harness across Waluigi's chest until the iron buckle bites through Waluigi's purple work clothes. Waluigi shouts over the rotor deafening din: *"You better be sure about this."* And what does our grand captain bark back? *"BETTER IS FOR PEOPLE WHO DON'T OWN THE MAP! I DON'T GUESS, I CALCULATE! AND MY CALCULATION SAYS WE LAND ON THAT ROOF OR WE DON'T LAND AT ALL — NO REFUNDS!"* He slaps an emergency toggle on the dashboard, warning lamps start strobing across the canopy, and he yells: *"HOLD YOUR BREATH THEN, STRINGS-BEAN, IT SAVES THE OXYGEN FOR THE PROFIT! WATCH THE GEARS DROP! WARIO SEES THE LANDING ZONE, AND THE LANDING ZONE OWES ME A FEE!"* 

Look through the open cargo hatch! Down between the streetlamps of Star Hill, Waluigi spots a figure standing on the cracked pavement four hundred feet below. Overalls and a cap, bright lime green in the swirling mist! Not Luigi's green — Waluigi knew from the air that the shade was sickly and synthetic, like cheap dye brewed in a copper vat — but Waluigi points a long purple finger out into the freezing gale and screams: *"THAT IS LUIGI IN THE STREET! HE IS STANDING THERE!"* And Wario's eyes bulge against the windscreen like two greasy brass door knobs! *"THAT'S NOT A LANDING ZONE, THAT'S A PAYDAY! HE LOOKS LIKE HE'S WAITING FOR SOMETHING — PROBABLY THE BILL I'M ABOUT TO SEND HIM!"* 

Then a second figure steps out of the shadow into the lantern glow, carrying a heavy leather courier satchel and wearing thick workboots, completely unconcerned by the screaming rotors above. Waluigi shouts: *"WAH! Who is that?"* And Wario wrenches the stick hard to the left, sending the airframe into a violent side-slip that pushes Waluigi's stomach up behind Waluigi's teeth! *"THAT'S A DISTRACTION! A DEBT COLLECTOR IN DISGUISE! I DON'T CARE WHO HE IS. IF HE'S TALKING TO THE GREEN ONE, HE'S INTERFERING WITH MY ACQUISITION!"* Acquisition! The man was preparing to crash a multi-ton helicopter into a municipal thoroughfare, demolish private storefronts, and invoice the streetlamps for hazard disruption!

sections.heading: 'WHO'S THAT MAN YOU SEE WHO GROOMS HIS 'STACHE SO WELL?' — A Notebook Falls Out The Cargo Hatch
sections.body:
Switch to the telephoto street lens mounted under the fuselage! Right on the cobblestones in front of Dr. Toad's shuttered clinic, the figure in lime green plants his boots, drops one shoulder, and begins reciting poetry as if the whole foggy square were his personal theater: *"Who's that man you see who grooms his 'stache so well? This mystery will be unsolved by those whole souls fell to his hell."* And look at the courier standing across from him! Paulo does not have time for theatrical recitations! Paulo has a locked leather satchel strapped to his chest, a black-powder pistol in his grip, and zero patience! He draws the hammer back and snarls: *"Who's that in the street stumbling like a drunken bum — get fucked, get out of my way. Do you not see the gun."* 

Up in the sky, Wario banks the helicopter sharply, and the rotor wash hits the street like a localized gale! Waluigi pulls Waluigi's leather-bound notebook from Waluigi's coat, desperately trying to transcribe the dialogue: *"Look there, talking to each other! Luigi is there — he is talking!"* But the green figure does not even flinch at the muzzle. He raises his chin and chants into the rotor wind: *"Now behold the twilight of the so-called-a-hero, who somehow found it easy to betray he who he claimed to love, the one who laid me low from up above."* 

And Paulo's thumb turns white against the iron frame! *"Cool but who asked — wait, I know the number — zero! I gotta go, you made me slow, I'm getting sick of ya."* Up above, the deck lurches forty-five degrees! Waluigi lunges across the vibrating deck plates, screaming: *"They will see us! WAH! Get this damn thing under control!"* Waluigi's boots slip on a loose bolt! The notebook flies from Waluigi's fingers, spins through the open hatchway like a fluttering white bird, and drops straight into the dark below! And what does Wario shout as our massive shadow falls over both men? *"THEY'RE LOOKING AT US! THAT MEANS THEY CAN SEE THE PROFIT!"* Profit! He watched our only intelligence notebook plummet into the street and saw a marketing opportunity!

sections.heading: 'I DIDN'T KNOW SKINNY T WORE GREEN' — Red Eyes, Elongated Arms, And Black Powder
sections.body:
Slow the playback down right here! This is the exact moment where the green figure stops looking like an eccentric recluse and turns into an unholy abomination! Look at those shoulders expand! The arms elongate until the tool-like hands scrape the stones, the eyes ignite into pulsing crimson coals, and the mouth widens past the ears like an open furnace door! Paulo does not step back an inch. He levels his pistol at the center of the chest, spits a glob of phlegm onto the cracked pavement, and says: *"What the fuck is that thing? I don't give a damn what kind of freak show you're running, just get your oversized head out of my way. You think some spooky transformation makes you special? It just makes you a bigger target. Move. Now."* 

And Mr. L laughs from the sewer grating beneath his boots! Hear that metallic scrape on the audio track? He screams into the night: *"Glad you're here. Now it's too late to escape! You will know the fear I felt as I began to melt in the flames of hate!"* And Paulo sneers right into the monster's teeth: *"Jesus Christ, you're the ugliest thing I've ever seen, fuckin' die! I didn't know skinny T wore green."* Skinny T! Waluigi wants that recorded in high fidelity! Paulo identifies him like a shady courier associate from the docks! 

Mr. L roars back, his long gray arms stretching into the lamplight: *"Witness who's behind the mask — desecrated — you should have been afraid to ask. Now in my desolation you will bask!"* And Paulo cocks the pistol: *"Buncha fancy words for making dudes dead. Nothing I haven't heard before. Eat lead — die, motherfucker!"* The pistol cracks! White muzzle flash strobes the square! Paulo drives a steel-toed boot straight into the creature's midsection, rolls behind a masonry pillar with his satchel pinned to his ribs, and shouts: *"I don't care how much you ‘melted’ or who you were before. You're just a fucking target blocking my route. You want to talk about desolation? You're the one standing in front of a gun with nothing but hot air coming out your mouth!"* That courier had ice in his veins!

sections.heading: 'RUN LIKE YOU'RE ESCAPING A TAX AUDIT!' — The Parapet Shreds The Rotor Blades
sections.body:
Back to the rooftop perspective! Here comes the landing Wario calculated by momentum! Look at the left landing skid catch the jagged stone edge of the clinic parapet! CRUNCH! The entire five-ton airframe does not land — it gets tripped like a runaway pig! The main rotor blades strike the chimney masonry, disintegrating in a blinding spray of orange sparks and shredded titanium! The canopy implodes, metal grinds against brick, and the cabin smashes into the roof with a shockwave that knocks the audio feed into static! 

Look at the wreckage when the smoke clears! Steam is hissing from ruptured coolant lines, oil is blazing on the manifold, and Wario's purple face is mashed against the cracked dashboard! *“...At least we're on the ground,”* Wario wheezes, *“Now I just have to figure out how much the repairs are going to cost me.”* Waluigi is choking on powdered brick and copper dust: *"Look over there. We have to get down."* Gunshots are echoing from the cobblestones below! And Wario kicks the mangled door off its hinges, seizes Waluigi by the collar, and roars: *"GUNSHOTS? THAT'S JUST THE SOUND OF A BAD INVESTMENT! GET OUT! MOVE YOUR LEGS OR I'M CHARGING YOU FOR THE MEDICAL BILLS! WE MOVE NOW, OR WE BECOME PART OF THE DEBRIS!"* 

Down in the street, Mr. L's elongated claw whips forward, snatches Paulo by the coat, and hurls him bodily through the clinic doors! Paulo crashes into plaster, rolls across broken timber, and fires straight back: *"You're going to pay for that! I don't care about your tantrum or your goddamn ‘desolation,’ I just want to finish this delivery."* Two rounds kick up grit at the creature's boots: *"Get your filthy claws off me! You think throwing me inside makes it easier for you? I'm still here, you overgrown freak, and I'm still pissed enough to bury you!"* And Wario drags Waluigi across the asphalt, howling: *"STRUGGLING IS A WASTE OF CALORIES! JUST MOVE! THEY'RE SHOOTING BECAUSE THEY DON'T LIKE THE COMPETITION — NOW GET OUT BEFORE I SELL YOUR BOOTS TO THE SCRAP DEALER! RUN! RUN LIKE YOU'RE ESCAPING A TAX AUDIT!"* A tax audit! That is the single word in the language that terrifies Wario into a sprint!

sections.heading: 'I DID LOVE YOU, MARIO — BUT WHY DID YOU TWIST THE KNIFE IN THE GASH?' — The Flesh-Paved Road
sections.body:
Turn up the audio on channel two! This is the most staggering passage on the whole spool of tape! Mr. L stands in the center of the street, his elongated arms dangling past his knees like hanging ropes, chanting a verse that chilled Waluigi to the bone: *"Standing at the bridge over the king's inferno, hand in hand, I thought that we'd fight together, and I never lost trust in my bro until he plunged me in the inferno."* *“Save your tragic little soap opera for someone who gives a damn!”* Paulo gasps, his back pinned flat to the clinic wall, *“I don't give a shit about your brother or your bridge, I just want you out of my way.”* Paulo fires a wild shot into the ceiling plaster to bring debris down! 

The cobblestones answer! Red fire climbs straight out of the cracks in the road! Mr. L throws his head back into the smoke and screams: *"For his betrayal the world shall burn — those who feel no guilt, those who have no sense of shame, all will play my game, all will perish all the same! Know my name!"* *“I don't care about your names or your games.”* Paulo snaps, his face bathed in blinding heat, *“You think I'm some hero who's gonna stand here and listen to you whine about shame? I just want the damn delivery made!”* Three heavy lead balls strike the monster's chest! 

And then — freeze the frame right here! Look at the street cobbles split open into wet pink flesh! Rows of jagged teeth sprouting across the roadway like the gullet of a leviathan! Mr. L twists his head completely backward on his neck, points a three-foot claw directly at Paulo, and screams: *"I did love you, Mario — but why did you twist the knife in the gash?"* Mario! Waluigi nearly dropped the clicker! He looked at a courier in grease-stained trousers holding an iron gun and called him Mario! And what does Paulo shout back? *“I don't know who your brother was, but he sounds like an absolute bastard. Stop screaming my name like we're some kind of friends — you're just another waste of space on my route.”* An absolute bastard! Paulo dismantled thirty years of legendary brotherhood in twelve words!

sections.heading: 'NO NEED FOR APOLOGIES — LONG PAST OVERDUE' — The Eyeball In The Road And The Falling Crossbar
sections.body:
Roll the footage into the narrow clinic alleyway! Mr. L's voice crawls out of the pulsing street like grinding stones: *"Who's that man you see who grooms his 'stache so well, who's the one who saw me as an empty shell to throw into the pyre, to damn within the fire? No need for apologies — long past overdue. Your sins you'll rue."* And right in front of the clinic threshold, a veiny, swollen eyeball the size of a beer barrel rises from the fleshy roadway and swivels toward the courier! Paulo does not hesitate! Paulo levels his pistol at point-blank range: *“I told you once, I don't give a damn about your poetry!”* Paulo spits, *“You keep talking like I'm some hero who owes you something. I just want to finish my job and get paid. Stop looking for an apology from someone who doesn't know your name!”* The hammer falls, and lead punches right into the vitreous fluid! 

Meanwhile, in the alley, Wario is hauling Waluigi through a choking cloud of soot! Waluigi sees orange flame leaping from the foundations and screams: *"That's-a not tax collectors, Wario, let go of me! FIRE! FIRE! WAH, WE ARE GOING TO DIE!"* And Wario's yellow grip tightens until Waluigi's purple fabric rips: *"TAXES OR NOT, THE FLAMES DON'T CARE ABOUT YOUR ACCOUNTING! IF WE STAY IN THE OPEN, WE'RE JUST TARGET PRACTICE FOR THE UNEMPLOYED! GET DOWN! GET LOW!"* 

A gas main ruptures five paces ahead, blossoming into a wall of roaring flame! Wario puts his head down, charges through the scorching smoke, and slams his entire three-hundred-pound bulk against the reinforced steel door of the clinic! The hinges give way, throwing both of us into the hallway! And what greets Wario? CLANG! A heavy rusted steel crossbar drops from the lintel and hits Wario directly across the back of his thick skull! He drops like an iron safe dropped down a mine shaft! And when Waluigi scrambles up, the corridor walls are throbbing with wet organic tissue, with Mr. L and Paulo facing us directly!

sections.heading: 'MASTER OF ICE, KEEPER OF THE GRIMOIRE' — One Slap To Wario's Face And A Jammed Pistol
sections.body:
Look at the corridor camera! Wario is spread-eagled on the grimy floor, snoring like a defective pump. Mr. L looms in the doorway, his layered voices clashing like gears: *"Do you hear that? That is the sound of your hope curdling. Let me peel away every layer of your resolve until nothing remains."* Waluigi does not despair! Waluigi leans down, draws back Waluigi's purple glove, and delivers ONE sharp, educational SLAP across Wario's cheek! Just one slap! The precise therapeutic dose! 

Wario snaps awake, thrashing like a landed cod: *"WAH! YOU TOUCH MY FACE?! I'm awake! I'm alert! I'm being assaulted by a coward! Is that thing... is it on the invoice? No. It doesn't have a permit! I'll charge you double for this! EXTRA_STRESS_FEE!"* Then a crate scrapes and Paulo emerges with his gun aimed right at Waluigi's forehead: *"Who the fuck are you!"* 

Watch Waluigi rise! This is Waluigi's supreme moment of stage command! Waluigi straightens to Waluigi's full seven feet, raises one long purple finger between the barrel and Waluigi's nose, and delivers the unvarnished reality: *“Waluigi is not a fool!”* One long finger rises between the muzzle and Waluigi's eye: *“I am the master of ice, the keeper of the grimoire, and the only person in this wretched corridor with a coherent grasp on the current situation! Put that crude piece of iron away before you pull the trigger and discover it won't do a lick of good against something with — sub-surface intentions!”* Waluigi swallows hard, then finishes him off: *“Your shouting is giving me a headache, and if my head explodes, I shall be forced to file a very lengthy complaint against your estate in the afterlife!”* 

Suddenly shadowy green clones peel out of the walls, reaching with gray claws! Paulo pivots and rakes the hallway with lead: *"Get your hands off my satchel or I'll break every finger you've got left!"* And then — CLICK! The cylinder jams on a bad primer! Paulo looks at the hammer, mutters *"Son of a bitch,"* throws the dead iron on the floorboards, and bolts for the rear exit! Waluigi's speech bought that exact jam!

sections.heading: 'STAR-A CLINIC!' — Dragging A Screaming Partner Away From The Growing Walls
sections.body:
Follow the interior tracking camera mounted high in the stairwell! Waluigi seizes Wario's thick wrist with both hands, plants Waluigi's pointed boots against the slimy boards, and drags: *"We are giving up on the Star-a clinic. Let's go."* And Wario digs his yellow workboots into the muck, flailing like an overturned tortoise and bellowing at the ceiling: *"LET GO OF MY HAND! THIS IS PRIVATE PROPERTY! I have — inventory! I have assets!"* He had a severe concussion, grease burns on both elbows, and ripped purple trousers! He had no assets! Waluigi was literally hauling two hundred and eighty pounds of shrieking deadweight through an active demonic digestive tract! 

Behind us, Mr. L's layered voice crawls along the ceiling like damp mould: *"Do not flee. Your legs will only carry you deeper into the maw of your own making. There is no exit from what has already been marked for consumption."* The hallway narrows by six inches every three seconds! Organic tendrils reach from the baseboards to snag our cuffs! Waluigi hits the heavy emergency exit with Waluigi's shoulder, throwing our combined weight against the latch and tumbling both of us out onto the freezing mountain dirt! Wario collapses face-down in the mud, clutching his battered temples and moaning: *"GET ME OUT! GET ME OUT OF THIS STINKING HOLE! My boots! My glorious shoes are getting ruined by this — this organic sludge! I'm filing a claim... for every single scratch..."* 

Waluigi turns back toward the open doorway, gasping for clean air. Mr. L stands directly on the threshold, flickering like a dying gaslamp in a draft, mist curling around his long gray boots: *"You believe you have crossed a threshold. But there is no ‘outside’ for one already marked. The gate remains open, and I am very, very patient."* Then the entire brick structure groans, mortar cracking as the building swells outward like rising bread! Waluigi heaves three hundred pounds of yelling partner over Waluigi's shoulder and runs for the wreck: *"Wario, we got to get outta here!"* Wario's skull bounces against Waluigi's spine with every stride: *"PUT ME DOWN! I AM NOT A BAG OF POTATOES! I'm going to — sue — for the bruising of my ribs!"* And Mr. L's parting words drift over the dark: *"Flight is merely a change in altitude. The rot remains within you."* That voice echoed in Waluigi's ears for three straight nights!

sections.heading: 'PICK WHICH WAY YOU WANT TO BLEED' — Paulo Puts A Muzzle Against Waluigi's Forehead
sections.body:
Roll to the wide shot of the square! The shattered helicopter lies tilted in the gravel, its hot turbines ticking like a dying clockwork mechanism while smoke curls from the crushed cowling. Mr. L's voice seems to seep from the very air between the stones: *"Choice is a cruel needle, sewing your desperation into the fabric of your fate. Pick your poison, little spark."* And Wario clutches Waluigi's sleeve from behind a crumpled landing strut, shivering with rage and terror: *"THE HELICOPTER! IT'S THE ONLY THING WITH A MOTOR! If we don't get that bird in the air, I'm going to be property of this land!"* Property of the land! The man was still worried about real estate titles while surrounded by teeth! 

Then Waluigi spots something pale and rectangular lying in the gravel twenty feet away: Waluigi's dropped notebook, intact in the dust! But before Waluigi's fingers can close around the leather cover, the cold black iron barrel of a carbine presses straight against Waluigi's forehead! Paulo has stepped out of the swirling smoke, his jaw locked like a vise: *"Get that piece of junk out of your hand before I put one in yours! You think you're making a choice? You're just picking which way you want to bleed. Give me the notebook! If it's got the coordinates, I can get us clear of this rot-zone in five minutes!"* 

Waluigi stammers, staring down the black rifled bore: *"Th-the notebook — WAH! Why would you need it at all?"* And Paulo's teeth grind together in raw fury: *"Because I'm the one who has to deal with the fallout of your failure, you moron! I don't care about ‘why.’ I just need what's inside so I can clear my debt and get out of this god-forsaken crater! Hand it over before someone decides your head looks better with a hole in it!"* He slams his heavy leather satchel onto the dirt, sending dust into the air! And what does our heroic syndicate boss yell from behind the bent landing gear? *"THE NOTEBOOK! IT'S THE ONLY THING LEFT WITH ANY VALUE! Give it to him, you fool! It's the only way out of this contract!"* Wario was already liquidating Waluigi's research to settle his own accounts!

sections.heading: 'YOU'RE RUNNING INTO THE NEST!' — Charging The Clinic With Stitched Paper For Armor
sections.body:
Watch the secondary camera angle on the auxiliary reel! Waluigi dives across the dirt, scoops up the leather-bound notebook, and holds it between Waluigi's temples and Paulo's gun! Paper! Waluigi used eighty pages of hand-ruled archival paper for body armour! But Waluigi does not sprint for the mangled helicopter! Waluigi charges straight back toward the clinic entrance! Wario screams from the ditch, waving his fat arms in hysterical protest: *"NO! THE HELICOPTER IS THE EXIT! DON'T GO BACK! You're going to get us sued! The medical fees alone for this trip will be astronomical!"* 

Paulo brings his carbine up, shouting through the swirling debris: *"YOU IDIOT! YOU'RE RUNNING INTO THE NEST! If you go back there, you're just volunteering for a funeral! The clinic is a death trap! You're choosing the grave over the getaway!"* BANG! The rifle blast tears through the mountain air! The muzzle flash illuminates the square in blinding white! The heavy lead slug strikes a jagged piece of sheared titanium a hand's width from Waluigi's left ear with a flat, screaming screech that vibrates straight down Waluigi's spine! Sparks shower across Waluigi's sleeves, and the shockwave nearly tears the paper from Waluigi's clenched fingers! 

And Wario screeches after Waluigi in total commercial contradiction: *"THE CLINIC IS A LIABILITY! But if we don't — well, at least the settlement will be bigger! Whatever is in that building, it has to have more gold than this wasteland!"* Gold! Even with high-calibre rounds tearing through the air, he was calculating insurance settlements! But Waluigi's boots hit a slick patch of gravel and motor oil. Waluigi's balance disappears. The stony ground rushes up and smacks Waluigi square in the teeth! Copper fills Waluigi's mouth, grit grinds against Waluigi's cheek, a high thin ringing drowns out the shouting, the notebook skids away across the cobbles, and the world goes completely black!

sections.heading: 'FINE! FINE! TAKE THE DAMN THING!' — Three Demands Before The Trigger Finger Goes White
sections.body:
Bring audio track two back up! Waluigi is lying unconscious in the gravel with a mouthful of dirt, but the directional microphones captured every single syllable of the transaction! Paulo steps right over Waluigi's outstretched boots, thumbing a fresh cartridge into his weapon, and levels the iron barrel straight at Wario's purple chest: *"Seems like he couldn't take the heat. Hand it over."* Wario has the notebook clutched fiercely against his belly, backing against a crumpled stabilizer fin: *"YOU'RE GOING TO PAY FOR THAT! YOU'RE GOING TO PAY IN INTEREST! Wario doesn't share! Wario keeps his assets! You want the book? Then you pay the processing fee! I'll call your father! I'll have you blacklisted from every trade route in the kingdom!"* 

He threatened to contact the courier's father! In the middle of an exclusion zone surrounded by throbbing teeth and burning pipes! Paulo does not even blink. Paulo does not negotiate. Paulo tightens his grip on the carbine stock until his trigger finger turns dead white: *"Last chance."* And that is the exact second where Wario's legendary financial bravery expires! He flings the notebook across the dirt: *"FINE! FINE! TAKE THE DAMN THING! There! It's yours! Wario is retiring from this negotiation! Just take the asset and let me live to see my next audit!"* 

The notebook hits the courier's chest. Paulo catches it against his heavy satchel, gives a thin, exhausted smile, and murmurs: *"Now let's see what you wrote down here, purple boy."* And Wario scrabbles across the dirt on hands and knees like an enraged crab, clawing at Paulo's trouser cuffs: *"HEY! THAT'S PRIVATE PROPERTY! That's an intellectual property violation! You haven't even signed the non-disclosure agreement! You're going to be audited! Wario will find your house! Wario will seize your shoes!"* Seize his shoes! Paulo thumbed open the front cover and strolled into the fog, reading Waluigi's field intelligence like the morning paper while Wario swore vengeance on his footwear!

sections.heading: 'THEY'RE SCRAPPING THE STOCK!' — A Single Torn Margin In A Bramble
sections.body:
Roll the final reel! Waluigi begins to regain consciousness in the freezing dirt. Mr. L's layered voice is drifting through the smoke: *"Awaken, and face the tally of your choices. The ‘purple boy’ seeks his prize in the dark, while you crawl toward the light of a very cold sun. But remember: every page turned is a debt incurred in blood."* And from ten paces away, Wario is screaming into Waluigi's ear: *"HURRY UP! GET UP! You're going to miss the audit!"* 

Mr. L reaches down a long gray hand from the mist: *"An eye for an eye. Such a primitive, charmingly violent sentiment. Wake, little scholar. The tally must be settled before the ink on your fate dries forever."* Wario screeches: *"GET UP! DON'T LET HIM TOUCH THE ASSETS! If he touches you, the contract is voided!"* Waluigi sits up screaming: *"WAH!"* And Wario scrambles over on his knees: *"WAH! YOU SAID IT! That's the spirit of a winner! Now get up and grab that notebook before the debt collectors find us both!"* Then the shadow pulls thin and vanishes into the air: *"You were gone long enough for the tally to shift. The debt remains, even if the face of the collector changes."* 

Waluigi searches Waluigi's pockets in total panic: *"My notebook? WAH? Where did it go? My notes! My new story I was writing — it had information about Luigi!"* Wario claws through a briar patch and comes up with a tiny scrap of paper caught on a thorn: *"THE NOTES! THE INTEL! THE ASSETS! Here! A piece! It's not the whole thing, but it's a start!"* Waluigi grabs Wario's tunic: *"Who took my-a notebook!"* And Wario roars: *"THEY'RE SCRAPPING THE STOCK! Some thief, some scavenger, some low-level bottom-feeder is trying to steal our monopoly! If they have those notes on the green one, they've just declared a hostile takeover of our interests! Give me a direction! Where did you last see it? We track the paper trail!"* 

The paper trail! He handed the book over with both hands to save his own skin, and now he is declaring a hostile takeover against a courier who walked away ten minutes ago! Waluigi slipped the torn scrap into Waluigi's coat, and that is where it stays. Cut the projector motor! Turn off the lamp! The reel is spooled, the screen is dark, and Waluigi is going to bed!

commentaries.title: The Unlocked Cell
commentaries.subtitle: In Which A Ceremonial Guard Jumps Four Times, A Toad In A New Suit Explains The Building, Five Rooms Are Wrong In The Right Order, A Koopa Says OH IT'S YOU, A Bean Shakes His Hand, A Wall Says SURPRISE, One Small Orb Ends A King, A Chamberlain Orders A Dog Dispatched, And A Bean Shop Has The Guard's Son
commentaries.standfirst: Waluigi was not born. Waluigi is going to talk you through it anyway, because the archive has ONE account of the night the Arrangement shook hands under Peach's Castle, and the account belongs to a Toad whose job was to stand next to a lamp. This is the whole night in order — the one o'clock post, the keys to every door, the ballroom, the wall of heavy Toads, the dining hall with the boy in it, the tower, the unlocked cell, the handshake, the wall, the fire, the sash, the orb, the applause, the kill order, five hours of drain, and a bean shop at dawn where the Guild has the guard's son and Fawful has a borrowed cloak. The jokes are Waluigi's. The night is the guard's. Waluigi will tell you which is which when it matters.
commentaries.pullQuote: A Koopa in a cell nobody had locked looked at a ceremonial guard with a lantern and said OH. IT'S YOU. Waluigi has waited fifteen years for a conspirator to sound that BORED.
commentaries.filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — read aloud at the desk the night after the filing, with the 955 drawer open, the Who Signed file on the floor, and the account squared to the blotter so that Waluigi could keep one finger on it the whole way through

sections.heading: Waluigi Was Not Born, Waluigi Has The Account, And The Account Begins With A KART RACE
sections.body:
Waluigi is going to talk you through this one from the beginning, and the beginning is one o'clock in the morning at Peach's Castle, a month or so before the Princess was killed, and the castle is AWAKE. Not ALERT. Awake. There is a difference and the whole night lives in it. The account is specific about why the building was up: the kart races were on. Somewhere in the palace a hall of Toads was watching a broadcast, and the noise of it came down the corridors in waves — a CHEER, a GROAN, the particular silence of a last lap — so that a guard standing a lantern post on the ceremonial route could follow the race without seeing it. Waluigi wants that on the record before anything else is. A kingdom thirty days from losing its monarch, and the palace is up late for KARTS.

Waluigi should say, before Waluigi says anything else, that Waluigi was not there. Waluigi was not born. Waluigi has ONE account — the guard's own, in the guard's own order, taken down as every session is taken down — and Waluigi has read it until the folds went soft. Everything that follows is on that paper or it is Waluigi's opinion of that paper, and I will tell you which is which, because I am PETTY and not a LIAR.

The guard. John Lee. Ceremonial guard, which is to say: a lantern in one hand, a sword at the hip that the kingdom issued for the LOOK of it, livery pressed, and an instruction to stand where the lamp made the castle look guarded. The account does not say how long he had held the post. It says he was GOOD at STANDING. Waluigi has met a great many Toads who were good at standing and not one of them ended a night with a captain's sash on both arms, so hold that thought. He had a small son asleep somewhere in the household wing — or so he believed at one o'clock. Underline *believed*. UNDERLINE it. The account did; Waluigi is only copying.

Two things were being talked about by every Toad who passed the lamp, and the guard collected both the way a lamp collects moths. First: the PRISONER. There was a prisoner in the dungeon — captured, held, *tense* was the word that travelled with him — and nobody who said the word prisoner would say what the prisoner was. Every Toad knew there was one. Not one knew it was a Koopa. Waluigi will tell you now what Waluigi worked out on the fourth reading: that is not secrecy about a prisoner. That is secrecy about a GUEST. Second: the MEETING. Mario and Luigi were expected. Coming to the castle that night to mediate a meeting with *this toad guy* — and the account never names the Toad, because the guards who said it did not know either. A meeting with NO named party and a prisoner with NO named species. The building was full of sentences with the nouns taken out.

And John Lee JUMPED. The account counts it, so Waluigi will count it: four times. STRAIGHT UP, lantern and all, at the news that the Mario brothers were coming to the building he was standing in. He was a FAN. Waluigi, who has spent a career not being the brother anybody jumps for, is going to let that sit without a joke, which costs me more than you know. The head guard came down the route to find out what a ceremonial post was doing BOUNCING, and questioned him, and the account records the questions as a formality and the jumping as the only honest thing anybody did in that castle before midnight became one o'clock. WAH. Four jumps. Remember them. They are the last thing in the account that is only funny.

sections.heading: A Toad In A NEW SUIT Comes Down The Corridor And Explains The Building To A Lamp
sections.body:
After the head guard went, Toadsworth came down the route. The account calls him the chancellor, and Waluigi is going to deal with that word in a minute, because Waluigi has to. First the suit, because the account puts the suit first: NEW. Cut for him. Worn the way a Toad wears a thing he has just been given and has decided he deserved. Waluigi has owned suits like that. Waluigi has been INSIDE suits like that at parties where nobody asked who invited me. You do not WALK in a suit like that. You ARRIVE in it, REPEATEDLY, down the same corridor.

He did not question John Lee about the JUMPING. He did not ask about the lantern, the post, the race, the brothers. He explained the building to him. *"I have the keys to every door,"* he said — and the account is careful here, and Waluigi is going to be careful with it — not as a threat. As an INVENTORY. The way a man tells you how many HORSES he has. Then, to a ceremonial guard with a lamp who had jumped four times because the Mario brothers were coming: *"Bask in your inferiority."* And on down the corridor, in the new suit, with the keys.

Waluigi wants to stop here and admire it, because Waluigi is an encyclopaedist of insults and that is a GOOD one. *Bask.* Not WALLOW, not SIT — bask, as if inferiority were weather and the guard were lucky to be out in it. Waluigi has had worse said to him by better-dressed people and none of them had the ECONOMY. TWO sentences. One inventory, one instruction. And then he was gone, and the lamp was still lit, and the guard was still a fan.

Now the word. The account says *chancellor*. In 955 BF the palace held two Toadsworths — the Elder as Royal Chamberlain, the son already styled Chancellor and already, by the Highsun 1 record, the Toad who found the figure in the chimney and took a beam from Fawful for his trouble. A ceremonial guard with a lamp is not the Toad you ask to tell the two apart. So Waluigi read the SENTENCE instead of the TITLE. The keys to every door are a CHAMBERLAIN'S inventory; the household's keys hang on the household's officer. A new suit a month before a succession is a chamberlain's suit. And later tonight — Waluigi is getting ahead of the lamp, forgive me — the same Toad in the same suit gives the Mages' Guild an order in public and is obeyed, which is the Guild's ear, which the disputed journals say the Elder had. Waluigi has filed the man in the new suit as Toadsworth the Elder and has written READING, NOT RECORD in the margin, in INK, so that it does not rub out. If a second account puts the son in the suit, the file moves and Waluigi apologises to the file. Not to the son. The son writes memoranda about guards. This Toad LECTURED one, and lecturing is what a man does who has recently been handed something and wants it seen in his hand.

Here is the thing Waluigi actually thinks, with the voice down for three sentences. The journals the Loyalists wave say *the positions were cleared*. Nobody has ever been able to say what a position was. A ceremonial guard, told by the man with the keys that he is inferior, an hour before he leaves his post — that is a POSITION being CLEARED, by a sentence, politely, with a lamp still in its hand. Voice back up. WAH. He said bask. To a Toad holding a LANTERN. The nerve of it is almost a credential.

sections.heading: Five Wrong Rooms, Every One Of Them BUSY, And A Boy At A Table Who Was Fine
sections.body:
After the suit went by, John Lee left the post. Waluigi is going to be exact about the verb because the account is: it does not say he was relieved and it does not say he deserted. It says he went to find where the brothers would be — he was a FAN, you will recall, there were FOUR jumps — and then it says, in order, where he was instead. Five rooms. Waluigi has walked them on the plans with a pencil and the line bends five times and never crosses itself, which is not what lost looks like. Lost LOOPS. This was a ROUTE.

The ballroom first. Trumpets — a fanfare being rehearsed or performed at one in the morning, the account cannot tell which — and Toads marching, in step, across the ballroom floor, in a formation that had nothing to do with a kart race and that nobody explained to a guard with a lantern. He backed out. Waluigi would like to know who rehearses a procession at one in the morning, and Waluigi knows exactly who, and so do you, and the account only knows that the trumpets were LOUD. VERY loud.

A corridor of heavy Toads next. BIG ones, ARMOURED, shoulder to shoulder in a wall formation across a passage, facing outward, not moving, not speaking. He did not try to pass them. He went another way. Waluigi has stood in front of walls like that. A wall of Toads facing OUTWARD is not guarding the corridor behind it from you; it is guarding you from the corridor. He went another way, and Waluigi notes that another way was available, which is to say the cordon had a GAP and the gap went EXACTLY where he went next.

The dining hall. And here the account slows down, and Waluigi is going to slow down with it, and the jokes are going to wait in the corridor. At the long table, past midnight, with the kart race audible through the wall, sat a small Toad boy with a plate in front of him and a maid beside him. *Marilyn*, the account names her — the only servant it names all night. And the boy was his. Toad Lee. Awake, at the table, being minded. The father looked at his son and his son's minder and — this is the sentence Waluigi believes above every other sentence in the account — he did not stop. Because he was a guard who had left his post and was in a room he had no business in, and because a boy at a table with a maid is a boy who is FINE. A LIAR makes the father heroic here. This father kept walking because he was embarrassed. Waluigi knows the Toad that boy grew into. He sits across from me and reads while stronger people argue about doors. Waluigi had taken that for temperament. Waluigi is no longer sure it was not training. Jokes back in the room.

A hooded figure passed him in the next corridor. Robed, head covered, walking with purpose toward the part of the castle he had just come from. The account notes it and moves on, because at that hour, in that building, a hood was a thing that went PAST you. Waluigi has circled the hood FOUR times in FOUR colours and will come back to it when there is a body on a floor to put beside it.

Then a tower, and a storage room at the top of it — crates, dust, the race very faint through the stone — and that is where the guards found him. A ceremonial post, in an ATTIC, with a LAMP. Waluigi has been found in worse rooms for better reasons and still would not have liked to explain the lantern.

sections.heading: Two Guards, No Names, No Anger, And A Staircase That Only Goes DOWN
sections.body:
Two guards. The account does not give them names and does not give them anger, and Waluigi, who gives everybody names and most people ANGER, is going to respect that for once because the absence is the information. They found a ceremonial post in a storage tower and did what the night's orders apparently said to do with a ceremonial post that was somewhere it should not be — which was to walk it down to the DUNGEON.

Stop there. Waluigi did. A guard off his post at one in the morning is a guard who gets sent back to his post, or sent to bed, or sent to the head guard for a second helping of questions. He does not get sent to the DUNGEON unless the dungeon is where SPARE Toads were being put that night, and the account is honest that it cannot tell which it was — punishment, reassignment, or simply the building's bottom shelf. Waluigi has decided the ambiguity is the guard's and not mine. He went. The lantern went with him. Down past the kitchens, down a stair, down a second stair, into stone that did not carry the race any more. Waluigi wants you to notice the race LEAVING. The whole night so far has had a soundtrack and the soundtrack was Toads cheering karts, and at the second stair it STOPS, and from here on the account is quiet in the way that cellars are quiet, which is not silence but the absence of anybody else's good time.

Now Waluigi is going to say the thing the account will not say for itself, because the account is a guard and Waluigi is not. Everybody who touched this Toad tonight moved him toward the cell. The SUIT lectured him off his post. The BUILDING funnelled him — ballroom, wall, dining hall, hood, tower — and every room turned him back toward the centre. Two guards walked him the last of the way. Waluigi is NOT saying the castle conspired to put one ceremonial guard with a lamp in front of a handshake. Waluigi is saying that if it had, the account would read exactly like this, and Waluigi has read a great many accounts of things that were arranged and they all have this shape: a man who thinks he is making CHOICES, walking down a corridor somebody else DREW.

Waluigi tried, for the record, to make the escort mean something and it will not. Two Toads, unnamed, with an order. The ONE thing Waluigi can squeeze out of them is this: the dungeon was staffed thinly enough that a lantern post could be sent down to it. A dungeon with a dangerous prisoner in it — *tense*, remember, the word that travelled — does not have room on its roster for a ceremonial guard who got lost in a tower. A dungeon with a GUEST in it does. It has ALL the room in the world, because NOBODY is watching the guest, because the guest is not going anywhere until his friend arrives. Waluigi is getting ahead of the lamp again. The lamp is on the second stair. The stone is cold. The race is gone. And somewhere ahead of it, in the dark, a door is standing the way a door stands when somebody has already turned the key.

sections.heading: 'So You Finally Came To Free Me — Oh. It's You.' — The Most BORED Sentence In Fifteen Years Of Paper
sections.body:
The cell door was not locked. Waluigi is going to give you the account's exact degree of emphasis, because the account is emphatic and Waluigi has learned to listen when a Toad with a lamp is emphatic: not forced, not open — UNLOCKED. Standing as a door stands when the lock has been turned by somebody with a key and left that way. One of the escort put a hand on it and it moved.

The prisoner was a Koopa.

Waluigi wants you to feel the lantern finding him. Every Toad in the castle had said *prisoner* and not one had said *shell*, and here is the lamp on the shell, and a ceremonial guard learning the SPECIES of the dungeon's guest at the SAME moment he learns that the dungeon's guest is not locked in. And the Koopa — this is the hinge of the night, the account gives it in full and Waluigi is going to give it in full — was not surprised by the door. He was surprised by the FACES. *"So you finally came to free me —"* and then, looking at a ceremonial guard with a lantern and two Toads in corridor livery, *"— oh. It's you."*

Waluigi has read that line aloud so many times the desk knows it. It goes UP and then it goes DOWN, and the down is not fear. A prisoner who is afraid of an open door says *who are you*. This one said *oh*. That *oh* is a man checking a clock. He had been expecting somebody, at an hour, and the lamp had come at the wrong hour or in the wrong livery, and he could tell the difference by the LIVERY. A real prisoner does not have APPOINTMENTS. Waluigi has been handed a hundred pieces of paper about the Arrangement — journals, forgeries, forgeries of journals — and not one of them had a voice. This one has a voice, and the voice is bored, and Waluigi would trade every signature in the capital file for one more sentence in it.

John Lee, a guard who had not known the prisoner was a Koopa until the lantern found him, had walked in on an appointment. Waluigi wants that phrase on the record exactly. Not a plot. An APPOINTMENT. Plots have CONSPIRATORS. Appointments have a TIME, and somebody who is LATE.

And then the escort fell. Waluigi is going to lower the voice here, because a Toad DIED, and the account that watched him die gives him one sentence, and Waluigi is not going to give him a joke. One of the two Toads who had walked John Lee down fell, dead, between one breath and the next, with no blade in him that the guard saw and no sound that he heard. The lantern shook. That is all the account has, and the account was standing next to him. The other escort is not mentioned again. Waluigi has read the passage a dozen times trying to find him — in the corridor, on the stair, ANYWHERE — and he is not there, and Waluigi has stopped believing the account is hiding him. Waluigi thinks he was simply not worth recording to anybody but me. Which is how Waluigi knows the account is honest, and how Waluigi knows what the night thought of Toads.

Voice back up, slightly. A hood went past John Lee in a corridor, walking this way with purpose. A Toad is now dead beside an unlocked cell with no mark on him, half a minute before — well. Waluigi will not put those together in the prose. Waluigi has put them together in the LEADS, where a reader can roll for it. The paper does not say. The paper only says the lantern shook.

sections.heading: I HAVE VICTORY — A Bean, A Koopa, Three Hoods, And A Guard Who Had Become FURNITURE
sections.body:
Fawful came in. The account describes him as a Toad would who had never seen one — small, green, the glasses, the teeth, the voice that arrives before the body does — and Waluigi, who has filed the bean across eighty-five years and three alphabets of CAPITAL letters, can confirm the description is accurate and that the voice has never once arrived AFTER the body. He went to the Koopa. The Koopa put out a hand. Fawful took it.

*"I HAVE VICTORY,"* Fawful said — and the account records it in capitals because that is how it was said, and Waluigi, who is in no position to criticise anybody's capitals, records it the same way. Victory. A month out. NOTHING had happened yet. The Princess was asleep upstairs, the brothers were on their way, the karts were still going round, and a bean in a dungeon had already COUNTED IT WON. Waluigi has been accused of declaring victory EARLY. Waluigi has never declared it before the building was awake.

*"Never thought I'd work with a bean,"* the Koopa said — which the account records as the only thing anybody in that corridor said in a normal voice, and Waluigi wants you to look at the verb, because Waluigi did, and it rearranged the file. *Work with.* Not plot with, not join, not serve. WORK. The Koopa has an employer and a job and an opinion about his colleagues, like a man on a site. He is not CONSPIRING. He is on SHIFT.

Then three hooded figures came in behind the bean. Mages' Guild — the account knows the robes; every Toad in the palace knew the robes — and they did not greet the Koopa and they did not greet the bean. Nobody shook THEIR hands. One of them said what they had come to say, and it was two sentences, and Waluigi has them on a card propped against the lamp: *The guild is already in place.* And then: *we won't act yet.*

Waluigi is going to drop the voice for this, because it is the most important paragraph in the account and the jokes would only get in its way. Read the grammar. *In place* is a word for a mechanism. *Won't act yet* is a word for a date. A Guild that was JOINING somebody else's plot would say *we agree*. This Guild said, in effect, the installation is complete and the switch is not tonight. The journals say the Guild provided the method. Waluigi had always read that as a thing handed over — a potion, a spell, a vial. The dungeon sentence says the method was not handed over. It was INSTALLED. The Guild was not a GUEST at the Arrangement. The Guild was the SCHEDULE. And a month later, on Highsun 1, the record has the Guild *already positioned* — scrubbing the chambers, snapping fingers at a Chancellor, in the vault during the killing. The same adverb. A month apart. From the Guild's own mouth. Waluigi did not expect to be handed the word *already* twice and Waluigi has not slept properly since.

Voice back. And through all of it — the handshake, the capitals, the two sentences — John Lee was still holding the lantern. The account is honest about this in a way that embarrasses the account: nobody had yet LOOKED at him. A ceremonial guard with a dead escort at his feet and a lamp in his hand had been, for the length of a handshake, furniture. A LAMP-STAND. The Arrangement shook hands in front of a Toad the way you would shake hands in front of a coat rack, and that — Waluigi is certain of this — is why he is alive. The schedule did not FORGET him. The schedule never COUNTED him.

Then he ran. The account gives it two words and Waluigi will not pad them. The plate on the filing shows the hoods with their hands lit; the account does not say that, and Waluigi left it, because SOMETHING put the escort on the floor and Waluigi would rather the artist guessed than nobody did.

sections.heading: SURPRISE, IT'S ME — The Wall Comes In, The Captain Does Not Come Out, And Bowser Has Never Heard Of The Bean
sections.body:
He ran up the stairs toward the only authority he had been questioned by that night, and found the captain, and told him — and Waluigi would like you to hear a ceremonial guard with a lamp say this to the Captain of the Palace Guard in one breath: the cell is unlocked, the prisoner is a Koopa, there is a bean, there are hoods, the escort is dead. FIVE facts. Any one of them is a night's work. The account does not record the captain's answer, because the captain did not get to give it.

The wall came in.

*"SURPRISE, IT'S ME,"* said Bowser, through the dust, at a hall of Toads who had been watching a kart race. Waluigi has filed Bowser's entrances for most of a career and this is, by some distance, the most honest one: he announced the surprise and then he announced who it was, in case the WALL had not made it clear. He had come to the meeting. He SAID so: *"I wasn't invited to the meeting."* He looked for the brothers and announced that they were not here — which was true — and the account says it seemed to disappoint him more than the Toads did. Waluigi believes that absolutely. Bowser without the brothers is a man who has thrown a PARTY and been the only one to arrive, and he had come through a WALL to arrive.

Then he breathed fire down the hall.

Waluigi is going to put the voice down now and leave it down for a paragraph, because the next thing is a death and the account was standing next to it. The captain stood in the fire. The account is brief about it in the way that accounts by people who were beside the person are brief: the fire went down the corridor, the captain was between the fire and the stair up to the royal apartments, and then there was no captain. John Lee was behind him and lived. The account does not say the captain was the target. It says he was between the fire and the stair. Waluigi has been fair to Bowser about very little in eighty-five years of filing and will be fair to him about that: the captain did not move, and the fire did not CHOOSE. That is the night's second body and the first one with a cause.

*"Take me to Peach,"* Bowser said, to whoever was left. Voice back up, because Waluigi cannot help it: he came through a wall, killed the captain of her guard with his breath, and asked to be TAKEN to her, as if there were a DESK. There has never been a desk. Bowser has asked to be taken to Peach at every door in the kingdom and not once has anybody said *certainly, this way*.

And now the line the capital file has been waiting fifteen years for without knowing it. Somebody in the smoke said the bean's name — the account is not clear who — and Bowser did not know it. *He didn't know Fawful.* Waluigi wants you to sit in the dust with that. The Koopa King, a month before the Highsun 1 narrative made him Fawful's partner in the murder of the woman he had just asked to be taken to, stood in the ruins of a wall he had made and asked WHO. TWO intruders in ONE castle in ONE night and they had NEVER met. Bowser came for Peach the way Bowser always came for Peach — loud, through masonry, asking for her by name — and was annoyed the brothers were not there to make it a proper evening. Fawful came through the dungeon with the Guild. Thirty days after Highsun 1 the kingdom decided these were the same visit. The guard who was in both rooms says they were not, and the guard had no reason to lie and every reason to be somewhere else. WAH. The only person in Peach's Castle that night who did not know who the conspirators were was the one the kingdom later convicted of conspiring.

sections.heading: Inventory: A Sword That Weighed Something, A Letter With An ADDRESS, And The Captain's Sash On Both Arms
sections.body:
What a ceremonial guard does when the captain is gone and the hall is burning is, by this account, INVENTORY. Waluigi respects that more than he can say. Waluigi has done the same in worse rooms — when the world is on fire you COUNT what is on the floor, because the floor is the only thing that is not MOVING. There was a dead Toad near him — a guard, not the captain, one of the ones the fire had reached first — and John Lee took three things from the floor. Waluigi is going to take them in the account's order.

The shortsword. His own was ceremonial; this one was not; and the account records that he knew the difference by the WEIGHT. Waluigi has read a thousand filings in which a man picks up a weapon and this is the only one that tells you what the hand learned. A ceremonial sword weighs what a sword LOOKS like. A real one weighs what it is FOR. He had been standing next to the first for however long he had held the post, and the second told him in one lift what the kingdom had been issuing him.

A letter, from the dead Toad's livery, which he read by the fire — and Waluigi wants you to picture the light source, because the account did: *meet me in Fawful's bean shop.* No signature the account mentions. An ADDRESS, in effect, on the body of a palace guard who had been standing in a hall waiting for the Mario brothers. Waluigi will say the thing plainly, voice down. The Guild was in the dungeon. The Koopa was in the dungeon. Fawful was in the dungeon. And up HERE, among the Toads waiting for Mario, at least one guard already had the shop's address in his coat. The Arrangement was not a thing happening beneath the castle. It was a thing the castle was already full of. Voice up. He went to a bean shop at dawn because a dead Toad's pocket told him to, which is the most WALUIGI method of navigation Waluigi has ever seen a Toad use, and Waluigi did not teach it to him, and Waluigi is a little jealous.

And the captain's sash. SCORCHED, the account says, but WHOLE. He wound it around both forearms, the way a Toad binds his arms for a fight he does not expect to win or to ask permission for. He was a ceremonial guard. He knew what a captain's sash was FOR and he knew it was not for this, and he put it on anyway. Waluigi has had the portrait painted with the sash exactly there, on both arms, so that the next person who sees a Toad wearing a captain's rank as a bandage knows whose it was and in what fire.

Around him, through the dust — the account does not forget this and neither will Waluigi — the Goombas were coming in behind Bowser and taking Toads. The account uses the word *kidnapping*. It does not count them. It records that it was happening and that nobody was stopping it, because everybody who might have was dead, on fire, or watching the Koopa King. Waluigi wants to be precise about what that sentence proves and what it does not. It proves that Goombas took Toads from the hall. It does not say WHERE. It does not say HOW MANY. It does not say whether the small boy at the long table was one of them, and Waluigi has read it forty times hoping it would, and it will not, and the Guild is about to tell the father something in a bean shop that makes the question worse. Three things off the floor. A sword that weighed something, a letter with an address, and a dead man's rank around both arms. Waluigi has seen knights go to war with less and a great deal more ceremony.

sections.heading: One Small Orb, One King On The Floor, A Hall That CHEERED The Wrong Heroes, And A Striped Sock
sections.body:
A Mages' Guild member ended it. Waluigi is going to be as exact as the account is, because the technology ledger needed every word and got only these: one hood, one object — *a small orb* — held UP, not thrown. And Bowser went down. Not staggered. Down, at once, the way a thing goes down when the thing that was holding it up has been switched off. ONE shot. The Koopa King on the floor of Peach's Castle with his fire still smoking in the walls.

Waluigi has filed Bowser being beaten by a great many things — brothers, falls, lava, his own architecture — and never in ONE, never by something the size of a FIST, and never, NEVER, to applause. Because the Toads cheered. The account says it without comment, which is the comment, and Waluigi is going to supply the comment the account was too close to make: the hall that had been burning cheered the GUILD. The hoods were heroes. The mages who had been in the dungeon shaking hands with a Koopa twenty minutes earlier were, as of that cheer, the mages who had saved the castle. Waluigi wants a date on that cheer and has given it one on the ledger: it is the first time the archive can place the Mages' Guild being LOVED inside Peach's Castle, and the kill order follows it by about a minute. LOVE first, then the ORDER. That is how a position gets cleared. You do not need the keys for that part. You need an orb and a room full of frightened people who have just stopped being frightened.

Mario and Luigi arrived then. Late — the account is precise that Bowser was already on the floor — into a hall that smelled of fire and relief, to a cheer that was not for them. Waluigi is going to say this with the voice down because it is the saddest sentence in the account and the guard did not know it was sad. He was still a FAN. He had jumped four times for them. They walked in behind the applause for somebody else, to a hall that had ALREADY been saved, and the Toad with the sash on his arms was, Waluigi would bet the desk, still glad to see them.

Luigi tripped on a striped sock. Voice back up, because what else is Waluigi supposed to do with that. The account does not say whose. A striped sock, on the floor of a palace hall, at two in the morning, after a kart race and a dragon. The account notes it. Waluigi notes it. Neither of us can source it and Waluigi has stopped trying, because some things are in an account because they HAPPENED, and a Toad who INVENTED a night would not have invented the SOCK. Waluigi has it on a card by itself. The card says SOCK and nothing else and Waluigi looks at it when the rest of the file gets too heavy.

The orb. Waluigi has no name for it. Nothing the archive holds from the Guild in 1040 looks like it, which means either they stopped making it or they stopped SHOWING it, and Waluigi knows which of those a guild does. It is on the technology ledger as exactly what it did: one object, hand-held, one use, one result, a Large dragon-turtle unconscious in front of witnesses. Pattern unknown. Price — and here Waluigi pulls the Guild invoice from the capital file and lays it beside the ledger card — price NOTHING. The Guild that would later bill a party three hundred gold for compounding a potion while frightened put the Koopa King on the floor of Peach's Castle for free. It took the CHEER instead. Waluigi has the paper. The love was the invoice.

sections.heading: 'Like A Lost Dog. A Nuisance To The Toads Is A Nuisance To Us. Mages' Guild — DISPATCH Of Them.'
sections.body:
John Lee said it. Waluigi wants you to see what he looked like when he said it, because the account does: the captain's sash on both forearms, a dead Toad's sword, a lantern somewhere about him still — and he said it INTO the cheer, to a hall of grateful Toads and two late brothers. The Guild works with Fawful. He had seen the handshake. He said so. A ceremonial guard, whose job that morning had been to stand where a lamp made the castle look guarded, told the castle what he had seen in its own basement, OUT LOUD, in front of the people who had just been cheered for saving it. Waluigi has made a career of saying the unwelcome thing in the wrong room and Waluigi has never once done it with a captain's sash on and a Guild in earshot. Four jumps. Remember the four jumps. This is where they went.

Toadsworth answered. The new suit, from the edge of the hall, in the voice of a Toad who has the keys. The account gives it as three sentences, and Waluigi is going to give them to you one at a time, the way they landed. *"Like a lost dog."* Then: *"A nuisance to the Toads is a nuisance to us."* Then, to the hoods who had just been cheered: *"Mages' Guild — dispatch of them."*

Read them as policy, because Waluigi did, with the voice all the way down. The first makes him an ANIMAL. The second makes him the Toads' problem and therefore *ours* — and look at the pronoun, because Waluigi has looked at nothing else for an hour: a Toad of the household, speaking of the Guild's interests as his own or his own as the Guild's, and the sentence does not care which. The third is an ORDER. Given in PUBLIC. By the man with the KEYS. To the Mages' Guild. And OBEYED. The journals say the Regency provided the opportunity. Waluigi had always read that as the date. It was also this: a man of the household, in front of witnesses, making a Guild killing a palace matter, with a sentence about dogs. Voice up. Waluigi has been called worse than a lost dog in better halls, and nobody who said it had the Guild on hand to make it stick.

A bolt came. The account says a bolt — from a hood's hand, across the hall, at a ceremonial guard — and it MISSED. Waluigi wants to be honest about why it missed, because the account is: not because the guard was QUICK, but because he was already MOVING, because he had been moving since the dungeon and had not stopped. A man who has been running since the cell is a hard thing to hit with anything that needs a moment's aim. He went down and out and away, into the part of the castle that does not carry the race, and the hall — this is the account's last word on the hall, and it is a cold one — went back to CHEERING.

Waluigi is going to be careful with this paragraph, because the Loyalists would give a great deal for it, and that is exactly why. It is a guard's account of a sentence said across a burning hall. It is NOT a journal. It is NOT a confession. It is not notarised and nobody in a new suit has signed it. But it is the only version of the Arrangement in the whole archive in which the Chamberlain is a MAN SPEAKING rather than a dead man's handwriting, and the man said *dispatch of them* in front of two brothers who, by this account, did nothing. Waluigi has opened a lead on that too. Waluigi is a fan of nobody and has been one of theirs longer than he admits, and that sentence — the brothers in the hall, the order given, the bolt loosed, nothing — is the one in the account Waluigi would most like a second account to contradict.

sections.heading: Five Hours Of Drain, One Goomba That COUNTED, A Pipe Full Of More, And A Grate
sections.body:
The account's clock stops at the bolt and restarts five hours later, and the five hours are the warp system. Waluigi is going to be honest about what Waluigi has for those hours, which is: the pipes under Peach's Castle — the drains, the sewers, the old warp lines the castle's basements are threaded with — and a ceremonial guard with a lantern going through them in the dark with a letter's worth of destination. *Meet me in Fawful's bean shop.* That was the MAP. A dead Toad's pocket and a lamp. Waluigi has navigated by LESS and arrived at WORSE.

One Goomba found him. He stomped it. And here the account does a thing Waluigi has learned to trust — it goes SHY. The first thing he had ever killed, a Goomba in a drain, flattened under a ceremonial boot. And it counted. The account says it counted — that the guard felt it count — which is a thing accounts say when the table has said so, and Waluigi, who has sat at tables, knows exactly the sound that sentence makes when it is said. A ceremonial guard. A boot the kingdom issued for parades. One Goomba, in the dark, under a castle that had just ordered him shot. Waluigi has filed the experience points on it as a preview, because that is what the archive does with a table's word until the table confirms it, and Waluigi would like it noted that of all the four hundred he awarded this Toad for the night, the TWENTY-FIVE for the Goomba are the ones Waluigi is SUREST of.

Then a pipe, and more Goombas out of it. An AMBUSH, the account calls it — a warp pipe mouth and Goombas coming out of it at a Toad who had just learned, thirty seconds earlier, that he could stomp. And he got through it. The account does not say how. Waluigi believes that too, and Waluigi will tell you why with the voice down: the people who get through things in the dark rarely know how. Waluigi has got through things in the dark. Waluigi wrote them up afterwards with great confidence and a diagram, and the diagram was a LIE, and the getting-through was TRUE. The account did not draw a diagram. The account said a pipe, Goombas, and then it said five hours. Waluigi trusts a Toad who will not explain his own survival more than any Toad who will.

Five hours. Then a grate, then a cellar, then a SHOP. FOUR words for the end of it and Waluigi will not add a FIFTH.

What Waluigi will add is this, because the warp system is already on the technology ledger as infrastructure and Waluigi promised the ledger nothing new: a lost ceremonial guard with a lantern — a Toad who could not find the ballroom from the ceremonial route, who got lost FIVE times above ground in a building he worked in — navigated the drains from the dungeon of Peach's Castle to one specific shop in Toad Town in five hours, with a letter for a map and a Goomba for a tutorial. Either the pipes under the castle are better signposted than the castle, or the shop is closer to the dungeon than any honest shop should be. Waluigi has written both on the card and underlined the second. WAH. A bean shop, on the drains, five hours from the cell by lantern. Somebody CHOSE that cellar. Somebody chose it BEFORE they chose the bean.

sections.heading: The Bean Badge At Dawn — The Prisoner Got There FIRST, The Guild Has The Boy, And A Bean Puts On A Cloak
sections.body:
Fawful's Bean Badge. A bean shop, in Toad Town, with Fawful's NAME on it and a tray of badges on the counter — Waluigi has the card filed, it is what a shop like that hands you — which the account walked into at dawn with a sash on its arms and found already occupied. The Koopa was there. The prisoner. Out of the castle, ahead of a Toad who had crawled five hours of drain to reach the address, sitting in the shop as though he had never been anywhere else. Waluigi wants you to feel that one in the knees, because the guard must have. FIVE hours. And the man from the cell is already in the CHAIR.

He explained himself, and the account gives the explanation plainly, so Waluigi will. He had led the escort into the ambush. He had alerted the castle to Bowser's attack — it was HE who had told them the Koopa King was coming. Two sentences. Voice down, because they rearranged the whole night above: the dead escort was his doing. The castle had KNOWN Bowser was coming — which means the only person surprised by SURPRISE, IT'S ME was the person who said it. And the unlocked cell, which Waluigi had been reading as the night's great wrongness, was the one honest door in the building. It was EXACTLY what it looked like. Everything ELSE was pretending to be locked.

Who was in the shop. Two Mages' Guild operatives. A Goomba, sitting by the door like a shop cat — the account's image, not Waluigi's, and Waluigi is jealous of it. And Fawful.

They told him about his son before he asked. Waluigi is putting the voice away for this paragraph entirely, and the reader will know when it comes back. *"Your son is being taken care of,"* one of the Guild said. *"Toad Lee won't have to worry about being trafficked in our care."* The account records the sentence whole and records that John Lee did not answer it. Nobody in that shop had said the word *trafficked*. The father had not said it; the account would have it if he had. The Guild put the word in the room, attached to a small boy, in the negative, in the same breath as *our care*, before the father had asked where his son was — which means they knew whose father had come through the grate before he came through it. Waluigi said in the filing that he would not editorialise on that sentence and Waluigi is keeping to it here, in a commentary track, where Waluigi editorialises on SOCKS. The people who said it chose the word. That is the editorial.

They told him about the castle. Bowser was waking — screaming, the account says, the ground shaking under Toad Town with it — and the brothers were busy with him, which was the POINT. That was what Bowser was for. Voice back, because Waluigi cannot leave that alone: the Koopa King, convicted a month later of the murder, was that night a noise the Guild kept running so that the heroes would have something to hit. An APPLIANCE. A KETTLE left on.

They asked him to join. Then Fawful explained the plan, and put on a cloak to do it — a Mages' Guild cloak, over the red, pulled up — and Waluigi wants you to understand that of everything in this account, the cloak is the thing Waluigi would LEAST have believed if a Toad with a lamp had not seen it. *"I HAVE PLAN,"* in capitals, and the plan was a MUSHROOM. The vacuum shroom — Fawful's own make, the account says, Fawful tech — which, inhaled, turns the inhaler into a vacuum: Bowser breathes it and sucks up everything in reach, the brothers included. The castle's wards were still active, which somebody in the shop said as a problem and Fawful said as a DETAIL. The Koopa had a fat vial — the account calls it that, *the fat vial*, a glass thing with weight in it — and the shroom was to go into Bowser by way of it. *"Dispatch of this finkrat and takeover kingdom,"* Fawful said, in the Guild's cloak, and the two operatives did not correct the pronoun. Waluigi has filed the shroom and the vial as described and not one word further; the account does not see them used. Waluigi has filed the cloak as the reason the first draft of Highsun 1 said Fawful and the second did not. By the time anybody was choosing a murderer, the bean was wearing the Guild.

sections.heading: 'Are You STUPID? You Just Said You Don't Trust Us. We're Protecting Your Son.' — The Last Sentence, And Waluigi's
sections.body:
John Lee said he wanted to disappear. Waluigi is going to give you the three things he said in the account's order, because the order is the man. First: he wanted to disappear. A ceremonial guard who had seen the Arrangement shake hands, watched a captain burn, been called a dog and shot at by the people a hall had just cheered, crawled five hours of drain, and found the prisoner in the chair — wanted, more than anything, to not be in the account any more. Waluigi has WANTED that. Waluigi has never once GOT it, and neither did he.

Then he said he wanted his son. Waluigi wants you to notice that the second thing came AFTER the first, and that the account does not pretend otherwise, and that Waluigi thinks more of him for it, not less. A man who says *my son* first is making a SPEECH. A man who says *let me vanish* and then hears himself and says *no — my son* is a father who has just remembered he is one, in a bean shop, at dawn, with a Guild watching him remember.

Then he asked the Guild for escorts to go and get the boy. And the Guild said the last sentence of the account, and Waluigi is going to give it to you whole because it is, in its way, perfect: *"Are you stupid? You just said you don't trust us. We're protecting your son."*

Waluigi has read that line more times than the sock. It is not an insult. It is a LOCK. BOTH halves are true — he did not trust them; they had the boy — and the sentence is built so that you cannot hold both halves at once. Ask for help from the people you have just said you do not trust and you are stupid. Do not ask, and your son stays where he is. Waluigi has been on the wrong end of contracts drafted by better lawyers and never one with fewer words. The Guild did not THREATEN the father. The Guild EXPLAINED his position to him, the way the suit had explained the building, and the account ends there, with the explanation hanging in a shop that smelled of beans, and a Goomba by the door, and Bowser screaming somewhere under the city.

Now the thing Waluigi owes you, with the voice all the way down and left there. The provenance. This night was played, at the table, as a session in 955 BF, with John Lee as the character at it, and it reached this desk as every session reaches this desk — as the record of what the table saw, in the order the table saw it. The archive has one account. It has filed it as one account. There is NO second guard, NO second Toadsworth, no chambermaid's statement, no Koopa's confession beyond the two sentences he gave in a shop. Waluigi has read the man in the new suit as the Chamberlain and marked it as a reading. Waluigi has left the escort's death unexplained and the hood in the corridor uncircled in the prose. Waluigi has not asked Toad Lee a single question about any of it, and will, in daylight, with the account closed, and will take whatever answer a diplomat gives who learned very young that a room full of adults can be wrong at once.

And here is where Waluigi pays for the whole night. Waluigi spent fifteen years arguing about a dead man's handwriting — the journals, the forgery claim, the ink, the fold — and the thing that broke the Arrangement open was not Waluigi. It was a Toad who could not find the BALLROOM. Who jumped four times for the brothers and was still glad to see them when they walked in behind somebody else's applause. Who took a sword, a letter and a sash off a floor and went down a drain with a lamp because a dead man's pocket told him to. Waluigi, the best archivist in the building — and I am — contributed a reading and a margin note. The guard contributed the NIGHT.

Voice up, one last time, because the file would not recognise me otherwise. He is in a bean shop he does not trust, with a captain's rank on both arms and a Goomba by the door, and the only escort on offer is the people who have his son. The next account, if there is one, starts at that door. Waluigi will be at the desk when it arrives. WAH. Somebody lock something.

commentaries.title: The Soul-Ring, the Feywild Wildfire, and the Twenty-One Day Cut: Waluigi's Cut
commentaries.subtitle: the waking Toad, Cornburary's shadow writers, the proposal with pants down, and twenty-one days on the clock
commentaries.filed: 10 October 2026
commentaries.kicker: THE WALUIGI CUT · FIELD AUDIT & DESK OBSERVATION
commentaries.pullQuote: Cornburary brought a clipboard to a burning haunted house; Hjumpik gave away an ancient soul artifact for a smile; and I discovered our whole universe has an expiration date stamped on a goblin tavern wall. WAH!
commentaries.standfirst: Waluigi watches the corridor minutes unfold from his desk, breaking down the exact moment Toad Lee woke up screaming, why an Iron Legion quartermaster tried to sue a collapsing ceiling, how emotional resonance burns purple, and why twenty-one days is twenty days more than Waluigi wanted to spend in the Feywild.

sections.heading: The Daydream of an Axe and the Unlocked Cuffs
sections.body: WAH! Look at where we open this filing! Toad Lee is tied to a chair in the middle of a bedroom being slowly swallowed by aggressive root systems, and his very first conscious reaction to being captured by foreign shock troops is to tell me about a pastoral family picnic! Listen to the transcript, word for word: "Where am I, Waluigi? I was in a plain field with bright green grass, clear blue skies, there was a hill. I saw what seems to be my dad. We were play fighting. I was fighting with the axe I have, he was fighting with his? I don't know, I have some snippets of my father... ehh don't know." I am sitting right across from him in an armchair, wearing heavy steel handcuffs that I had already slipped five minutes ago. Waluigi does not stay locked in standard IRON restraints! Waluigi slipped them immediately and just sat there wearing them anyway because an uncuffed prisoner gets watched twice as hard by suspicious guards! I asked him if he wanted to go back to his daydream because, frankly, standing inside an overgrown bedroom with guards holding loaded crossbows on us is expensive. When Toad Lee asked me to remind him what happened, Waluigi gave him the clean tactical summary: Hjumpik traded us for an audience with a plant monster, either out of sheer desperation or raw SELFISHNESS. And the IRON LEGION guards standing by the door actually chimed in to validate my arithmetic! The guards say: "He got the story mostly right." When the enemy's own sentries agree with Waluigi's breakdown of party loyalty, that is not cynicism—that is ACCURATE military accounting! Toad Lee apologized to our captors with a humble "Sorry my sirs, didn't mean to" and announced: "While I wait for rescue, might as well look around." Waluigi admires the composure, even if the family AXE psychology requires its own separate case file. You wake up tied up by the IRON LEGION, and you immediately start browsing the furniture like it is a polite Sunday estate sale! Waluigi has seen many hostages in his career, but none who treated enemy captivity like a polite hotel lobby! Waluigi made a mental note to inspect the wardrobe hinges while our guards were busy chuckling at Toad Lee's manners. If an imperial garrison offers you hospitality while holding you hostage, Waluigi takes the armchairs and plans the exit! WAH!

sections.heading: Elven Desk Reference and Special Forces
sections.body: WAH! Toad Lee walked over to the fine writing desk and discovered a stack of journals, logbooks, and references, every single one of them penned in classical elven script. He turned to me and asked for paper and pen. Waluigi always carries a pristine field writing kit, so I handed it over without hesitation. Then Toad Lee turned to the two armored sentries and politely asked if they spoke elvish. The guards were completely baffled: "What? We don't know that." Toad Lee pressed them, asking: "What do you mean you don't know this? Weren't you guys denizens of the Feywild?" And that is when they dropped the curtain: "Huh? We're the Colour Division of the Iron Legion." They are not fey nobles! They are an external imperial expeditionary unit in full MAGITEK uniform!
