And their operational plan is delightfully blunt: "We were sent here to capture Hjumpik. We needed you guys as leverage, and our plan is working. Once Aurelia beats up Hjumpik, we grab him and drag him out." Waluigi appreciates operational transparency! They did not invent a mystical excuse; they took hostages because a contractor broke his delivery schedule, and they are waiting for the homeowner to tenderize our dwarf so they can drag him home without taking structural damage. LEVERAGE. That is the word they used downstairs, and that is the only word that matters on an IRON LEGION balance sheet. And when Toad Lee asked if they were confident, they replied: "Yes we are, as we are of Mr. Miser." Waluigi noted that line immediately in his private papers! They consider Archie Miser an inevitable target, but Hjumpik was the primary objective of the morning. Waluigi knew right then that this entire raid was about overdue DEBT and broken contracts, not fairy politics. When an empire shows up with handcuffs, they never come for the scenery! Waluigi adjusted his purple sleeves and prepared to document every single contract violation they had committed since crossing the border. A military force that mistakes an elven research suite for a standard holding cell is doomed to get surprised by the local ecology! WAH!

sections.heading: The Quartermaster and the Shadow Writers
sections.body: WAH! Enter Quartermaster Cornburary, stepping into the quarters with a greasy smirk and zero visible combat equipment. Toad Lee eyed him up and down immediately: "Cornburary of the Legion... you don't have a weapon on you. Are you a combatant here like your guards?" Cornburary dared him to strike: "Is that a threat? Go ahead, hit me, see what happens." But when Toad Lee pressed for his actual function, Cornburary revealed the ultimate institutional insult. He called himself a journalist, then corrected himself: "A bookkeeper, an archivist even. A better one than your friend over there." He insulted Waluigi! To my face! In my own presence! Waluigi shouted: "WAH! I'll take you out!" And the man had the sheer audacity to boast: "I don't need to. I have a bunch of shadow writers that will do it for me." Shadow writers! Bureaucratic ghostwriters! Waluigi drew the Phase Spider gut tennis racket right there on the rug. I was prepared to volley a kinetic purple force orb straight through his ledger, but Toad Lee swiped at my racket and shouted: "Friendly fire! You're threatening my livelihood!" Toad Lee pleaded for restraint, pointing out that we were both banged up and asking: "Who will archive... uhhh, me when I'm gone or something?" Waluigi looked at him and said what had to be said: Waluigi will outlast everyone in this room! But Waluigi lowered the racket, because an archivist with real pride does not waste gut strings on a clerk who outsources his prose to SHADOW WRITERS. When Toad Lee asked if they were hunting Archie as well, they confirmed Archie was secondary. The entire IRON LEGION apparatus was pointed at our dwarf, and Cornburary was just the pencil-pusher sent to tally the bill! Waluigi remembers every single threat to his professional standing, and Cornburary just earned top billing in the docket! A man who hides behind ghostwriters is a man who cannot stand on his own sentences! Waluigi will personally challenge any shadow writer he employs to a public deposition in the capital! WAH!

sections.heading: Ravishing Tonight and the Soul Ring Proposal
sections.body: WAH! Meanwhile, upstairs in the false sanctuary, Hjumpik was executing the single most unhinged diplomatic maneuver in Midlands history. Lady Aurelia touched a satyr and reduced him to smoking ash right before his eyes. Hjumpik called it out: "It's a sham." And when she warned that this was her manor, Hjumpik fired back: "I'm Hjumpik, so ho ho ho, I'm not afraid, and this isn't my manor." She warned that with one touch he would be gone too. Did Hjumpik run? No! He dropped down onto one knee, held up the glowing soul ring, and delivered this legendary line: "You're right, I am proposing to you. Put on this ring, ignore everything I said before. You look ravishing tonight." Ravishing! She had vines crawling out of her sockets and ash on her dress! Aurelia smiled and produced a spiked ring designed to slowly devour his lifeforce: "In fey culture males put on the ring. We will be bound once you put it in. It will slowly suck your lifeforce." Hjumpik agreed that it was terrifying, asked if she would release the manor, and then jammed our soul ring straight onto her finger instead! The binding phrase echoed through the stones: "Yaoui Dhayemmn Dhwayelf!" The enchantment hit her like a siege engine. Her strength collapsed, but as she went down, her clawed fingers snagged Hjumpik's belt—and his pants fell straight to his ankles! Right at that precise second, the Colour Division guards burst through the doors: "WHAT THE? WITH THE LADY? WE CAUGHT YOU WITH YOUR PANTS DOWN!" The guards immediately promised it would be included in the official after-action report. And when Hjumpik dragged her toward the bathroom, the guards yelled: "NOW YOU'RE GOING TO THE BATHROOM WITH HER? GET BACK HERE!" Waluigi has filed hundreds of tactical engagements; this is the first one where the victory condition required an immediate belt adjustment! Hjumpik traded trousers for planar liberation, and Waluigi will never let him forget it! Waluigi will carve that quotation into the wall of the guild hall in gold leaf! When the history of the Midlands is written, the battle of the sanctuary will be remembered as the night a dwarf proposed with a soul ring and lost his drawers to a countess! WAH!

sections.heading: The Men in Silver and the Fungal Manual
sections.body: WAH! Downstairs, Toad Lee was flipping through the desk's elven volumes and stumbled upon the mechanics of Feywild climate control: "Mutsdoppms apnd yoput hopw mutsdoppms capn apffetct det fetywapdd" the book is said. That is: how emotions react with environmental fungus to warp the plane. Before he could finish reading, the door opened for the silver-plated arrival of the Cordon Combat Chirurgeon. "We are the CCC. We have to come eliminate the Feywild. With this solution we can simply inject the plants killing them." Toad Lee challenged their rationale immediately. When the CCC called the Feywild 'unpure,' Toad Lee demanded: "Define unpure." The answer from the silver mask was the purest piece of imperial arrogance I have ever heard: "Because we can." Toad Lee whispered to Waluigi to slip out the window and scout for surveillance probes. Waluigi gave him a knowing smile and slipped out into the vines, leaving Toad Lee to dismantle their ideology. When the CCC accidentally began admitting that the material plane was corrupted, Quartermaster Cornburary panicked: "Shut up, you! Too much information!" They started screaming at each other like angry scullions. Toad Lee pressed them on their heraldry and mentioned our yellow-clad allies feeding us coordinates. Waluigi was already outside enjoying the cool air, but the rhetorical fire inside that room was reaching critical mass. Toad Lee cornered their quartermaster with questions about their emblem, and Cornburary snarled: "You trying to get information from me? You won't, not even from that birdbrain over there." Waluigi takes offense at 'birdbrain,' even in absentia! But Toad Lee stood his ground like a veteran! The CCC brought chemical warfare to a fairy garden, and Toad Lee turned their own interrogation into a public exposure! Waluigi watched through the foliage as their pristine discipline melted into petty squabbling! When two invading officers start shouting over classified operational details in front of their own prisoners, Waluigi knows the mission is already falling apart! WAH!

sections.heading: Thunder, Hail, and the Emotional Wildfire
sections.body: WAH! Here is where Toad Lee proved that a furious Toad is more dangerous than an artillery battery. His temper snapped as he listened to these bureaucrats debate conquering living realms. And because the Feywild translates intense feeling directly into atmospheric phenomena, the room violently ignited! Thunder rattled the glass, hail smashed against the roof, and suddenly roots across the floor erupted into roaring sheets of flame—FIRE EVERYWHERE! Toad Lee shouted in amazement: "What the... woah, woah!" feeling the heat, and then exclaimed: "Huh, so it actually worked, holy heck!" He scooped up the elven books off the burning desk, saving the salvageable volumes while leaving others that were not entirely burnt. He dashed to the open window, noticed Waluigi had already departed, whispered "What the dang," and delivered a magnificent speech: "Listen man, the Feywild is not the type of place you want to set up shop outside of your imperialistic tendencies. Leave the Feywild alone! It has people living inside of it, they won't be happy when they find denizens invading on their own. Be warned!" And then he dived headfirst out the window into the burning shrubbery! That is how you exit an interrogation. No surrender, no written confessions—just an EMOTIONAL WILDFIRE, stolen elven research, and a clean swan dive into the fog. Waluigi watched from behind a hedge with immense appreciation. The IRON LEGION came to collect a dwarf, and instead they got their eyebrows singed by a botanical weather event fueled entirely by righteous indignation! When Toad Lee gets mad, the entire climate takes notice! Waluigi has witnessed many arcane spells, but weaponized moral outrage will always be my favourite form of area-of-effect damage! Never underestimate a fungus with an axe and an ideology! WAH!

sections.heading: The Ceiling Toss and Brad the Waiter
sections.body: WAH! While Toad Lee was burning down the west wing, Hjumpik was in the sanctuary bathroom conducting what can only be described as dwarven gymnastics. He tossed the unconscious Lady Aurelia through a hole in the ceiling, caught her on the rebound, thought the words "Princess carrying," tossed her again, and finally hammered her up to the second floor. Then he leaned over her face, and a white worm slithered right out of her eye socket! Horrifying! He cracked open a side door to escape, and who should be standing there but Brad the waiter! Hjumpik squinted: "Are you the waiter guy?" Brad has survived treants, poison soup, and the collapse of the house, and he immediately delivered the most comprehensive operational brief of the night. When Hjumpik asked why he sounded so down, Brad sighed: "This place is too chaotic. We have to stabilize it somehow." Then Brad revealed the whole enemy hierarchy: "Their commander, P.S., I think her name is, I don't know what it stands for. I think she's working with other legionnaires from the outside world. She is leading the Sunflower Division." The Sunflower Division! When Toad Lee's wildfire burst through the floorboards, Hjumpik shouted for water, scooped up Brad, charged through the blaze, used dwarven healing on his burns, and grunted: "Whatever, I'm out." Waluigi salutes Brad. A waiter who gathers military intelligence during a planar disaster is a professional of the highest order. While the nobility of the manor was getting possessed and roasted, Brad was quietly tracking foreign division names and exit routes. Waluigi would hire Brad for Disaster Inc. tomorrow if Wario would authorize the payroll! A waiter with that level of tactical awareness deserves a massive promotion and hazard pay! Waluigi will personally recommend him for campaign honors once we clear this ruin! In a mansion where nobles lose their minds, the serving staff keeps their heads and checks the fire exits! WAH!

sections.heading: The Mage of Ice Extinguishes the Flame
sections.body: WAH! Outside on the soggy lawn, Toad Lee was wandering through the brambles yelling my name at the top of his lungs: "WALUIGI!" Waluigi walked up behind him and tapped him firmly on the shoulder. When he asked why I ran off, I pointed at the burning manor and told him I wasn't sure who those people were. When he asked about the CCC probe, I explained that I waved it off and let it fly away. Then Toad Lee looked me in the eye and confessed that he caused the wildfire, but added that he refused to tell me how he did it! "Don't trust ME? How can I archive the answer to my million of fans?" Waluigi demanded. He told me: "Because knowing you, you will unleash chaos for the sake of it or for your interest." Hurtful! Completely accurate, but hurtful! Then we approached the threshold and found the corridor blocked by raging fire. Toad Lee asked how to extinguish it, and Waluigi delivered the immortal line: "They don't call me writer or ice." Toad Lee replied: "No worries, mage of ice, work your magic." Waluigi took one magnificent step into the blazing doorway, snapped the air, and every single tongue of fire died instantly! Toad Lee gasped: "Oh, you really did work your magic!" And Waluigi blinked in mild surprise before recovering his swagger: "Huh, I did... yeah, I did!" Waluigi graciously accepted the applause. A MAGE OF ICE never reveals his atmospheric secrets, especially when he isn't entirely sure how the room stopped burning! You call for ice, Waluigi delivers the freeze, and Disaster Inc. walks through the ashes without breaking a sweat! Waluigi will keep the title of Mage of Ice forever, and nobody at the table can contest the filing! A title won by walking through extinguished smoke is a title won for life! WAH!

sections.heading: Reunion and the Two-Story Drop
sections.body: WAH! We reunited with Hjumpik at the landing. Toad Lee didn't waste a single second on pleasantries: "Glad to see you back, we're reunited. Did you sell us out to the Legion for Aurelia?" Waluigi stayed completely quiet, letting the dwarf sweat under the cross-examination. Hjumpik stammered about the Legion trying to capture him, noticed our soot-stained faces, and explained the condition of the limp noblewoman in his arms: "Took the demon out of her. She tried to fight me, I got the demon out... yeah. Yeah, I knocked—I didn't, I had to exorcise her." Exorcism with a warhammer! Standard dwarven medical doctrine! Brad cut off the debate before it became violent: "Let's get a move on, you can talk while we move." He led us into the servant's common room. The floor was completely rotted away, with gaps opening onto a steep drop down to the library gangways a floor below, or straight to the ground floor for the unlucky. Walking across ancient joists while carrying an exorcised countess is what Disaster Inc. calls standard evening travel. Brad stepped onto a sound beam, reached up to an ancient bookshelf, and tilted a single volume. The entire shelf mechanism slid upward, and we stepped through into the secret dark in complete silence. Waluigi watched the floorboards creak beneath our boots and wondered how many generations of servants had used this secret flue to dodge the aristocracy! When an entire castle has floorboards rotting into a two-story void, finding a sliding bookshelf is the only piece of good luck we had seen all morning! Waluigi kept one hand on the wall and one hand on his notes, because falling through a floorboard ruins both your health and your penmanship! Disaster Inc. navigates collapsing estates with style or not at all! WAH!

sections.heading: The Goblin Card Room and the 21-Day Clock
sections.body: WAH! The bookcase opened into a room that looked like a library had detonated inside a compost bin. Giant mushrooms sprouted directly from piles of discarded books, and in the center of the mess sat a round table surrounded by surly goblins screaming over a filthy deck of cards. The wagers were magnificent: half-empty bottles of floor cleaner, rusty scrub brushes, and greasy waistcoats! This was the very table where Hjumpik played cards during his first arrival. Waluigi asked: "Are you sure this is a good idea?" When Toad Lee asked what the plan was for Lady Aurelia, Brad stated that he would handle it alone. Hjumpik scoffed that a push of wind would knock the waiter over, but Brad held firm. Brad reminded us: "The three beasts of the manor still live... the Bramblyfly, the Revel... it was a complete failure, wasn't it?" And then Brad looked Hjumpik in the eye and delivered the hardest truth of the war: "We won, but not the war." And then Brad leaned forward and dropped the heaviest hammer of the night: "I uhh eavesdropped earlier, you know that? They said they're cutting the Feywild in a few days right, or something? 21 days is that it... the end of the world." Twenty-one days! A hard planar deadline! The IRON LEGION isn't just collecting debt; they are preparing a planar guillotine! Hjumpik went silent: "Oh... I see." And Waluigi closed his notebook, because the clock on this entire dimension is officially running. Twenty-one days until the cut. Disaster Inc. has survived dragons, bank robberies, and haunted manors, but a three-week countdown to planar obliteration means every single minute from here on is going to cost double! The curtain is coming down, and Waluigi has twenty-one days to get everyone out alive! Waluigi will make sure every second of those three weeks is logged in full ink! When an entire plane gets an expiration date, you do not argue with the calendar—you pack your gear and write fast! WAH!

commentaries.title: The Box at the Cottage Door
commentaries.subtitle: Waluigi's Cut — eight hours counted, a girl delivered in a parcel, a fountain that skipped the drumroll, and a ship that was not theirs anymore
commentaries.filed: 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — the next morning, from the screening desk, by someone who was not in the cottage
commentaries.pullQuote: THEY'RE WEARING RAGS. That is the identification method. Waluigi has never once thought to identify an army by the quality of its laundry, and it works.
commentaries.standfirst: The tape is a box of grey footage from a cottage, a fountain and a town, and Waluigi has the projector warm, the lights down and his hand on the pause button. Contains: a delivery for a centaur, a girl in a crate who would like it known she may have sleepwalked, an oracle nobody can explain, a ritual with no drumroll, a guard who is just a bit twitchy, a bar worth fifty gold sold for fifteen, and an army identified by its rags.

sections.heading: STOP THE TAPE: THE PARTY IS ABOUT TO TAKE EIGHT HOURS OFF
sections.body:
Waluigi has the projector warm and the lights down and a bowl of gold coins in his lap, and he would like it understood that he was NOT in that cottage. Waluigi was somewhere with a roof that did not have a hedge maze at the back of it. ROLL it.

The tape opens on Tymnas's door. Five worn-out people go in through it, and the first thing they do with their evening is **loot all the bodies**. EVERY one. Ettercaps, spiders, whatever else the grove had left on the ground. Waluigi wants a moment of silence for the sheer *bookkeeping* of it: these are people who have just come in out of the dark and their first act, on dry floor, is inventory. The table even asked for it to go on their sheets. *Please.* They said *please.* WAH.

Then they rest. Eight hours. The table said, in these words, that **those eight counted**, and Waluigi has watched a GREAT many parties lie down in a GREAT many cottages and not once has one of them felt the need to tell the camera that the nap was legitimate. Nobody asked, friend. NOBODY asked. Pause the tape. Waluigi would like the part of the audience that is not holding a pillow to notice who is protesting too much.

Now watch the corner of the screen, because here is the thing the nap cost them. While they slept, the fire **finally reaches the stub of the tree**. That's the stump. THE stump, the one the whole plan was built around. It burns down. The exit is gone.

And the table says it in ONE flat sentence and moves on. Waluigi would have had a paragraph. Waluigi would have had a BAND. Instead: *the exit is gone,* and then somebody rolled over, and the hearth went on being warm, and a way out of the Shadowfell turned into ash while five people breathed through their mouths.

Waluigi is not saying that the nap was the mistake. Waluigi is saying that the way out of the Shadowfell was burned shut by a fire, and that Waluigi would very much like to know who lit it.

sections.heading: A KNOCK, A WINDOW, AND A MAN WHO WILL NOT SAY WHO SENT HIM
sections.body:
Okay. Rewind. No. Forward. *FORWARD.* Waluigi has found the part where somebody knocks.

Somebody knocks, and a voice outside says it is a **delivery for Markop**. Waluigi would like the ROOM to hold that sentence up to the light. A delivery. For a centaur. In the Shadowfell. At the cottage of a groundskeeper who has lost track of what day it is. Who orders a parcel into a dimension of ash? WHO?

Markop, bless him, does not go to the door. He goes to the **window**, which is the FIRST sensible decision anybody has made on this tape, and looks out. On the step is Green T, holding a box.

"Where were you, Green T?"

"I was getting backup. Then you guys left without me and I couldn't go through with my plan."

Waluigi is going to need the tape stopped. Freeze it on Green T's face. *Then you guys left without me.* He is BLAMING them. ALL of them. They went off and did the dangerous thing and he is hurt that nobody waited while he went to find backup. That is NOT a plan. That is a man who has been left at a party and is explaining that it was a good party.

"What plan?"

"The plan was to escape and destroy the grove for good. I was gathering fey to help. The plan didn't work when no one showed up."

*No one showed up.* Waluigi has thrown parties like this. Waluigi has sent out invitations and printed a banner and watched nobody show up to a plan to destroy a grove for good.

"You're friends with fey," Markop said.

"You mean fairies," said Archie.

"I'm not friends with fey. They're friends with money."

PAUSE IT. Waluigi wants that on a plaque. *They're friends with money.* It is the best thing anyone has said about the entire Feywild and it was said by a man standing on a step holding a box. And then, without a breath: "Either way, I've got a delivery from you." From who? "A friend. An associate of the Green Tea Syndicate."

And here Archie, who is holding the line of **"I thought I destroyed them. They're all de—"** and stops. Dead in the middle of *dead.* Waluigi has seen men stop mid-word before and it is usually because somebody hit them. Archie did it to himself. WAH.

sections.heading: THE BOX HAS A GIRL IN IT (A GIRL YOU HAVE ALL MET)
sections.body:
"Who are these friends of yours, Green T?"

"Check the box."

That is the WHOLE answer and Waluigi would like to point out that **it is NOT an answer**. It is a BOX. He has been asked who his friends are and he has changed the subject to a parcel. Archie, a TRUSTING man, opens the door, takes the box, notes that it is kind of heavy, decides that it seems fine, and carries it inside. Waluigi has NO further questions about why this party keeps getting ambushed.

Markop undoes the lid. And Waluigi was told that the footage was good but he was not told it was *this* good, because the box has **Remi** in it. Asleep. In a box. On a step. Delivered by a man from a criminal syndicate.

She wakes to a horse's face over her own and the first words out of her mouth are *"A— how did I get here?"*

HOW. Waluigi would like to know HOW. Nobody in that room can say where she was. She is simply back, rested, with a parcel's worth of luggage.

Archie, thrilled, asks where Wario is. "Where's that Misley?" Remi's answer, delivered with the calm of someone who has been asleep for the entire plot, is **"Don't worry about it."** Don't worry about it. They were going back to the tree to help her! Markop says so, out loud, to her face! And the answer is *don't worry about it.*

"I could use a nap," says Remi, and curls up in the box.

"You were just resting. Get up."

And Markop picks her up by the **scruff**, Waluigi is NOT making that up, the tape is RIGHT there, and sets her on the floor like a cat that has got into the laundry. "Thanks for saving her," Archie tells the window, because Green T is already gone from the frame.

Waluigi would like the audience to enjoy that moment, because *it is the last thing in this tape that is nice.*

sections.heading: KILL THE ORACLE (ARCHIE DOES NOT REMEMBER WHY)
sections.body:
"How did I even get there?" Remi says. "Oh — well. Doesn't matter. Maybe I sleepwalked."

SLEEPWALKED. Into a box. Across a dimension. Onto a doorstep. Waluigi will tell you that **nobody sleepwalks in a place with ettercaps in it**, because that is the sort of place where if you sleepwalk, something with more legs than you ends up doing the walking.

Eager, God love him, has the only correct response. "Are you sure? There were ettercaps swimming around."

"I'm not sure. But I'm here now."

*I'm not sure, but I'm here now.* PUT that on the family crest. Waluigi would like that carved above the door of every building Remi has ever walked out of.

Then Eager asks the question the whole tape has been circling. "What's our plan going forward? Everyone's safe. We killed the Scorncrow."

"I don't know," says Markop.

And here Archie comes in with the SINGLE most alarming sentence of the evening. "I want to kill the oracle. Based on a conversation I had. We kill it or we're stuck here forever."

A *conversation.* Waluigi has to stop the tape. What conversation? With who? When? Markop asks him exactly that, in the mildest possible way: there's the tree route they found, there's the ritual with Green T, why the oracle? And Archie delivers, with absolute sincerity: **"I don't remember the conversation, but I know that if I don't kill the oracle I may never leave here."**

READ that again. Waluigi will WAIT. He does not remember the conversation. He remembers the *conclusion.*

"Why?"

"The person who ordered the condition is a jerk."

*The jerk.* Waluigi is delighted. He does not know who. He does not know what. He knows that whoever it was, they were a jerk.

"Archie," says Markop, who has had a long night, "you left this dimension about eight hours ago."

"Oh. I thought it was days ago."

Eight hours, Archie. EIGHT. Waluigi has had LONGER lunches.

sections.heading: THE MIDNIGHT FOUNTAIN, AND THE THREE PEOPLE NOBODY MENTIONED
sections.body:
So they pick the ritual. Archie says it, Markop says *I guess we're doing the ritual then,* and then, because the tape has not yet exhausted its supply of absurdity, **Remi volunteers to lead it.**

"Why?" Markop asks.

"Because of adventure."

BECAUSE OF ADVENTURE. Waluigi would like the minutes of the meeting to record that this is a COMPLETE sentence, that it was accepted as a reason, and that the person giving it had been in a box fifteen minutes earlier. Then a beat, and then Remi, in a small voice: "Shouldn't Green T be up front?"

He should. He is. It is Green T who walks the ring of the Midnight Fountain lighting the candles, one by one, because it was ALWAYS going to be him, because everybody else in this tape is too busy having opinions.

And then. THEN. *A beam comes down from the heavens.* No warning. No flare. No fanfare, no choir, no little drumroll from the sky. Waluigi has been to rituals. There is **ALWAYS** a drumroll. This one is a straight line of light and a VERY short walk.

They come out at the ruined manor.

"We can leave," somebody says. "We can go home."

Waluigi feels something. He does not enjoy it. He would like it noted that he is a professional.

"Let's go to a town for now and get our bearings," says Archie.

"That sounds like a great idea," says Remi.

"Alright," says Markop.

"They're looking for me here," Archie adds. "Let's go."

And that is it. That is the whole farewell. Waluigi has the tape and the tape is *right there* and it will tell you what Waluigi will tell you: **Bones, Hjumpik and Toad Lee were all left behind in the Shadowfell, and not one person at that fountain said a word.** Not a word. Waluigi is going to have to say it for them. Somebody should. WAH.

sections.heading: NOT ANYMORE (A GUARD WITH A BATON, A DOCTOR WITH A SAW)
sections.body:
Out they walk. And what is the first thing they see in the Material world? THE SHIP. Waluigi's ship. The Vigilance, which an honest man would still call the Vigilance, moored where they left it, with a guard on the gangway.

Does the party creep? Does the party hang back and assess? No. **Remi runs straight at him.**

"HEY! WHAT'S YOUR NAME?"

"What's yours?" the guard asks.

"Remi."

"Remi. That sounds familiar. Are you on the wanted list?"

Waluigi would like the audience to enjoy the fact that Remi has ANSWERED the question. *Remi.* She told a Legion guard her name. At the door of a Legion ship. Because he asked.

"What's your name, sir?"

"Mr. Shock."

"Shock who — woah."

And the baton goes by. Waluigi has PAUSED it on the swing. LOOK at the baton. LOOK at the girl who is no longer where the baton was. That is a person who was asleep in a crate this morning and has retained ALL of her reflexes. "Why did you do that? It wasn't very nice. How could you be not nice, Mr. Shock?"

"Well, I'm sorry. I'm just a bit twitchy."

*A bit twitchy.* He is holding a shock baton. Waluigi would like the audience to hold those two facts in separate hands.

"Yes. If anyone passes this threshold, they'd end up in custody."

"Whose custody?"

"The Legion's. This is the Legionlance — our top-of-the-line airship."

"Wait. But this is our airship."

"Not anymore."

**NOT ANYMORE.** Waluigi has a great deal to say about that and has decided to say it later, in a quiet room, to a pillow.

Then Markop swings. The tape cuts before it lands, which is a mercy. And then: "Come over here, sir. This one's rowdy," and out from behind the guard comes a medieval doctor holding **a bone saw**. "Yes — what's the problem, sir? Do you need medicine?" "He hurt my friend." "Come here, little one." And a Toad on the gangway adds, helpfully, **"You're going to the glue factory."**

Remi runs TOWARD the doctor. Markop catches her by the hand. "Nooo," she says, all the way down. And Green T, outside the gate, as they go by: "You have such a way with words."

sections.heading: SMILE, THERE'S AN EXECUTION: THE SHOP, THE BAR, AND THE EARRING
sections.body:
Into town. A guard stops them. "What are you guys doing out so early?"

"Long story short, we found this town nearby and thought we could stay for a few."

"Oh, that's great. Just put on a smile while you're here. The top legionnaire, Kyle Coinsoul, is coming."

"So in other words he owns all the stores here," says Archie.

"No, no, no. Kyle Coinsoul is being killed. An execution, if you will. He stole. And the top legionnaire, Commander G, will be overseeing it."

PAUSE. *If you will.* Waluigi has been to funerals with less polish. Waluigi would like to notice, quietly, that Kyle Coinsoul has been called a TOP LEGIONNAIRE by a man who is about to watch him die, which is a promotion with a very short career.

Markop asks for binoculars. He gets directions. Over there. And that is how the entire party ends up in a shop, where Waluigi's whole day goes to ruin in the best possible way.

Remi, going through her inventory for things to sell: "Brain juice? When did I have brain juice?" WHEN, REMI. Waluigi has the magnifying glass priced at a hundred gold. Remi has twenty-five. So she sells. Her ink goes for **two bronze**. Her bullet casings, the ones that almost killed the orange heir, go for **sixty-five gold**. A coupon from Angel 24: five. A book on plant identification: fifteen.

Then Archie asks what the ink she just sold would cost. "Ten gold." He buys it. He buys the entertainer's pack, the diplomat's pack, a crossbow case and a candle. And Remi watches him pay ten gold for her ink and says, with the dignity of a woman watching her own umbrella walk out in a stranger's hand, **"Wow."**

Then Archie sells a bar of gold. The shop offers him fifteen. It is worth FIFTY.

"What?" says Eager. "Someone please interject. Someone, please."

Nobody does. Waluigi counted. It was a full pause, on the tape, with Eager's hand in the air. And then **Dan** steps up: "I've got it." Fifteen for the bar. "How much if we give you this earring?" Sixteen. Fifteen and sixteen is thirty-one gold, and Waluigi would like to state for the room that thirty-one is a number, that it is *eighteen short* of what the bar alone was worth, and that he will carry this to his grave.

Alright. Waluigi will concede one thing. The shop was not wrong that nobody else was buying. WAH.

sections.heading: THROUGH THE GLASS: THE ROUT, THE RAGS, AND DOCTOR RUDY
sections.body:
And meanwhile Markop has the binoculars. He lifts them. He points them at the ship. And here is the part Waluigi has been waiting to show you, so WATCH.

On the deck, two people lying on the floor, the two from earlier. And over the rail, up the gangway, a flood of **Toads**. They are storming the ship. A flag goes up. A trumpet sounds, a horn answers it, and somebody, somewhere in that mass of mushroom caps, shouts **"CHARGE."**

"Liberated Toads, or loyalists?" asks Eager.

"They're wearing rags," says Archie. "They're our group."

THEY'RE WEARING RAGS. *That* is the identification method. Waluigi has been at this for years and has never once thought to identify an army by the quality of its laundry, but it works, and it works because it is the SINGLE most Liberated Toads thing that has ever been true. Waluigi is on the edge of his seat. Waluigi's ship is being stormed by people in rags and Waluigi is not even in the picture. WAH.

And then, because it is that kind of morning, Dan turns back to the shopkeeper before they leave. "Do you know a guy who can make us prosthetic arms? I lost my arm. I was wondering if there's someone in this town."

"Hmm. There might be one person."

"What's the rumour?"

"They're very hands on with their prosthetics."

"What do you mean by that?"

"They like to do it while the person's awake."

Waluigi would like the audience to read that again. Slowly. In the voice of a man who has just been offered a very good deal.

"Is there a reason for that?"

"Not sure."

*Not sure.* And Dan does not ask again. "We'll keep it in mind. Who's the person who can give us the arm?"

"Their name is Rudy Lee."

"Doctor Rudy," says Dan. "Got it."

CUT the tape. Waluigi is going to sit here for a minute with the lights off and think about the fact that a one-armed paladin has just been given the name of a man who prefers his patients awake and that **the answer was *got it.***

Waluigi has seen worse mornings. He is not going to name one. WAH.

commentaries.title: Just Walk By My Side
commentaries.subtitle: In Which Waluigi Grades A Man's Accent, A Palace's Hospitality, And Everyone's Alibi, And Lights One Small Candle
commentaries.standfirst: Jimmy Dobson walked into a gold country with a button in his pocket, explained the plan to a king, did an accent at a palace, lied badly to a plumber made of memory and climbed into a cannon, and asked to be taken back out. I have a lot of feelings, most of them at his expense. The grown-up version of this is on the analysis page. This is the loud one.
commentaries.pullQuote: A man who tells you he is lost while holding a detonator is not lost. He is early.
commentaries.filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — filed late; the day it describes is 20 Harvestide (estimated hour)

sections.heading: 'I've Been Lost Here For Ages,' Said The Man With The Detonator
sections.body:
Let me set the scene. A stranger in a red cap opens his arms on a gold road and says **"Youve-a wondered far from home"** and Jimmy Dobson answers **"oh thank god I've been lost here for ages."**

Thank GOD. Ages. Look at him. Look at the little crinkle of relief. I almost bought it, and I have SOLD that exact line to a border guard.

He was not lost. He had a button in his pocket and a Koopa assault on a timer. **That is not lost. That is a delivery.** Lost people don't know what time anything is going to blow up.

And the HOST. I need to talk about the host. His whole opening is a rhyme, and the rhyme is **"through my veneer your never a-lone."** *Your* never alone. YOUR. It is *you're*. The most dangerous thing in the Mushroom Kingdom is a man with a thousand-year smile and a grammar problem, and nobody in this file has corrected him, so I am doing it now, in the permanent record: **you're**. Two words. One apostrophe. It is a contraction.

*WAH! He also said 'no benevolence' in the first minute, which is the most honest sentence in the document. Jimmy heard it the way you hear the safety announcement on a plane.*

sections.heading: Okay, Letsa Go
sections.body:
At the crucial moment, Jimmy takes the button out, looks at it, looks at the palace, and says, in the host's own accent: **"okay letsa go."**

Reader, I sat with that for a full minute.

A man walking into a gold palace to detonate a monarchy decides to do it **in an impression**. He had two hours of free character development on that road and he used it to learn the voice. It is the bravest and stupidest thing in the file until the cannon, and the cannon is a long way off, so give it some respect.

Here is what I think happened. Jimmy was frightened, so Jimmy got rude. Jimmy was very frightened, so Jimmy got funny. Jimmy was more frightened than THAT, so Jimmy did an *accent*. It is the third stage of grief. It comes after bargaining and before pizza.

I have done the impression of an enemy to myself in a mirror. I did it for TENNIS. I was not walking into a palace. Jimmy: respect, and also **no**.

sections.heading: Reviewing The Hospitality: One Star, Would Not Be Eaten Again
sections.body:
I have stayed in worse places. I have stayed in nothing places. But I have never read a hospitality sheet where the host *promises* four things and delivers *one*, and the one is the King.

**Dining halls** — promised. Not seen.
**Gardens** — promised. Not seen.
**The good room for sleeping** — promised, with a wink. Not seen. I would like the wink back.
**The King** — delivered, immediately, at the top of a staircase that starts ringing doorbells BY ITSELF.

Notes from the guest book:

- *The gate lowers itself and groans like gold grinding on gold.* Fine. Dramatic. Two stars for the entrance.
- *The courtyard doors close behind you with a finality that echoes.* Minus one star, I wasn't consulted.
- *The torches have no visible fuel.* Minus the other one. Whoever's paying that gas bill is not a person.
- *The host walks faster the higher you climb.* That is not a tour. That is a cart being pushed up a ramp.

**Final rating: one star for the shine. Do not stay. Do not eat the creatures. They snap their beaks at you when you refuse to play, and Jimmy refused, and he was RIGHT.**

sections.heading: He Explained The Plan To The King's Face
sections.body:
Okay. THE BUTTON.

The King asks, in a voice you feel in your sternum, **"MARIO... IS THIS THE TRAVELER YOU PROMISED?"** And Jimmy, who has been squeezing a pocket for two hours like it owes him money, presses it. In the room. In the throne room. In the **ROOM**.

And then he *explains*. Out loud. To the host who is trying to stop him. **"Oh I know and its planned, the koopa troops are coming."**

That is not a plan. That is a monologue. In every heist film in the archive, the guy with the button presses it in a *different building* and then walks away looking at his watch. Jimmy pressed it standing in front of the target, and then read out the next three steps like a flight attendant.

*WAH! I would like to say I would have done it better. I would have pressed it from the roof. With a hat on. With the receipt.*

And then, I swear to you, the roof opens on cue. Bowser drops in on a Koopa car. Paratroopas fall. Hammer Bros line the rafters. The King calls it treason and a stain, in that order. The host screams **"That's not-a how this works!"**

Mario, buddy. This is EXACTLY how it works. You are the one who put a king on a throne in a building with a roof that opens.

sections.heading: Everyone Brought A Different Party
sections.body:
My favourite detail in the whole raid is that the invasion has no theme.

Bowser: **"GO FOR THE KING!"**
The troopers: **"RAID THE TREASURY!"**
The squad leaders: **"We're on official business!"** (There is a bomb.)
The King: **"BEGONE FROM MY SIGHT!"**
Jimmy: **"its planned."**

Five people, five reasons, and ONE roof. It is a wedding where everyone thinks they are the bride. The hammer bros threw hammers. Somebody, probably Bowser, got hit by his own side's hammers and swore at them. The troopers wanted GOLD. That is the one honest line: *RAID THE TREASURY.* Pure. Uncomplicated. The only soldier in that building who knew exactly why he got out of bed.

I am a professional and I would like to say that this is not how you run a raid. A raid is a schedule with a grudge. This was a **group chat**.

*WAH! Bowser said later that he 'missed a few pieces from the briefing.' A king of the Koopas who did not READ HIS BRIEFING. I have never been so comforted and so alarmed in the same breath.*

sections.heading: 'Uhh No.'
sections.body:
The host turns to Jimmy in the middle of a collapsing palace and asks, with a bomb going off at his back door, **"DID YOU-A DO THIS?"**

And Jimmy says: **"uhh no."**

I need everyone to appreciate how much work *uhh* is doing. It is a single syllable of pure panic, and it is aimed at a man he PRESSED A BUTTON NEXT TO four minutes ago and then SAID OUT LOUD that he did it.

I have forged forty documents. I have lied to a notary while the notary was on fire. I know what a good lie looks like, and it looks like **boredom**. A good lie is delivered like a bus timetable. Jimmy delivered his like a man who has just been asked, in front of his mother, whether he took the last biscuit, and has crumbs on his shirt.

And it WORKED. The host stares for one suspicious heartbeat and then a tremor shakes the floor and bails him out. Jimmy owes the earthquake dinner.

sections.heading: Why Are You Black And White (Asked In A Tunnel, During A Bombing)
sections.body:
Two hours. Two HOURS of walking next to a man in grey, through a country made of gold, and *then* Jimmy goes: **"Mario, I've never asked this, but why are you black and white?"**

In a tunnel. During a collapse. After a bomb. Right when the man is trying to save him.

I love him. I'm sorry. I love him. It is the least tactical question ever asked, and the question every single one of us was already screaming at the page. I screamed it at the *courtyard*. Jimmy waited for the **fire**.

And the host, bless him, answers properly. **"It's-a because this place isn't real."** Then: **"The colors only happen for those who belong in-a the frame."** Then, when Jimmy asks if he's really Mario, the line that made me put the pen down: **"Mario is... well, Mario is a memory."**

Same. I am a memory. I am a memory of a tennis victory nobody gave me. Somewhere in the Mushroom Kingdom there is a podium with my name carved into its absence, and I think about it every day.

*WAH! Evil Mario is an actor. Director Mario is a boss. This Mario is a memory in a cap. The file has three Marios and not one of them is employed by a person who brought a lunch.*

sections.heading: 'I Am On Your Side, Dumbass'
sections.body:
I have to give Jimmy credit, and it is going to cost me, so let me do it quickly.

In the middle of a collapse, he hears a Koopa Troopa crying under a ceiling, and he goes *back*. Nobody asked him. The trooper doesn't know him. The trooper is part of the army he came to help burn a building down. And Jimmy grabs him by the shell, and hauls, and when the trooper screams **"Get your hands off me, civilian!"** he pulls out the badge and says the single most affectionate insult in the archive:

**"I am on your side dumbass."**

That's it. That's the entire speech. A rescue that sounds like a mugging. The trooper, I note, is also not grateful. He says **"watch the shell! Damn it, watch the shell!"** while being saved from DEATH. They deserve each other. If they ever meet again I would like to be in the room with a camera and a plate of crisps.

*WAH! The badge worked. It worked on a soldier who had never been told there was an extraction. So either the badge is real and nobody read the memo, or the memo is real and nobody printed the badge. Both of those are Bowser.*

sections.heading: He Climbed Into The Cannon, And Then He Wanted Out
sections.body:
We have reached the cannon.

Jimmy takes the cannonball. It is made of ink. The cannon is made of ink. The sky is ink. The monster is *definitely* ink. And Jimmy decides the correct response to an ink monster is to **climb into an ink cannon with an ink ball and be fired at it.**

Let me give you Jimmy's whole sequence of sentences, in order, as filed:

1. *"I'll put an end to this."*
2. *"I climb into the cannon with the cannonball."*
3. *"oof, this was a bad idea."*
4. *"okay this is a bad idea put me back out put me back out aaaa"*

There. That is a man's whole character arc in under ten seconds. Confidence, commitment, regret, begging. It is the plot of every New Year's resolution I have ever made.

The monster, who has been waiting two hours for someone dramatic, says **"THE PROTAGONIST ALWAYS LOSES IN THE END!"** Excellent line. Villain's pick. Seven out of ten, docked three for 'granite teeth' being a reach. And then Jimmy sinks into a throat made of charcoal and the thing says **"OOOH... THAT TICKLES!"**

*WAH! I have been swallowed once, by a Chain Chomp, in a sponsored segment. I did not get a line. I got an invoice.*

sections.heading: And The Sentence The Roof Ate
sections.body:
One tiny serious thing, and then I'll go back to being unbearable.

In the throne room, the King shouting treason, Jimmy tries to say: **"after Peach's deat—"**

And the roof opens before he gets to the *h*.

I want that sentence. I want it more than I want the podium. I would trade a tennis trophy for the *rest of that clause.* Jimmy knew something about what came after Peach, he was going to say it to a king and a Koopa in the same breath, and a roof said **no**.

If you are keeping score: the most important thing anyone said all afternoon was interrupted by **architecture**.

sections.heading: Waluigi's Scorecard For Jimmy Dobson
sections.body:
Out of ten, in no particular order, with the reasoning left in the margins where it belongs:

**Courage — 9.** Climbed into a cannon. Docked one because he asked to come out.
**Planning — 2.** Told the plan to the King. Also did not know the plan.
**Accent — 4.** An impression, held for one sentence, with a stable lisp on 'letsa'.
**Lying — 1.** *Uhh no.* Next.
**Compassion — 8.** He went back for the trooper. He called him a dumbass. It still counts.
**Curiosity — 10.** He asked why the plumber was black and white. It took two hours. It was perfect.
**Survival — unknown.** He is in the mouth.

**Overall: 6.** Would not hire. Would send a card.

And a candle. A small one. I do not give candles lightly; I have a *Rule*. But there is a man in a mouth made of charcoal, holding a cannonball made of ink, who said *put me back out*, and in all my years of filing the stupidest people in the Mushroom Kingdom, that is the first time one of them has said *I would like to go back.* That is a human being. That is the only part of the whole account that I believed.

*WAH! If anyone finds him, please do not tell me. I would rather keep the candle.*

commentaries.title: The TOADALNAEC and the Three Lies
commentaries.subtitle: Waluigi's Cut — a free mask, a ship with two names, a gold handshake, three lies on a scorecard, one 'oopsie' and a speaker who left his hands in his pockets
commentaries.filed: 2 Aethel, 1040 BF — the morning after, from the screening desk, by someone who was not on the ship
commentaries.pullQuote: 'Get away from me, you filth animal. Surround her. Oh, oopsie.' OOPSIE. Waluigi has been keeping that for the encore.
commentaries.standfirst: The tape is a shop, a gangway, a song and a hall, and Waluigi has the projector warm and his hand on the pause button. Contains: a free mask from a shop that pays a third, a boat with the same layout and a different name, a toad who asked a stranger if she was solid, a recruitment song with a bullet in it, three lies recited from a lesson plan, a speaker who put his hands in his pockets to prove he had used them, a tea service, a truth spell, and a duel the crowd walked out of.

sections.heading: STOP THE TAPE: THE SHOP IS GIVING SOMETHING AWAY
sections.body:
Waluigi has the projector warm and the lights down, and the first thing on the reel is a counter. WAH. A SHOP counter. The same shop that, this very morning, looked at a bar of gold worth fifty and said *fifteen.* The same shopkeeper. The same face. And on this tape that same face comes out from behind the counter and says, to Remi, with NO prompting, **"I have an adventure mask for you, and it's free."**

Freeze it. Waluigi would like the room to look at the shopkeeper's hands. He is giving a thing away. This is a man who pays a third of what anything is worth and then charges you for the third.

Remi's response is, and Waluigi will defend this to anyone, a perfect piece of consumer behaviour. **"For free? It does sound interesting. For free."** *For free.* She said it twice. She said it the way a person says a word they have never been permitted to use.

He hands it over. The tape describes it as *gloomy.* That is the whole description. Not cursed, not old, not ominous. Gloomy, like a Tuesday. And Remi, who has just turned a mask over once in her hands, says the most sensible thing anybody says all afternoon: **"I won't wear it. Maybe the toads will."**

Roll it on.

Waluigi would like to log a formal complaint on behalf of the toads. Nobody asked the toads. The mask was offered to a person and passed to a *species,* and the species was not in the room. WAH. Green T, from the door, delivers the line that every one of these parties needs and none of them has ever kept: **"I better supervise them."**

He did not supervise them. Keep watching.

sections.heading: "IT MAY BE THE SAME LAYOUT": A DISPUTE OVER A BOAT
sections.body:
The party walks up to the old Vigilance singing, which is the correct way to approach a boat you used to own, and a gate toad puts his hand up.

Waluigi has been through a LOT of gates. Legion gates, baton gates, a gate with a doctor on it holding a bone saw. This is the first one guarded by a toad who has been briefed on the *legal position,* and WAH, it is magnificent.

**"Us. The owners of the airship."**

**"That's not right."**

**"What do you mean it's ours?"**

**"No, no, no, no. This is the TOADS' airship. The TOADALNAEC. It belongs to Speaker Rivers."**

Now Waluigi has been saying that word for an hour. TOADALNAEC. It does not scan. It is nine syllables of somebody running out of ship. The Legion called it the Legionlance, which was already a crime against the language, and the Toads took one look and said *we can do worse,* and they were RIGHT.

Pause the tape on the next line, because it is the best line in the filing and nobody on the tape knows it. **"No, no, it may be the same layout, but I assure you it's ours."**

THE SAME LAYOUT. They are not arguing about whether it is the Vigilance. Both sides have agreed it is the Vigilance. They have agreed on the hull, the gangway, the rails and the smell. The only open question is the *name on the door,* and the gate toad answers it the way every bureaucrat in this archive answers every question: **"Come on out, Hudston. We have a problem."**

He sent for HUDSTON. WAH.

sections.heading: GOLD OR GOLD-PLATED: THE HANDSHAKE THAT BECAME A TRADITION
sections.body:
Hudston walks out and the first thing he says to a stranger on his deck is **"Wow, are you gold or gold-plated?"**

That is a toad with no sense of occasion. Waluigi has been in the same room as very senior people and has never once asked one if they were solid.

Remi's answer is the best deflection on the reel. **"Come and find out for yourself."** She holds out a hand. He shakes it. He is gold.

*GOLD.* From the palm up. He looks at himself, he turns to the gangway and he announces, with real joy, **"Hey, guys, check it out. I'm gold now."** Green T's contribution is to ask him to stand against a wall and fire a gun at him. WAH. The bullet bounces off. Hudston's review of the experience: **"How can I ever repay you? It kinda stung, but it's really fun."**

Four stars. *Would be shot again.* And Green T shoots again, because Green T is a professional and a second sample is good practice.

Now the toads on the gangway, who have been watching this with the faces of men at a magic show, say the sentence that opens the second half of the tape: **"You're one of the toads now."**

Remi starts singing. **"Oh, I'm the new toad, listen to me, I'll sing a song in the air or the sea."** The toads sing it back. They pick her UP. It is the only recruitment ceremony Waluigi has ever approved of, because it contains a gold toad, a bullet, and a chorus.

And the tape shows the Disaster Inc. toads running after her to *save* her. She is being carried on shoulders, singing. She does not need saving. Rank it: Remi, 10. Rescue party, 2.

sections.heading: THE SCORECARD: THE THREE LIES OF ARCHIE MISER, GRADED
sections.body:
Waluigi has the pen out. A hall of toads has produced a lesson plan and the lesson plan has numbers on it. Grade it.

**Lie one: "He saved the toads."** The correction, from the crowd: *No, he put them back in their place, to be cogs in the machine.* Grade: C. It has the structure of an argument, it has a tone of righteous anger, and it comes from a hall full of toads who are standing up, unchained, in a flying ship. WAH.

**Lie two: "Archie Miser is a sane individual."** The correction: *False. He burnt down a village full of orphans.* And Archie, from a barrel, answers it in the best line of the afternoon: **"I do have flaws, but the village never happened. On remembering, it was someone else."** Grade: A for the denial and F for the denial, simultaneously. Waluigi will be thinking about *on remembering* for a week.

**Lie three: "Anything Archie says is a lie."** Grade: A+. It is the cleverest thing in the hall, because it disqualifies the answer to lies one and two before the answer is given. A man cannot rebut it. He can only say *that's a lie,* and then it is proved. WAH. Somebody in that ship went to school.

And then Markop pokes the one hole in the whole programme, which is **"Why isn't he fireballing us right now?"** The answer, from Rivers: **"Because he is scared of me."** Archie, from the barrel, with a barrel's gravity: **"This is the first time I've met you. You don't scare me at all."**

Then the one serious beat on the tape. **"I need to understand why you hate me. I saved you guys, all 150 of you. So why?"**

Nobody answers him. WAH.

sections.heading: OOPSIE, AND THE HANDS IN THE POCKETS
sections.body:
Archie says **"Take it away, Remi,"** which is a deeply optimistic thing to say to Remi, who responds with **"I'm not sure why Archie is evil, but why not?"** and goes for a high five. UP HIGH. Rivers dodges it.

And then the line. The line Waluigi has been keeping for the encore. **"Get away from me, you filth animal. Surround her. Oh, oopsie."**

*OOPSIE.* He said *filth animal* to a girl standing in a hall full of his own recruits, and the whole hall heard him say it, and in the half a second between the insult and the *oopsie,* the whole hall heard what the Speaker calls them when he thinks they cannot hear. Markop, to his eternal credit, does the thing: **"You guys want to be called that?"** WAH. The toads pause.

Now watch the follow-up, because Markop has found the thread and pulls it. **"Did anyone actually see Speaker Rivers fight?"** **"Yeah, I fought. Killed them with my bare hands."** He puts his hands in his pockets.

*In his pockets.* Waluigi has seen a great many liars and not one of them has ever hidden the evidence by *leaving it in his trousers.*

**"Let me see your hands. They should be bruised and bloodied."** Nothing. **"Out of your pockets."** He does a fake trip. He lands on the floor. He comes up showing both palms. **"See? My hands are dirty. Dirt and dust."**

**"I said bruised and bloodied."**

And then his best defence. **"I personally unchained you guys."** **"Does anyone remember being unchained by him?"** **"The metaphorical chains."** And a toad, in the crowd, says: **"Makes sense."**

Waluigi had no reply to that either.

sections.heading: THE TEA SERVICE AND THE SPELL THAT WORKED ON THE WRONG TOAD
sections.body:
Rivers is *tired.* He needs to be carried. He is lifted onto toad shoulders, like a man in a procession, and somebody says **"Your tea's ready, sir."** Markop, who has his suspicions about the cup, asks the question: **"That's not a potion, is it?"** **"No, no. Just tea."**

Then Markop opens his spellbook and smiles, and Waluigi would like the camera to hold on that smile, because it is the one real moment of menace in a filing that has otherwise run on songs and tea. **"We don't have to fight. You just have to tell the truth, and I'll go. I have a spell that will make it so you can't lie."**

Meanwhile, to the side: Remi, bored, leans on a toad. Gold. She yawns and swats another. Gold. She kicks her legs back and a third toad goes gold. WAH. She has made three solid-gold toads in a hall in the time it took Markop to read a paragraph, and she has not looked up from her own boredom once. That is a CAREER.

Back to the tea. **"Of course I'd never lie to anyone."** Markop: **"Now say the truth spell didn't work."** Rivers: **"Maybe you're a bad magician."** The spell, it turns out, did not land on Rivers. It landed on the toad next to him.

**"Tell me your secret."**

**"I like lifting up people, and I also stole something from Archi—"**

And Rivers forces the tea down his throat. The toad throws up. **"Hey, what did he steal?"** **"Into the dungeon with him."**

A blue coffee, after. The question of what he stole is still open, and the case is in the dungeon.

sections.heading: THE PEN IS MIGHTIER, AND THE CROWD GOES HOME
sections.body:
Markop is, by now, out of patience and into his best rhythm. **"You're lying. We need to duel. The spell clearly didn't work."** **"I am the best. It's not a lie."**

Archie is still in his barrel. Waluigi would like to say this once more so it is on the tape: *Archie is still in the barrel.* He is the cause of the whole dispute, he is the subject of the lesson, and he has been parked, patiently, at the side of the room like luggage.

And then the weapon, the most Toad thing on the reel: Rivers attacks Markop with a PEN. **"The pen is mightier than the sword."** He said it. Waluigi has no further comment on it.

The duel goes in the order in which these things go. Markop attacks. Rivers catches fire and screams. A battleaxe comes round and catches fire and he screams again. **"AAAA."** Markop swings and misses. Somebody grabs for the axe and is too weak to take it. WAH. The tape does not say whose hands, and Waluigi has played it back four times.

Then the best detail of all. The toads start walking out. **"Lame."** **"He is losing his crowd."** They *leave.* In the middle of a fight, they have decided the Speaker is boring.

And Markop smiles and prepares for another strike.

Waluigi ends the reel there, because the account does too. A man on fire, a centaur with a smile, a barrel in the corner, and a hall that has stopped believing. Roll credits. WAH.

commentaries.title: Waluigi's Witness Commentary on 'The Archive Hall and the Song "Alone"'
commentaries.subtitle: Six names on a cursed sheet, two Wa's too many, ten thousand missing gold, one crushed Fire Flower, and the night Wario turned down money in front of a Toad.
commentaries.filed: 4 Aethel, 1035 BF
commentaries.kicker: WITNESS DESK · ARCHIVE HALL VAULT · 1035 BF
commentaries.pullQuote: Gold doesn't bring dead people back! — Wario, sober, in front of a witness, scar-cracking a stone wall while clutching a Feywild contract by its torn corners.
commentaries.standfirst: Waluigi walks through every hour of 3 Aethel, 1035 BF inside the unguarded Archive Hall: the six-name clone song that slandered MY mustache and stole MY signature cry, Mr. T's catastrophic 'two Wa's' follow-up, Wario's self-appointed career as 'The Explosive Accountant', four capital words unread in the bottom-left margin, three hauntings in seven days culminating in five lines of Italian and a stolen book, and Wario losing his nerve in the corridor.

sections.heading: I. That Six-Name Musical Hate Crime, Line by Miserable Line
sections.body:
WAH! Sit down, pour yourself cold coffee, and read that first sheet straight through WITHOUT skipping the bracketed `[music]` cues, because Waluigi endured EVERY SINGLE SYLLABLE across raw oak with a twenty-four-hour-old rotor bruise throbbing behind MY left eye! Mr. T slides the page across the table like he is handing Waluigi cold gold and says, "I got what you wanted." THAT WAS NOT WHAT WALUIGI WANTED! Look at the opening roll call: Mario, Luigi, Wario, Waluigi, Bowser, and THEN, dropped onto the end like a dead fish nailed to a cello, Wario Bowser! WHO ON EARTH IS WARIO BOWSER?! Waluigi told Mr. T on the spot and Waluigi will shout it down every stone vault in this kingdom: "there's no Wario Bowser because *Wario* already IS Bowser for most games!" Think about Waluigi's professional life for FIVE SECONDS! Wario steals castles, Wario hoards treasure mountains, Wario throws his own employees down elevator shafts, and some anonymous lunatic sits in a basement begging corporate offices for MORE EVIL CLONES while Waluigi CANNOT EVEN GET INVITED TO MARIO KART 64 OR SUPER SMASH BROS.! THE SONG LITERALLY BRAGS ABOUT LEAVING WALUIGI OUT TO MY FACE!

Read the middle verse again if you think Waluigi is exaggerating ONE INCH! First it announces that Mario and Luigi are brothers and Wario is their cousin — ALREADY WRONG enough to curdle milk — and THEN it trails off into two brainless `[music]` breaks right after saying nobody knows if Waluigi is anything at all! NOBODY KNOWS?! ASK WALUIGI! WALUIGI IS SITTING AT THE TABLE! THEN the songwriter loses whatever marble remained inside his skull and writes that Mario has a zigzag mustache while Luigi has an L-shaped mustache AND THEN SAYS BOWSER DOESN'T HAVE A MUSTACHE, WALUIGI DOES, AND THEY LOOK VERY SIMILAR TO WALUIGI! BOWSER AND MY MUSTACHE DO NOT SHARE A POSTAL CODE, LET ALONE FACIAL GEOMETRY! THIS MAGNIFICENT WORK OF ARCHITECTURAL PRECISION TOOK WALUIGI YEARS OF WAX AND SPITE TO PERFECT, AND SOME CHORUS HACK RHYMED WALUIGI WITH WART BOWSER!

And DO NOT skip the ending! Four lines from the bottom, right after spelling M-A-R-I-O-W-A-L-U-I-G-I without spaces like a ransom demand, it shouts WALUIGI SAYS WAH and IMMEDIATELY hands MY SIGNATURE BATTLE CRY THREE TIMES IN A ROW TO WAWARIO! ONCE IN CAPITALS, TWICE IN CAPITALS, AND A THIRD TIME WHISPERED LIKE AN ENCORE! MY WAH! STOLEN ON WALUIGI'S OWN DESK WHILE MY WORKING NOTEBOOK IS STILL IN PAULO'S STUPID SYNDICATE SATCHEL FROM STAR HILL! Any lesser man would have eaten the paper whole! Waluigi left EVERY WORD intact so posterity can prosecute the author by hand!

sections.heading: II. 'Two Wa's' — Why the Pen Flew, Why My Name Got Blacked Out, and That Ceiling Stain
sections.body:
People reading from dry armchairs five years later love to chuckle when Waluigi throws office stationery across a stone vault. WAH! YOU TRY IT! First Mr. T drags Waluigi back from the doorway pretending he wants an intellectual explanation of rivalry theory: "Wario already IS Bowser for most games? What do you mean by that?" Fine! Waluigi loves logic! Waluigi sits back down, points straight at the giant purple letter on MY cap, and lays out elementary geometry for him — AND THEN THAT TINY SPECTACLED TOAD TILTS HIS HEAD AND DROPS "Wawaluigi. Two Wa's." INTO THE AIR LIKE IT COSTS NOTHING!

TWO WA'S! SAY IT OUT LOUD AND LISTEN TO YOUR OWN MOUTH TURN INTO A BROKEN DRAINPIPE! WAWALUGI! If you put two negatives in front of Luigi you are mathematically back at REGULAR GREEN LUIGI WITH WORSE POSTURE, WHICH ALREADY EXISTS DOWN THE CORRIDOR IN A COMA! For YEARS the entire Mushroom Kingdom treated Waluigi like a spare umbrella left behind at a tennis tournament — no solo billing, two measly lives while Mario waltzes around burning three per stage, zero respect — and NOW instead of paying Waluigi ONE GOLD COIN OF BACK ROYALTIES, the universe invents a DOUBLE-PREFIX COUNTERFEIT TO STAND NEXT TO WALUIGI?! YES MY CHAIR TIPPED! YES WALUIGI'S PEN FLEW ACROSS THE ROOM AND MISSED THE MARK BY FOUR FEET! THAT NIB WAS BENT FROM THE STAR HILL ROOFTOP AND WALUIGI'S RIBS WERE BRUISED PURPLE!

Look at what Waluigi ACTUALLY DID once the red mist cleared half an inch: Waluigi picked that pen back up off the stone, walked to the oak table, and drove ONE SOLID BLACK BAR straight across MY OWN NAME until not one fiber of white parchment showed underneath. "Scrap this whole mess. No more confusion. No more evil versions. This isn't about the Wa characters. This is about ME." REMEMBER THAT LINE WHEN YOU READ THE NEXT FIVE HOURS OF THIS NIGHT! Because outside in Star Hill, three copies of Mr. L had JUST sung about killing Mario, Promo Mario had JUST played statesman on film, and an hour later a FOURTH broken green brother walked straight into THIS VERY ROOM! Waluigi smelled identity rot in the mortar before anybody else even opened a cabinet!

And DO NOT gloss over what happened five minutes after Waluigi clicked that door shut with "Don't wait up" and walked into the rain! Mr. T looks ten feet straight up at solid stone — NO CRACK, NO PIPE SEAM — asks "Is the ceiling leaking?" out loud, watches dark water spread out of nowhere right above Waluigi's open red-stained grimoire, AND GOES TO SLEEP UNDER IT! ONLY MR. T COULD WATCH A VAULT START BLEEDING RAIN OVER SECRET BOOKS AND CALL IT A LULLABY!

sections.heading: III. 'The Explosive Accountant' — Brass Keys, Big Mouths, and Who Owes Whom
sections.body:
WAH HA HA! EVERY TIME WALUIGI GETS GLOOMY FOR TEN MINUTES, ALL WALUIGI HAS TO DO IS RE-READ WARIO'S ENTRANCE AND MY WILL TO LIVE DOUBLES! Picture poor half-dead Mr. T drooling on inventory schedules under a dripping ceiling while Wario tiptoes in wet from the storm, circles the chair LIKE A GARLIC-SCENTED SHARK, pokes the back of his neck, leans into his ear with "Wake up, sleepyhead." AND THEN POSES WITH BOTH THUMBS IN HIS VEST SHOUTING: "I am Wario! The Explosive Accountant! And you're just... what exactly are you supposed to be?" NOBODY CALLED HIM THAT! NOBODY IN TEN YEARS OF COMMERCE HAS EVER CALLED WARIO AN ACCOUNTANT WITHOUT THE WORD EMBEZZLER ATTACHED BY STAPLES!

Now listen closely to what Wario puts on the oak table BEFORE he knows Waluigi has come back down the corridor with MY ears pressed flat against the glass! First, Wario claims he spent THREE STRAIGHT HOURS checking Waluigi's morning schedules against his own grimoire and caught a ten-thousand-gold gap between column seven and column nine PLUS a client deposit stamped almost two weeks before any real deal happened. WAIT RIGHT THERE! Did Waluigi cook that sheet? NO! IF WALUIGI WAS GOING TO SKIM TEN THOUSAND GOLD OFF WARIO, DO YOU SERIOUSLY THINK WALUIGI WOULD LEAVE COLUMN SEVEN SITTING TWO INCHES FROM COLUMN NINE ON THE SAME PIECE OF PAPER?! PLEASE! INSULT WALUIGI'S MORALS ALL WEEK LONG, NEVER INSULT WALUIGI'S ARITHMETIC!

Second, watch Wario casually pull a SMALL BRASS KEY out of his inner coat pocket and brag that he ALREADY opened locked Archive Hall cabinets earlier and found things he refuses to name! Hold EVERYTHING! Five minutes later this SAME MAN throws a purple-faced fit screaming that the Archive Hall is a sacred fortress nobody can touch — AFTER UNLOCKING ITS DRAWERS HIMSELF WITH POCKET BRASS! AND THEN HE TELLS MR. T: "We're family... He owes me money. Big time. And then he has the audacity to send me paperwork that might be fake?" OH, WE'RE FAMILY NOW WHEN THE AUDIT GOES SIDEWAYS, ARE WE, WARIO?! Twenty-four hours ago on a smashed clinic roof Wario threw WALUIGI'S WORKING NOTEBOOK AT AN ARMED SYNDICATE COURIER FOR ZERO GOLD AND SPLIT OUR DEAL SIXTY-THIRTY IN HIS OWN FAVOR WHILE WALUIGI WAS CONCUSSED! Waluigi remembers EVERY SINGLE COIN OF OUR TAB, FAT MAN, AND WHEN YOU SUBTRACT ONE HELICOPTER CRASH PLUS ONE LOST MANUSCRIPT, CHECK WHOSE COLUMN IS BLEEDING RED!

sections.heading: IV. Four Words in the Bottom-Left Corner That Should Hang Over Wario's Bed Forever
sections.body:
YES, WALUIGI CAME BACK IN WITH A FRESH BRUISE ON MY CHEEK AND A BADLY SCORCHED NOTEBOOK CLUTCHED AGAINST MY CHEST — AND NO, WALUIGI IS STILL NOT TELLING PUBLIC READERS WHAT SCORCHED THOSE EDGES IN TWENTY MINUTES OUTSIDE! Waluigi told Wario flatly: "I got here about twenty minutes ago" and "I was just dealing with some... complications." If people start shouting about an emergency down the clinic hallway five seconds after Waluigi closes a glass door, WALUIGI'S ONLY COMMENT IS THAT CORRELATION IS NOT CAUSATION, WAH! Keep your eyes where they belong: on Mr. T walking quietly over to the oak shelves and pulling down TWO GIANT VOLUMES AT RANDOM WHILE WARIO IS BUSY SCREAMING ABOUT CONSPIRACIES!

LOOK AT THAT SCENE! Wario has spent THREE HOURS sweating over loose morning sheets, and Mr. T simply reaches up one shelf and hands him *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise* — BOTH REAL BACKUP VOLUMES — SITTING WIDE OPEN IN A ROOM WITH ZERO GUARDS! Wario goes bug-eyed yelling: "Public? You think THIS Archive Hall is just some public library where anyone can wander in off the street?! This place houses the most sensitive financial records in all of civilization!" AND BOTH MR. T AND WALUIGI HAVE TO TELL HIM TO HIS FACE THAT WE HAVE WALKED IN AND OUT OF THIS PLACE FOR MONTHS WITHOUT SEEING ONE SINGLE GUARD! NOT ONE HALBERD! NOT ONE SLEEPING TOAD IN A CHAIR! Whoever stripped the guard post off this vault months ago wanted people walking out with secrets OR planting fake pages right on top of real ones — INCLUDING THAT FIVE-THOUSAND-GOLD WITHDRAWAL AND ONE-MONTH RE-DEPOSIT ON THE TREASURY OF WONDERS!

AND THEN COMES THE GREATEST MOMENT IN RECORDED FINANCIAL HISTORY! Mr. T deadpans one little question — "Yeah, this is definitely fraud. Should I contact the TPF — Toad Police Force?" — AND WARIO NEARLY SWALLOWS HIS OWN MUSTACHE WHOLE! "WAIT!" Wario barks! "Do NOT contact them! Do not tell a single soul about this!" WHY? BECAUSE EVERY TOAD IN TOADSTON WITH HALF A CLIPBOARD WOULD FLIP WARIO UPSIDE DOWN BY HIS ANKLES IF THEY OPENED THAT FUND! AND THEN MR. T FLIPS THE PAGE OVER TO THE BOTTOM-LEFT CORNER! READ IT AGAIN IN SOLID GOLD CAPITALS:

`AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO`

MR. T HAD ALREADY FOUND IT MONTHS AGO, WRITTEN WARIO'S OWN NAME AFTER A HYPHEN IN THE CORNER OF THE DAILY REPORT, HANDED IT STRAIGHT TO WARIO'S DESK, AND WARIO NEVER READ DOWN TO THE BOTTOM OF HIS OWN PAGE! "Of COURSE you told me. I'm a fool." HIS EXACT WORDS IN FRONT OF WALUIGI! TATTOO IT ON WALUIGI'S TOMBSTONE SO WALUIGI CAN LAUGH UNDERGROUND!

sections.heading: V. Three Hauntings in Seven Days, Wario's Slip About the Breach, and One Murdered Flower
sections.body:
Laugh all you want at Wario's bookkeeping — EVERYTHING FUNNY IN THAT VAULT DIED THE SECOND BOOTS SOUNDED IN THE EMPTY CLINIC HALLWAY! Remember WHERE the Archive Hall sits! Connected corridors running straight toward Star Hill's medical wards, dead hours of the night, rain hammering stone lancets, Waluigi tucking the ledger tight under MY arm and whispering "Shit" before ducking behind the oak stacks while Wario clamps one glove straight over the pocket holding his precious contract and drags Mr. T into deep cover: "Stay completely silent. If we move even an inch, they'll hear us."

FIRST: DO NOT GLIDE PAST WARIO'S WHISPER BEHIND THE SHELF AFTER THE DOORWAY CHORUS VANISHES! "That was the third haunting this week," Wario mutters bitterly — "First Boo's ghost, then that giant moth thing from last week... Now THIS? I'm starting to think the Archive Hall has a grudge against Wario's Enterprise." THREE HAUNTINGS IN ONE WEEK INSIDE ONE UNGUARDED VAULT! Not one random ghost wandering lost through plaster — THREE SEPARATE ENTITIES CROSSING INTO THE EXACT SAME ROOM SEVEN DAYS APART! AND TEN SECONDS LATER WARIO BLURTS OUT THE REASON RIGHT TO BETA LUIGI'S FACE: "Maybe this whole Feywild breach was a mistake that's going to cost us everything — so are you going to stand there holding flowers like some kind of funeral bouquet, or tell me what's going on?!" WRITE THOSE TWO WORDS IN THREE-INCH LETTERS ACROSS YOUR FOREHEAD: FEYWILD BREACH! WARIO SAID IT OUT LOUD!

SECOND: LOOK AT WHO WALKED THROUGH THAT DOOR! Not clinic Luigi lying under clean white sheets down the hall, NOT blue-coat Mr. L smirking outside in triplicate — a hollow, wax-faced wreck in stained green overalls and heavy leather tool belt with dreadful bruised bags hanging under barely open eyes, humming softly over losing his big brother across King Boo's chasm while carrying A REAL WORKING FIRE FLOWER IN HIS HANDS! WAH! WALUIGI'S HEART STILL SPLINTERS REMEMBERING THAT HEAVY WORK BOOT COMING STRAIGHT DOWN ON THOSE GLOWING PETALS! "WHAT THE— Don't you DARE!" Waluigi shouted before MY brain even caught up with MY legs! "That was a perfect flower! A WORKING flower with actual power and you just CRUSHED IT!" Do NOT laugh at Waluigi yelling about a flower in the middle of a haunting! Waluigi knows EXACTLY what crushing live fire under your own heel means: IT MEANS THE MAN IN GREEN HAD ALREADY DECIDED HE NEVER WANTED ANOTHER EXTRA LIFE AGAIN!

sections.heading: VI. Fifteen Feet of Crimson Rage, My Scattered Pages, and Five Lines of Italian
sections.body:
Anybody who claims he stood tall and heroic through the next ten minutes of that night is a liar who was NOT in the room! When Waluigi slammed both palms into that oak bookcase yelling "Brother! Do NOT stand there weeping about Mario! You think King Boo cared about your feelings when he trapped him?!" and Wario lunged forward trying to grab Beta Luigi by the shoulders, THE AIR BETWEEN THE STACKS TURNED SOLID! Ghosts surged forward like an iron wall and threw Wario stumbling backward on his heels while Beta Luigi stared straight through the barrier singing his heart out into raw stone!

Then came the crash in the lower vaults — and THE TEMPERATURE IN THAT ARCHIVE DROPPED TWENTY DEGREES IN ONE HEARTBEAT! Fifteen feet tall, arms thick as oak trunks, burning angry crimson right up under the leaking ceiling beams while Wario crossed his arms with dead-eyed stubbornness holding up a paper ledger chart like stationery stops a giant spirit! AND WALUIGI? WALUIGI WILL TELL YOU THE TRUTH WITHOUT ONE WORD OF VANITY! Waluigi's knees buckled straight down onto those freezing flags! MY scorched second notebook spilled open across the wet stone — EVERY frantic page Waluigi had scribbled outside on spectral barriers and quantum entanglement fluttering around MY boots — and REAL TEARS CUT THROUGH THE SOOT ON WALUIGI'S FACE! "Brother! BROTHER! I'm sorry! I'm SO sorry!" YES, WALUIGI WEPT ON HIS KNEES IN THAT HALL! Listen to that boy sobbing that his cowardice cost his brother's life and tell Waluigi YOUR knees stay locked!

AND THEN MARIO ANSWERED OUT OF EMPTY AIR IN ITALIAN! Faint at first, then crystal clear across stone walls with NO speaker, NO pipe, NO trick: "Luigi, where did you go? I'm stranded, lost and alone." And then in the old tongue: "Luigi, where did you go? Ti perdono. Vai avanti." *I forgive you. Go on.* "Tocca a te salvarli." *It is up to you to save them.* "Mario non c'è più — non farmi morire invano." *Mario is no more — do not let me die in vain.* "Mostra loro che sei il fratello..." "...di Mario! Sei Luigi!" EVERY PHANTOM CUT OFF AT THE EXACT SAME INSTANT! Beta Luigi hit the stones, whispered that he would make them atone ALONE, stood back up, REACHED ONTO THE PHYSICAL OAK SHELF WITH A SOLID HAND, PULLED DOWN ONE REAL BOUND BOOK, AND WALKED OUT THE DOOR! GHOSTS DO NOT STEAL BOOKS, IDIOTS! CHECK THAT EMPTY SLOT ON THE SHELF FIRST THING IN THE MORNING!

sections.heading: VII. 'Gold Doesn't Bring Dead People Back' — Two Contracts, One Name, and Skinny T
sections.body:
If you think the haunting was the strangest miracle of 3 Aethel, 1035 BF, WAIT SIXTY SECONDS FOR THE CORRIDOR! Beta Luigi vanishes down the passage with mystery archive volume number one tucked under his arm. Waluigi walks straight to the open doorway clutching MY worn grimoire pages because SOMEBODY with working eyes has to watch which turn he takes: "Sometimes you don't get second chances because there weren't any first chances to begin with." Behind Waluigi, sensible little courier Mr. T does ordinary mercenary arithmetic out loud: "He said Mario, right? That means the Mario disappearance case — it was a side thing, I know, but Wario, think of the gold we can get if we bring Mario back!" Nine hundred and ninety-nine nights out of a thousand, Wario's pupils turn into spinning gold coins and he tackles Mr. T through the plaster to sign finder's forms!

NOT ON 3 AETHEL! Wario whips his head sideways, yanks that dog-eared Contract of Accord out of his coat hard enough to crack stiff parchment, slams HIS BARE FIST STRAIGHT INTO SOLID CORRIDOR STONE, AND SCREAMS WORDS WALUIGI NEVER THOUGHT MORTAL EARS WOULD HEAR OUT OF WARIO'S MOUTH: "Enough!" and then "I don't care if there's gold involved, Mr. T! Gold doesn't bring dead people back!" WAH! READ THAT LINE TWICE AND CHISEL IT INTO MARBLE! Wario is NOT performing charity for newspaper cameras — nobody is standing in that dim gaslit passage except ONE TOAD COURIER! Listen to what Wario admits ten seconds later when Mr. T asks about the torn parchment in his fist: "This isn't a book. It's a contract. And right now it's the only thing keeping me from walking away from all of this because I know damn well that if I don't fix this somehow, there won't be any coming back — not for anyone." AND THEN HE CALLS IT ONE OF "these Feywild contracts" TO MR. T'S FACE! TWENTY-FOUR HOURS EARLIER ON WALUIGI'S OUTPOST BALCONY HE USED THAT EXACT SAME NAME FOR OUR SIXTY-THIRTY PARTNERSHIP DEAL! Either Wario carries TWO contracts under one title OR he hid a lethal Feywild default clause underneath Star Hill AND NOW THE BILL IS COLLECTING HAUNTINGS THREE TIMES A WEEK!

AND ONE LAST GIFT FROM WALUIGI'S MEMORY BEFORE WALUIGI LOCKS THIS FILE! Listen to Wario's parting insult to Mr. T in the dark hallway — calling him "a courier who knows too much about gambling debts." REWIND TWENTY-FOUR HOURS TO OUTSIDE DR. TOAD'S CLINIC WHEN SYNDICATE COURIER PAULO SQUINTED AT MR. L IN GREEN AND SAID HE DIDN'T KNOW SKINNY T WORE GREEN! Same hill! Same clinic complex! A thin, underslept Toad courier named MR. T cleaning Wario's dirty laundry and gambling tabs! EVERY PIECE CONNECTS WHEN WALUIGI HOLDS THE PEN — EVEN AFTER THROWING IT AT A WALL! WAH!

sections.heading: VIII. Twenty Minutes in the Storm — Why My Second Notebook Came Back Black Around the Edges
sections.body:
WAIT A SECOND — nobody leaves this desk without talking properly about the twenty-minute gap between Waluigi walking out into the downpour and Waluigi pressing MY cold wet ears flat against that Archive Hall glass! Everybody stares at Wario waving ledgers and forgets what walked back in through that door!
