Waluigi left ONE working notebook in Paulo's courier satchel the night before on Star Hill, left MY heavy grimoire open in red ink right beside sleeping Mr. T on the oak table, stepped out into pouring rain with NOTHING except a spare pocket pad and a bruised cheekbone — AND CAME BACK TWENTY MINUTES LATER WITH FRESH CONTUSIONS AND FOUR SCORCHED BLACK MARGINS SMELLING OF OZONE AND BURNT RAG PAPER! WAH!

Listen to what happened five seconds AFTER Waluigi pulled that door shut behind ME: boots pounding down the distant clinic passage and voices yelling about an emergency! Wario looks straight at Waluigi's face, sees the fresh mark swelling under MY eye, steps closer, and gets shut down cold: "I got here about twenty minutes ago" and "I was just dealing with some... complications. That's none of your concern right now." WHY DID WALUIGI KEEP THOSE PAGES PRESSED TIGHT AGAINST MY CHEST UNTIL THE FIFTEEN-FOOT RED SPIRIT KNOCKED WALUIGI ONTO HIS KNEES?! Look at the two subjects scribbled across those singed leaves when they scattered across the stone flags: spectral barriers and quantum entanglement!

DO THE ARITHMETIC WITH YOUR OWN BRAIN FOR ONCE! Waluigi walked out of the Archive Hall furious about evil doubles and counterfeit prefixes — AND WITHIN FIVE STEPS OF THE CLINIC CORRIDORS RAN HEADFIRST INTO LIVE ECTOPLASMIC SPILLOVER ALREADY LEAKING THROUGH THE COMPLEX BEFORE BETA LUIGI EVER REACHED OUR DOOR! That ceiling stain ten feet above Mr. T's sleeping skull did NOT open because Star Hill hired bad roofers! The rain coming down outside hit a thinning seam between worlds where a Boo had crossed days earlier, where a giant moth had crossed the week before, and where something hot enough to char damp paper scorched MY pocket pad while Waluigi was taking field notes in the dark! Anybody else in this kingdom gets jumped by corridor anomalies at midnight and sprints straight for a ferry ticket! Waluigi wiped the soot off MY chin, tucked the scorched pages against MY ribs, marched STRAIGHT BACK TO THE ARCHIVE DOOR, listened through the glass until Wario finished incriminating himself, AND CAME BACK INSIDE TO FINISH THE AUDIT! NAME ONE HERO ON A CEREAL BOX WITH HALF THAT SPINE! YOU CAN'T!

sections.heading: IX. Five Lines in the Old Tongue — Why Even Waluigi Stopped Breathing
sections.body:
Now shut the door, blow out half the gas lamps in your head, and listen AGAIN to those five lines that came out of empty stone when Beta Luigi hit rock bottom — because Waluigi has spent YEARS despising Mario's red cap, Mario's rigged three-life safety net, Mario's effortless applause, AND YET WALUIGI REFUSES TO CHEAPEN WHAT SPOKE INSIDE THAT ROOM! WAH! If Waluigi wanted to lie to make himself look cold-blooded and untouchable, Waluigi owned the pen! Waluigi could have scraped MY own tears straight off the page in thirty seconds! Waluigi DID NOT SCRAPE ONE DROP!

Listen to the exact cadence of how that voice arrived. Not booming off the rafters like a stage wizard trying to scare children — FAINT FIRST, barely audible through rain on lancet glass, asking one plain human question: "Luigi, where did you go? I'm stranded, lost and alone." Think about what that first sentence DOES to every smug rumor floating around Toad Town! Not 'I am vacationing on an island!' Not 'wait for my triumphant press tour!' *Stranded, lost, and alone!* And watch how Beta Luigi answers BEFORE he even registers whether the voice is inside his own skull or standing in the room: "Oh, Mario, where do I go? The kingdom's lost and alone."

AND THEN THE VOICE CLARIFIES AND DROPS STRAIGHT INTO ITALIAN! Why Italian?! Because no Toad clerk, no Koopa forger, no cheap illusionist running a parlor trick in Star Hill speaks to Luigi in their private household tongue when nobody is supposed to hear! *Ti perdono. Vai avanti.* I forgive you — go forward! *Tocca a te salvarli.* It falls to YOU to save them now! *Mario non c'è più — non farmi morire invano.* Mario is gone — do not let me die in vain! And then the split line where brother talks straight over brother sobbing that he still had so much left to prove: *Mostra loro che sei il fratello... di Mario! Sei Luigi!* SHOW THEM YOU ARE MARIO'S BROTHER — YOU ARE LUIGI!

WAH! Read that again and tell Waluigi why EVERY SINGLE GHOST IN THE HALL WENT DEAD SILENT ON THE FINAL WORD! The crimson giant vanished! The invisible wall locking Wario and Waluigi behind the bookcase vanished! Even the thunder outside held its tongue while water dripped once, twice, three times onto cold stone! Whatever reached across from wherever Mario is trapped spent EVERY LAST SPARK OF SIGNAL IT HAD JUST TO TELL ONE BROKEN GREEN WRECK TO STAND BACK UP! And when Beta Luigi stood up, he did NOT smile, he did NOT thank heaven, and he did NOT ask Wario or Waluigi for help — he whispered that they laughed at him, swore he would make them atone ALONE, pulled one bound book off the oak shelf, AND WALKED OUT!

sections.heading: X. Closing the Night's Tab — Four People, Four Doors, Zero Safe Exits
sections.body:
Step back ten paces from the oak table and count what actually walked out of the Archive Hall at the close of 3 Aethel, 1035 BF, because every amateur historian in this city misses half the board when he only watches the loudest man in the corridor! WAH! Waluigi counts ALL FOUR PLAYERS AND EVERY OBJECT IN THEIR HANDS!

Player Number One: **Beta Luigi** — out first into the rain, alone by sworn oath, boots wet with crushed Fire Flower sap, Mario's forgiveness ringing behind his eyes, carrying ONE UNIDENTIFIED BOUND BOOK PULLED STRAIGHT OFF THE ARCHIVE SHELVES! Until Waluigi checks every empty gap between those oak uprights tomorrow, assume whoever wrote or owned that missing volume is NEXT ON HIS LIST!

Player Number Two: **Wario** — out down the clinic corridor scar-fisted and white around the knuckles, clutching *The Complete Ledger of Wario's Enterprise* under one arm, a brass cabinet key in one pocket, and a torn, dog-eared parchment he calls ONE OF "these Feywild contracts" in his bare fist AFTER screaming "Gold doesn't bring dead people back!" at full volume! Let Waluigi underline that twice in purple ink: a Wario who turns down gold because a contract threatens total erasure is ten times more dangerous than a greedy Wario — because a scared Wario swings blind!

Player Number Three: **Mr. T** — dragged straight down that dim passage at Wario's heels whether he likes it or not! Do NOT underestimate that tiny tired Toad for ONE SECOND! Tonight alone he delivered the clone sheet, slept through a supernatural ceiling leak, pulled two needle-in-a-haystack backup ledgers off unindexed shelves ON THE FIRST REACH, humiliated Wario with `AUDIT REQUIRED - WARIO` in four tiny block words, AND accidentally answered Paulo's mystery from last night about skinny T! Mr. T knows EVERY dirty secret inside Wario's books AND Waluigi's tabs — if anything eats Mr. T in that corridor, half the financial memory of Star Hill dies with him!

And Player Number Four: **Waluigi!** Standing right on the threshold between the haunted room and the dark passage with MY scorched quantum-entanglement notes in MY pocket, MY worn grimoire pages tight against MY ribs, MY name blacked out in permanent ink so NO DOUBLE, NO WAWARIO, AND NO WAWALUGI EVER WEARS IT, AND BOTH COMPLETE SONGS LOCKED INTO WALUIGI'S ARCHIVE FOREVER! Nobody erases Waluigi! Nobody outlasts Waluigi! NOW HAND ME DRY BOOTS AND FIND OUT WHICH BOOK THAT GREEN LUNATIC TOOK! WAH!

sections.heading: XI. Postscript from Waluigi's Blotter — Why Every Last Syllable Stayed Uncut
sections.body:
ONE FINAL WORD FOR EVERY FUSSY CLERK WHO EVER ASKED WHY WALUIGI DID NOT SUMMARIZE TWO SONGS INTO THREE NEAT SENTENCES AND SAVE INK! WAH! Put your red pencil back inside your ear before Waluigi snaps it in half! Think about how every fraud inside that stone hall operated tonight: somebody took real events, trimmed out one inconvenient line, shifted one date two weeks sideways, swapped one summary sheet on top of two thick volumes nobody bothered opening, AND WATCHED GROWN MEN SCREAM AT EACH OTHER FOR HOURS OVER A COUNTERFEIT!

Waluigi DOES NOT RUN WARIO'S DESK! On Waluigi's desk you get EVERY rotten bracketed `[music]` marker on the first sheet AND EVERY broken gasp and Italian line on the second sheet — because FIVE YEARS FROM NOW in 1040 BF, when half the witnesses have amnesia and the other half pretend King Boo was a fairy tale invented to sell lanterns, some smug palace archivist WILL claim nobody ever heard Mario speak after the mansion! TRY CLAIMING THAT OVER WALUIGI'S RECORD! Three witnesses stood inside solid stone — Waluigi, Wario, and Mr. T — while a live flower died under a heavy boot, a fifteen-foot crimson spirit froze the marrow inside our shins, Mario forgave his brother in plain Italian, AND ONE BOUND ARCHIVE VOLUME WALKED OUT INTO THE STORM IN SOLID HANDS!

And YES, Waluigi kept the stupid opening song right beside it ON PURPOSE! Because look at the night's geometry from start to finish: it OPENS with Waluigi furious that some anonymous fool reduces MY entire existence to an afterthought behind six names and a fake prefix, AND IT ENDS WITH WALUIGI STANDING TALL IN THE DOORWAY WHILE WARIO POUNDS CORRIDOR PLASTER BEGGING A TOAD COURIER TO EXPLAIN FEYWILD CLAUSES! Who threw a tantrum at seven o'clock and STILL walked out holding every fact of the night in proper order by midnight?! WALUIGI! Who missed four capital words addressed to HIS OWN NAME in the corner of HIS OWN DAILY REPORT for MONTHS?! WARIO! Keep your summaries, keep your cover-ups, and keep your double prefixes off MY purple cap — Waluigi's archive stays UNCUT! WAH!

commentaries.title: Waluigi's Witness Commentary on 'The Locked Cottage, the Hypno-Helmet, and the Dragon at the Goblin Camp'
commentaries.subtitle: A locked room, one button with suspiciously broad authority, a disguise minus its shorts, and a dragon that leaves the question behind.
commentaries.filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — the screening desk, after the report; exact hour unrecorded
commentaries.pullQuote: A locked door is a terrible plan when one button can unlock the entire cottage.
commentaries.standfirst: Waluigi puts the 2 Aethel account on a screen one paragraph at a time. This is a reading-room conceit, not a claim that anyone recorded the cottage on camera: the words themselves supply two armed guards, a failed swipe, an emergency release, a hypno-helmet, a very specific clothing decision, an absurdly separate mustard drone, a goblin-camp recruitment pitch, and a dragon whose arrival does not settle who summoned it. Waluigi has the pause key. He is going to need it.

sections.heading: I. Freeze the Text: Two Armed Guards and a 'Bonding Ritual'
sections.body:
Freeze the first card. Bones wakes in a cottage, and the words give him two armed Toad guards and locked doors before they give him a route, a reason, or a name. The previous session had him asleep under trees beyond the Legion wall; now he is somewhere else entirely. Waluigi taps the blank between those two pictures with a pencil. There is no road in it. There is no guide. There is no travel time. THE BLANK IS THE BLANK. THE GAP IS NOT A DOORWAY. NO ROAD. NO GUIDE. NO EXCUSE TO INVENT ONE. A transition is not a teleportation service just because the next room has better lighting.

Then the guards offer the phrase *bonding ritual*. Waluigi puts a circle around it on the screen and immediately draws a much larger circle around the weapons and the locks. A phrase can describe how the speaker wants a scene to sound; it cannot unlock the door or make two armed guards disappear. The guards' explanation is part of the scene, not a magic eraser for the scene. Waluigi is not calling them anything the account does not call them. He is pointing at what is actually visible: Bones is held in a room, and the room is locked.

The crop has no answer for why he woke there. It has no answer for whether the guards know how he arrived. It has no answer for what is beyond the doors. Waluigi would love to supply a convenient corridor, a suspicious wagon, or a hand-written invitation with a skull on it. He has none of those things. He has the cottage, the guards, and a gap large enough to park a carriage in.

The funniest part is that the phrase is trying to sound pleasant while the room is doing all the talking. Waluigi can hear the quotation marks from here. The screen puts *bonding ritual* beside the locked doors; one is the guard’s explanation, the other is the room’s condition. Guess which one Waluigi believes first. WAH! Keep the screen on the room. Do not cut to an explanation nobody gave.

sections.heading: II. The Swipe Fails; the Button Unlocks Everything
sections.body:
Next card: Bones tries the key swipe. It fails, and the door stays locked. Waluigi magnifies that line until it fills the screen, because an archive's worth of people keep treating failed access like a minor inconvenience. It is the entire first result! The record does not tell us whether the swipe was a card, a borrowed credential, or some other gesture, so Waluigi will not draw a shiny badge into the picture and pretend he found it in the room.

Then Bones finds the emergency-release button. One press, and every door unlocks—not just the door in front of him. Waluigi pauses the projection. EVERY DOOR? ONE BUTTON. EVERY LOCK. THAT IS A LOT OF AUTHORITY. In a cottage with two armed guards? The button has more authority than the key swipe, the guards, and whatever system was supposed to keep Bones there. Somebody designed an escape hatch that works on the whole building. Waluigi will applaud the button's efficiency while asking why it was installed where the person being held could reach it. A marvelous safety feature, if the plan was to test the locks by releasing the entire cottage.

The source does not say the button is red, identify its maker, or tell us what happens to the system afterward. Waluigi's picture can include a button, a hand, and the doors opening. It cannot include a maintenance crew racing in from offscreen. Please stop asking the projectionist to add one.

Bones gets outside. The story moves from the room to the ground beyond it, but the route between those images is still missing. Waluigi is willing to give the button its full credit: it opens all the locks, and that is exactly what saves the scene from becoming a very long discussion with two guards. The swipe failed. The release worked. The door has spoken in two different ways, and only one of them was useful. WAH!

sections.heading: III. A Green Cloak, a Name, and a Dragon Claim
sections.body:
Waluigi advances the text to the tree line. There is an unnamed green-cloaked figure. Mimbus is named nearby. The words do not give the cloaked person a face, an allegiance, or a relationship to Mimbus; they do not establish that the name belongs to the historical person rather than another figure. Waluigi writes “unknown” in the margin, then underlines it, because sometimes the most useful thing a screen can show is what it refuses to show.

Fawful's declaration arrives in capital letters: **‘I HAVE DRAGONS.’** Waluigi leaves it on the wall for a full five seconds. Three words, and already the room has been redecorated as a threat. The claim might be boast, promise, or something closer to an order of service; at this point it proves that Fawful said it. It does not show a dragon, demonstrate control, or explain how a ritual might work. Waluigi will not let the sentence grow wings and fly away with its own evidence.

This is where an ordinary screening voice would announce that the dragon is coming. Waluigi will not. The account has not shown a dragon yet. It has shown people, a claim, and a gap between scenes. The difference matters. NOT A DRAGON. NOT A CONTRACT. NOT A MAP. A grand announcement is still an announcement, even when the speaker puts enough force behind it to shake the subtitles.

Waluigi is not pretending that Fawful's words are harmless. The rest of the account will give them weight. But the screen has not reached the rest yet. No cutting ahead. No slow-motion dragon shadow pasted over the trees. Waluigi has seen editors do worse with much better budgets. The green cloak remains unidentified; Mimbus remains a name not reconciled to a person; Fawful's claim remains a claim. Roll the next paragraph, not the ending.

sections.heading: IV. The Helmet Is Removed; the Victim Is Still Unknown
sections.body:
The next paragraph starts with a drone tackling an unnamed person and forcing a hypno-helmet over the victim's head. Waluigi stops the projection at the phrase about the machine eating the person's brain. The account gives that as what the notes describe; it gives no medical report, no name, and no outcome. Waluigi can be horrified without pretending he has seen a scan. The victim's identity does not come into focus just because the machine does.

Bones runs in. The drone's vines lash at him. Waluigi rewinds the line and counts the moving parts: a flying device, a helmet pressed down over a person, and vines reaching for Bones. This is already one machine too many for the workshop's safety pamphlet, and the clip has barely begun. The older woman and fox-eared Toad help pull the helmet off. The drone scurries away. Waluigi lets out one breath at the removed helmet, then immediately takes it back: a helmet off is not the same thing as a victim recovered. Nobody on this card gets a confirmed medical ending.

The device is not the earlier Fawthful surveillance drone. The old machine watched; this one attacks with a helmet and vines. Waluigi would like a manufacturer to issue a product catalogue that says, “Please distinguish the flying camera from the brain-eating plant helmet.” Since there is no such catalogue, he is doing the distinction himself. Two machines, separate actions, no invented chassis connection.

Waluigi can see why Bones intervenes. He can also see how much remains out of frame after the intervention. Who was under the helmet? What did the attack do? Where did the drone go? The paragraph gives no answer. Waluigi's audience may demand a clean rescue shot. The screen does not have one. It has a removed helmet, a retreating drone, and a person whose next breath is not reported. NO NAME. NO MEDICAL OUTCOME. NO FOLLOW-UP. Hold there.

sections.heading: V. The Enclave, the Sacrifice, and Twenty Gold
sections.body:
Waluigi sets the next page beside the projector: the older woman and fox-eared Toad speak of the Emerald Enclave, a closed door to new members, and a plan to stop Fawful's forces from completing a dragon-linked ritual. They say a sacrifice is involved. The stakes are plain enough to make the introductions look even less tidy. “Konathin” appears, and so does unclear wording about “Toad ie Fox”; the account does not let Waluigi decide who said which name or whom either name belongs to. He refuses to finish the cast list with a pencil.

The possible dragon comparison reaches back to the one used at Bowser's Castle before 1035. Waluigi holds two pictures side by side and finds no shared marking, custody record, or reliable identifier in this sequence. A resemblance is a reason to ask a question. It is not a name tag. The claim that the Enclave is trying to stop a summoning gives the danger shape; it does not prove the ritual can work, that the dragon later seen is the same one, or that the two companions speak for every member of the group.

Bones offers to help for money. The woman pays him twenty gold. Waluigi writes the number on the margin and draws a box around the word *payment*, not around a total. Twenty gold changes hands in this scene; it does not tell the screening desk what remains in Bones's purse after a later exchange the account cannot quantify. A number is a number, not a license to do arithmetic on missing numbers.

Waluigi is always pleased when the stakes arrive before the invoice, and always irritated when the invoice is clearer than the roster. Here the need is urgent, the organization is only partly described, and the fee is specific. The Enclave's leadership and home are not. A NAME IS NOT A ROSTER. A CLAIM IS NOT A TREATY. The fox-eared Toad still has no confirmed identity. Waluigi can understand why Bones accepts the arrangement without pretending that one payment answers any of those questions. Keep the scene moving. The screen has more danger to show.

sections.heading: VI. Outer Clothes, No Shorts, One Broken Window
sections.body:
The clothing decision gets its own freeze-frame. Bones takes the unnamed guard's clothes but leaves the shorts behind, then uses the rest as a Bean guard disguise. Waluigi is not going to upgrade “clothes” into a list of jacket, boots, buttons, insignia, and matching hat. The source gives him the outer look and a very pointed exception. The shorts stay in the picture. The disguise does not include them. WAH! There are details an archivist can safely leave where the trousers are.

Bones sees two hooded figures and a Magikoopa shape. The account does not decide whether those figures are guards, prisoners, or witnesses, so Waluigi will not assign them uniforms or motives while the text is still running. The woman and fox-eared Toad are later taken by guards; a fight breaks out among the people in that arrest, but the winner and the result never arrive in the paragraph. Bones does not stay to settle it. He takes the broken window and jumps through. CLOTHES, YES. SHORTS, NO. EXIT, YES.

All right: he found an exit. The broken window is real in the story, the disguise gets him past the room, and Bones does get outside. Waluigi concedes the physical result. But he is not going to turn “escaped” into “everyone escaped”; the woman and her companion remain in the scene with no confirmed outcome, and the other figures stay unidentified. A window is a way out for the person who uses it, not a blanket for the whole cast.

Waluigi watches Bones pass through the broken frame and then cuts the image before it can become a victory parade. No triumphant salute, no shorts recovered, no new name pinned to the guard. The disguise is borrowed, incomplete by design, and still useful. The window is broken. The people left behind are still in danger. Waluigi's hand stays over the pause key because this is precisely where the story refuses to give him the neat ending he wants.

sections.heading: VII. The Mustard Drone Is Not the Helmet Drone
sections.body:
The screen jumps to Fawful announcing that preparations are ready and that he has a sacrifice. A hulking Bean grabs Bones. Bones drives his shortsword into the Bean's chest, hoping the poison takes effect. Waluigi freezes the frame on the verb *hoping*. That is the word doing all the work. The target's reaction and the poison's result are not supplied, so Waluigi will not make the blade glow green and call it a confirmed victory. A strike happened. The result is still out of frame.

Then Fawful winds up a separate clockwork drone, and this one sprays mustard across the passage and Bones. SEPARATE. Waluigi writes it in capitals across the screen so nobody can accidentally mash it into the helmet machine from the previous reel. That drone had vines and a helmet. This one is wound up and spits mustard. Two attacks, two devices, no statement that they share a chassis. MUSTARD, YES. HYPNOSIS, NO. SAME MACHINE, NOT ESTABLISHED. Waluigi has seen audience members do less careful work with a bowl of condiments.

Bean forces close in. Bones is grabbed again, slashes for space, breaks free, and bolts. The older woman and fox-eared Toad are brought out as backup, held against a wall, and hit with mustard spray while the pursuit continues. Bones judges that they can manage themselves and leaves. That is Bones's judgment, not proof that they escape. Waluigi turns the screen toward the two figures and waits for the next line. It never comes.

He runs into the trees and climbs out of the immediate chase. The ritual has no recorded result; no sacrifice is confirmed. The mustard is real, the poison is uncertain, and the captives' outcome is missing. Waluigi has the absurd pleasure of Fawful weaponizing a condiment and the less amusing fact that he has not watched the woman and her companion get free. The drone is mustard. The earlier drone is hypnosis. Waluigi will not let the audience call them the same thing just because they both fly.

sections.heading: VIII. WATERBALL! A Recruitment Pitch and a Fart-Spray Gap
sections.body:
At the goblin camp, Bones keeps apart while the light goes. A fart-spray gag sits in this part of the account, but its user, target, and effect are unclear. Waluigi tries three possible freeze-frames and gets no reliable hand, face, or consequence out of any of them. The audience is welcome to laugh at the beat; it is not welcome to assign the can to Bones, the goblins, or the Archie-like figure. It is not a new item just because a gag has a prop-shaped shadow.

The goblins light a fire. A figure they call an Archie bot uses a water trick and shouts **‘WATERBALL!’** The fire goes out. Waluigi had expected many things from a camp-side entrance and none of them involved a one-word fire department with a recruitment table. The goblins ask for a blessing, hear the figure's pitch about having a bandit on their team, needing it to win, and paying it, then accept. They shower the figure with bones and gold. The amount is not counted, and the account does not say that the money goes to Bones.

Waluigi keeps the name in quotation marks because that is how the camp describes the figure. “Bot” could be mechanical, a title, or a joke; a later dragon passenger might be the same figure, but the scene has not proved it. The water trick and recruitment are visible. The identity is not. FIRE OUT. RECRUITED. USER OF THE SPRAY? UNKNOWN. There is a whole economy being built in one campfire scene: fire, water, bandit, bones, gold, employment. Waluigi would like a copy of the goblins' hiring policy. It may be only one sentence long, which would already put it ahead of several royal offices.

But no fast cut to an identity card. The fart spray remains unassigned. The camp figure is described, not reconciled. The goblins accept the pitch, and the fire is out. Waluigi advances the text only when those are the facts actually on the screen.

sections.heading: IX. A Dragon Arrives with an Appointment and Leaves with a Question
sections.body:
The trees shake, a dragon roars across the camp, lands, and asks, **‘WHERE IS ARCHIE? I WAS SUMMONED.’** Waluigi takes his hand off the popcorn. The dragon also says, **‘I BETRAYED THE BEANS FOR THE TOAD GOD.’** Two declarations, one landing, and no identified summoner. Waluigi will not cut from the word *summoned* to a picture of the ritual site and label it a direct connection. The earlier preparations and this arrival occur in one account; the mechanism between them is not shown.

The camp's Archie-like figure goes with the dragon. Training and an “Omega Fireball” are offered; the exchange says Archie had failed a Feyward mission. The figure starts to object that it uses water, then lets the objection go. Bones is invited too, says he has no quarrel, and declines. The dragon's parting line is **‘Green D to you,’** and it leaves with the passenger. Waluigi pauses the image on the departure, not the arrival. The departure is the thing the scene actually completes. ARRIVAL, YES. CAUSATION, NO. IDENTITY, STILL OPEN.

Who summoned the dragon? Is it the dragon Fawful claimed? Is the passenger the bot, or another figure called Archie? The event does not settle any of those questions. Waluigi can enjoy the contradiction between a water trick and an offered fireball without announcing that he has solved the character roster. A strange offer is not a forged identity document.

The dragon says it betrayed the Beans for the Toad God. That is what it says. Waluigi does not know whether this is a confession, a boast, a new allegiance, or a sentence intended to sound impressive beside a goblin fire. He watches Bones decline and the dragon leave. No ritual result appears in the final shot. No name tag turns toward the camera. WAH! Roll the reel to the last frame, but do not put a face on the unanswered question.

sections.heading: X. One Hour on the Map, and the Reel Stops
sections.body:
Bones declines the dragon's invitation, sleeps in the trees still wearing the borrowed disguise, and spends one hour measuring a map. Waluigi lays a blank sheet beside the projection and writes only the duration. One hour. No route, origin, region, scale, or destination has been transcribed. The map is not a treasure map just because Waluigi would enjoy having a big red X to circle. It is an object someone measured, and that is all the final card gives him.

The disguise is still on Bones at the end. The shorts are still behind. The map is with him, but its contents are not. Waluigi watches the frame hold on the trees and waits for the camera to tilt toward a direction. It does not. The session stops before a next destination appears, and Waluigi will not use the blank margin to draw one.

There are still people whose outcomes have not been shown: the helmet victim, the older woman, the fox-eared Toad. Fawful's ritual has not been completed on screen. The dragon has left, but the scene has not told us who summoned it or who the passenger is. Bones is outside the chase, not outside uncertainty. Waluigi is allowed to be relieved that he is alive in the last frame without pretending the story has become safe.

A measured map can be important. A one-hour measurement can be deliberate. Neither fact supplies a road. Waluigi closes the projector's shutter, keeps the empty sheet on the desk, and refuses to decorate it with arrows. That is where the reel stops: a man in borrowed clothes, trees overhead, one hour spent, and no destination on the page. ONE HOUR. NO ROUTE. NO X. NO ARROW. WAH! End card. No credits for the person who left the map blank; they did not give Waluigi a name either.

commentaries.title: The Intake Drone and the Unfinished Escape — Waluigi’s Cut
commentaries.subtitle: Waluigi’s Cut — one unanswered high five, a week-long power drain that meets a staff, and a wall that is not yet an exit.
commentaries.filed: 5 Aethel, 1040 BF — the screening desk, retrospective reading; exact hour unrecorded
commentaries.pullQuote: “If I can’t see them, I can’t see me.” Waluigi sees the wall. He is not calling it a door.
commentaries.standfirst: Waluigi reads the session transcript aloud at the screening desk, with the words projected one beat at a time. This is a reading of the record, not a claim that anyone filmed the ship. The high five, the intake drone, the questions about the missing Pond Patrol, the blackout, the barrel, the wounded Perot, and Remi at the wall all arrive in order. Waluigi has the pause key, a pencil, and no permission to write the ending before the transcript does.

sections.heading: HOLD THE SCREEN: THE HIGH FIVE THAT THE TRANSCRIPT WILL NOT CONFIRM
sections.body:
Waluigi has the transcript under the projector, the room is quiet, and the first voice says, “Okay… let’s see, where was I?” That is how this reading begins: not with a clean recap, not with the speaker knowing the previous sentence, but with somebody trying to find her place while Waluigi tries to find his pencil. Then she spots a porcupine Toad. “Hey, porcupine Toad. High five.” Waluigi lifts his own hand. FREEZE. The notes do not say whether their hands meet. His hand is left hovering in the air like a very athletic question mark. Nobody gets to write “successful high five” just because the setup is good.

The next words are “Bring out the stolen technology.” Waluigi circles *the* in that sentence. Which technology? Who stole it? Why is Remi being ordered to produce it? The transcript does not answer before an intake drone opens and Remi notices something shiny inside. “I wonder if there is a person in there.” Then the drone sucks her in and its bars close. Waluigi points to the screen: that is the whole transition from curiosity to confinement. No tidy explanation arrives to make the machine less of a cell.

A machine that opens and closes bars is already making a very strong case for what it does. Waluigi is not going to invent a scanning beam, a warning buzzer, or a helpful instruction manual. The transcript gives a shiny something, a question about a possible person, and Remi being taken inside. That is enough for one opening. The high five remains unconfirmed; the theft remains unexplained; the prisoner is now in the drone. NO CONTACT CONFIRMED. NO TECHNOLOGY NAMED. Waluigi lowers his hand. THE HIGHLIGHT OF THE SCENE MAY HAVE BEEN A HIGH FIVE, BUT THE ARCHIVE HAS NOT SEEN CONTACT. Keep the screen moving. WAH!

sections.heading: THE OUTTAKE DRONE: EAGER IS QUESTIONED AND RELEASED
sections.body:
The Toads drag Eager over to the intake drone and tell him to speak the truth. Their promise is that they will not let the machine become an “outtake drone.” Waluigi stops the projector. That is a threat delivered by a pun. It is not a clever name for an interview room; it is a threat delivered by a pun while the person being questioned is standing beside a machine that just swallowed Remi. Waluigi would like the room to notice how quickly the joke gets its own bars.

They ask about the Pond Patrol, which they say has been missing for three weeks. Eager says, “I was sent without a detachment.” The trip became a misadventure and took longer than expected. He believes Toad Lee and Rodger were sent over too, and he cannot say where either one is. Salam is here. Eager repeats that the other two look M.I.A. Waluigi writes those three letters on the margin of the projection, then underlines *look*. A person who says he cannot find someone is not a tracking spell, a recovery team, or a map with a blinking dot.

The interrogators accept the answer: “You are free to go. Welcome aboard.” Eager sighs. Waluigi smiles at the timing and then catches himself: being released aboard the same ship is not the same as being handed a route to the people who are missing. The Toads say their three-week estimate; Eager gives his limit; nobody gives us a destination. The scene has one answer and two absences. Waluigi wants a map; the transcript gives him a statement. Waluigi can make a joke about a welcome mat on an interrogation deck, but he cannot make Rodger and Toad Lee appear on the screen. The drone has not become an outtake drone. The question has not become a search result. MISSING IS NOT LOCATED. NEXT PAGE. WAH.

sections.heading: “ALPHA ZETA BETA”: A DESIGNATION IS NOT AN EXPLANATION
sections.body:
Now the Toads turn to Salam. The transcript gives the designation “Alpha Zeta Beta,” and Waluigi writes it across the screen in enormous letters. Not because he knows what it means. Because it is enormous lettering. The Toads say they heard Salam worked for the traitor Speaker L, who was cast away down to the “bowels of the earth.” Salam asks, “You did? What happened to him?” Waluigi leans toward the projector. Good question. The answer we receive is a threat about what will happen to Remi, not a verified account of Speaker L.

Salam says he failed the mission and became separated from Rodger and Toad Lee’s detachment. The transcript does not explain whether “Alpha Zeta Beta” is a rank, a nickname, a new office, or a sequence of letters somebody shouted while looking for a badge. Waluigi refuses to let the sound of a title do the work of an explanation. He is not a rank translator just because the letters are large. Salam says he was separated. He does not say where the pair went. The Toads offer an accusation about Speaker L; they do not offer the missing Toads’ location.

The intake drone starts moving toward the engine room. Waluigi draws a little arrow under the line, then writes **NOT AN EXIT** beside it. The cell is changing rooms, not opening. Remi’s destination is the next restraint, not freedom. The question about Speaker L hangs on the screen, unanswered by evidence; the threat about Remi lands in its place. Waluigi wants to ask the interrogators whether this is their entire procedure: announce a grand title, mention a person underground, then wheel the prisoner away before anybody can ask the next question. He will not add that as dialogue. He will simply point at the moving cell and say the room has changed, while the answer has not. A TITLE IS NOT AN ANSWER. WAH.

sections.heading: A WEEK TO DRAIN, ONE STAFF TO REMOVE, AND NO FLIGHT REPORT
sections.body:
The engine room. Remi is placed in a field associated with X.O.’s staff, and a Toad explains, “this will drain your power over time.” Perot is assigned to watch her; the explanation says the power will drain after a week. Waluigi gets out a calendar, counts to seven, and then the transcript keeps going before he can finish drawing the squares. A week-long drain is the plan. Perot is the watcher. The staff is there. Those are the shapes of the arrangement, and the screen has not said exactly how the field works.

Remi looks around and wonders, “Did we even take off yet?” Waluigi stops with the calendar in his hands. The transcript does not answer. There is no view out of a window, no voice from a pilot, no altitude marker. Remi reaches for X.O.’s staff and removes it. The power immediately goes out. Waluigi throws the calendar into the air—not at Perot, who is on the page, and not at the ship, which he cannot see. Waluigi puts it away; nobody has given him an altitude. The plan said a week; the blackout arrives now.

The transcript gives a sequence: the staff was in the field; Remi took it out; the power failed. It does not say the staff itself produced the field, or that the ship is falling, or that the engine room has become a crash scene. Waluigi is very tempted to add a cartoon airship with a dotted line plummeting toward the ground. He puts the crayon down. The words say “power,” not “impact.” They do not tell us whether the ship has taken off. The prison is now dark, and a dark ship is not automatically a crashed ship. Waluigi writes that sentence where the projector operator can see it. BLACKOUT, YES. CRASH, NOT SHOWN. He will not let a sound effect write the next line. WAH!

sections.heading: “YOU PRISONER”: THE MUSKET DOES NOT SETTLE THE SHIP QUESTION
sections.body:
Remi casts a light spell, and the Toads move through the dark. The Toad Rangers assemble and call for a search for an escaped prisoner. Waluigi points at the contradiction and keeps the projector moving: the prisoner is in the same room as the search party. Remi walks straight up to a Toad and presses her musket against his head. The Toad turns toward her. “You prisoner.” Waluigi opens his mouth, closes it, and looks at the audience. That is a very short diagnosis from a person who is presently looking down the barrel of a musket.

Remi fires. The bullet bounces off the Toad’s squishy body. He falls bleeding. “You shouldn’t have locked me up like that,” she says, followed by “This is our ship now.” Waluigi moves the frame back and forth between those three facts: the bullet bounced, the Toad is bleeding, and the ship is being claimed. None of them cancels the others. The transcript does not name the wounded Toad in this moment. Lulu Green identifies him as Perot later; Waluigi will not put that name on the screen before the text does.

The other Toads panic. They grab Archie’s barrel and run. Waluigi pinches the bridge of his nose. A barrel carrying a person is now in motion during an escape search on a powerless ship, and nobody says where the barrel is going. It is a terrible time to be a barrel, an uncertain time to be Archie, and a very loud time to be Remi. The musket does not settle who owns the TOADALNAEC. “This is our ship now” is Remi’s claim; the transcript has not concluded the argument. Her light makes the search visible, and the shot tells the searchers where she is. A WOUND IS NOT A DEATH SCENE. Waluigi circles **SEARCH CONTINUES** and resists the urge to draw a victory flag. WAH.

sections.heading: THE BARREL REACHES THE ELECTRIC PORT BEFORE THE STORY DOES
sections.body:
Remi disguises herself and walks with an escort. The transcript does not show what the disguise looks like or say which Toads think she belongs with them. Waluigi sketches a question mark where the costume would go. He refuses to award the disguise points when the costume is not visible. The group talks as they move. Remi asks who Speaker Rivers was; she is told he overthrew Speaker L, rules with his heart rather than his fist, and was the savior. Waluigi underlines *was told*. The screen has a claim about Rivers, not a signed biography.

Remi asks about the person in the barrel. The answer says he started fires, may have freed the Toads from tyranny, and betrayed them. Waluigi looks from that description to the barrel being carried through the ship. It is a striking way to transport a person whose history is the subject of a political argument. The barrel reaches an electrical port it was not meant to enter. Archie is shocked, stays quiet, and then crawls out through the bottom. Waluigi pauses on “not meant to enter.” THE PORT IS NOT A BARREL PARKING SPACE.

A Toad sees sparks and Remi with the staff: “Wait, that’s the staff. Remi, no, that’s the staff, don’t—” Someone grabs her head. She bonks him. Contact turns a Toad gold, and Remi says, “You forgot I am made of gold.” Archie tackles a Toad with a gun. Waluigi is trying to keep three things in separate boxes: the barrel’s route, the disguise’s unknown appearance, and the gold-touching contact. The transcript supplies the events; it does not supply the costume designer, the port’s manual, or a proper noun for the person being grabbed. He will not draw any of those. The barrel fails as a container, the escort is not a guarantee, and the arguments about Rivers and Speaker L keep traveling along with everyone else. Next card. WAH!

sections.heading: “WE WILL TALK LATER”: TWO PEOPLE, TWO DIFFERENT EXIT PLANS
sections.body:
Archie says he cannot see well in the dark. Remi tells him she is right above him; he chooses left instead. Waluigi puts a little arrow on the screen and watches it point in exactly the wrong direction. Remi says she was kidnapped and that the only way out was to cut power to the whole ship. Archie’s response is, “Wait, you what?” Waluigi understands the question. This is a large plan to discover after the lights go out.

Remi is dragged away again. The Toads sing, “We are the Toads who will kick your ass.” Waluigi holds up one finger: that is the line the transcript records. No chorus after it, no sheet music, no sudden five-part harmony. He is not going to write extra lyrics for people who are already holding a search. Archie bumps into a wall. Remi stabs his arm with her dagger; the transcript does not explain why or what the wound does. Waluigi turns the pencil over and leaves that question mark alone.

Archie hears Remi screaming, calls her name, and follows. He says Eager, Salam, and Remi will not like the consequences. The reply is that the only way out was to cut the power and that Remi’s friend will understand. Archie says, “We will talk later.” He wants an inn and a chance to get their bearings. Waluigi waits for the inn reservation; the transcript does not supply one. Then: “It pains me we have to leave our friends here,” and he coughs as he looks at the Toad. Waluigi points to the screen: one person wants to leave the immediate fight; the other has cut power to the whole vessel and is still inside it. They disagree, and the disagreement keeps moving.

Archie’s line is not a signed agreement with Remi’s decision. “We will talk later” is a delay, not a reconciliation. Waluigi knows this because the words are right there, large and readable, while the room is still dark. He gives the Toad chant exactly one line and the dagger exactly one unanswered question. The route to the inn is what Archie wants, not proof they reach one. THE CHANT HAS ONE LINE. Nobody gets to fast-forward past the people still on the ship. WAH.

sections.heading: VINES, A DUEL, AND ARCHIE CHOOSING TO HELP PEROT
sections.body:
Lulu Green stops Archie and Remi with vines. Archie asks to get off the ship and find their bearings. Remi calls Lulu “just plants” and says plants are flammable. Waluigi looks at the screen, then at the phrase “just plants,” and gives the audience one small nod: it is an argument based on a material property while the material property is currently holding the route closed. Archie calls the encounter a huge misunderstanding. Lulu points to Perot and asks whether he wanted trouble. Remi shot him. The transcript has reached the name Perot; Waluigi can now put it under the earlier scene, but not under a final outcome.

Remi says the Toads wanted trouble when they took the ship. “You Toads are all the same,” she says. Lulu asks for a duel. Remi fires her crossbow. Archie tells her not to kill anyone while she is fighting blind. Remi asks, “If they’re liberated, why are they evil?” Archie says they have trust issues. He lights his staff, and for a moment he can see Remi and the person with the arrow. Waluigi finds the pause button. A ship ownership argument, a generalization about Toads, vines, a duel, and a temporary light source have all entered the same room.

Archie sees Perot about to die and stops trying to leave. He tries to stabilize him. “I did the best I could,” Archie says, trusting that Perot has a faction to look after him. Then Archie leaves. Waluigi lowers his voice for a moment. Archie really does turn back and try to help. He does not know whether it worked. That effort matters; it does not tell us Perot’s outcome.

Lulu pardons Archie for what she calls small crimes, though she will speak to the higher-ups. Remi, she says, is now target number one: “This isn’t just for me anymore. It’s for the Toads.” Waluigi raises the volume again. A pardon for Archie is not a pardon for Remi, and a target declaration is not the end of the fight. Waluigi will not turn either sentence into a neat courtroom ending. The doorway is open for Archie; Remi remains. KINDNESS, NOT A MEDICAL REPORT. WAH.

sections.heading: “NOW WE’RE EVEN”: LIGHTNING, A CROSS, AND A DISPUTE THAT KEEPS TALKING
sections.body:
Archie watches from the doorway. Lulu’s skin hardens into stone. “Now we’re even,” she says with a smile. Remi rushes her and casts lightning. It passes through Lulu’s stone skin. Lulu is shocked and calls herself “crispy.” Waluigi makes a note in the margin: the stone transformation did not stop this lightning. He does not add a weakness chart or a scientific explanation, because the transcript gives an effect, not a lecture from the engine room. The fight continues.

Zesty Black appears. A giant cross appears over Remi’s head, and he says he has found a new target. Vines prod her; the plants open a pit in the floor, and she dodges it. Black fires two bullets; she dodges those too. Remi takes Rhelmon’s Anchor and hits Lulu over the head. Lulu becomes dizzy. Waluigi puts four action cards in a row and asks the projectionist not to shuffle them. There is a mark, a pit, two shots, and an object used as a striking tool. The notes do not describe the Anchor or say who owns it. Waluigi can laugh at the speed of the sequence without making up an inventory list.

Under the attacks, Archie asks Remi not to be racist. He says the Toads are scared, as she is now. Remi says, “They took our ship.” Archie replies that it is technically their ship and that he is trying to respect their way of life. Remi says, “Their way of life is wrong.” Waluigi stops the tape on the word *technically*. A duel can be happening while the ship’s ownership remains contested; the combat does not resolve the argument.

Yellow dodges the next thunderbolt. Pink blasts color into Remi’s eyes. A thunderclap follows, and Remi says she cannot see and needs to unblind herself. Waluigi is now tracking stone, lightning, a cross, vines, a pit, bullets, an Anchor, an ownership dispute, and a blinding attack. THIS IS A LOT OF SCENE FOR ONE SCREEN. He advances the transcript only when it advances. The fight has not concluded. The ship has not been awarded by a lightning bolt. STONE IS NOT A DEED. WAH!

sections.heading: INVISIBLE IS NOT THE SAME AS OUT: AROUND THE WALL
sections.body:
The Toads surround Remi. Their masks let them see in the dark; they smile and celebrate. Waluigi holds the projector steady while the room tries to make this sound like a victory lap. Remi thinks for a while. “It’s not over yet,” she decides. Waluigi nods. It is not over on the page. Remi turns invisible and reasons, “If I can’t see them, I can’t see me.” Waluigi almost applauds the symmetry and then remembers there is still a ring of people who can see in the dark. Invisible is a change in what the other side sees, not a magic map showing the exit.

Remi moves by touch. Her hand finds a solid wall. She can climb it or go around it. She chooses to go around. The transcript ends there. Waluigi taps the screen once, gently, as if the next line might come from being polite. Waluigi waits. No line comes. The wall has not become a door; Remi has not been shown clearing it. The Toads have not been shown catching her. Perot’s condition has not been reported after Archie’s attempt. The ship’s power state has not been updated. Rodger and Toad Lee have not appeared. The screen gives us the choice, not the result.

Waluigi does have one concession for the room: the power went out, the masks let the Toads see in the dark, and Remi is invisible. Those are inconvenient physical facts, and all three can be true at once. He is not going to pretend that invisibility automatically makes her safe, or that a wall she has not passed is a completed escape.

So Waluigi keeps the last frame on Remi’s hand at the wall. She is still moving. The choice is still ahead of its outcome. The ship is still the setting; the search has not ended. Nobody gets a cheerful end card announcing a getaway the transcript does not show. Waluigi closes the projector shutter before his imagination can draw a door into the stone. Around is a direction. Invisible is a condition. Free is not yet on the screen. INVISIBLE. NOT FREE. WAH!
